sentence: Direban ya tsai da motar a gaban asibiti domin mace mai ciki ta sauka.
translation: The driver brought the car to a stop in front of the hospital so a pregnant woman could get out.

sentence: Jami'in tsaro ya tsai da mu a shingen bincike har muka nuna takardunmu.
translation: The security officer held us at the checkpoint until we produced our papers.

sentence: Ruwan sama ya tsai da wasan, sai muka zauna cikin ɓacin rai muna jira.
translation: The rain brought the match to a standstill, and we sat there waiting, thoroughly fed up.

sentence: A gidan namun daji na Kano, giwa ta miƙa hancinta ta karɓi ayaba.
translation: At the Kano zoo the elephant stretched out its trunk and took the banana.

sentence: Manoma sun kwana suna tsaro, don giwa takan lalata gonakinsu da dare.
translation: The farmers stayed up all night on guard, because elephants wreck their fields after dark.

sentence: Zuciyata takan yi ciwo idan na ji labarin yadda mafarauta ke kashe giwa.
translation: It hurts me every time I hear how poachers are killing elephants.

sentence: Limamin masallaci ya yi wa'azi a kan illar zina ga rayuwar iyali.
translation: The imam preached about the damage adultery does to family life.

sentence: Kotun shari'a ta saki mutumin bayan shaidun ba su tabbatar da zargin zina ba.
translation: The sharia court released the man after the witnesses failed to prove the charge of zina.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan gargaɗe mu da cewa zina tana ɓata mutuncin gida gaba ɗaya.
translation: My mother keeps warning us that zina destroys a household's good name completely.

sentence: Wandona ya yage a gwiwa, sai na kai shi wurin maɗinki kusa da gida.
translation: My trousers tore at the knee, so I took them to the tailor near the house.

sentence: Mahaifina ya sayo mini sabon wando da riga kafin bikin Sallah.
translation: My father bought me new trousers and a shirt before the Sallah celebration.

sentence: Wandon da na saya a kasuwa ya yi mini ƙanƙanta, na ji haushi ƙwarai.
translation: The trousers I bought at the market turned out too small for me, and I was really annoyed.

sentence: Da aka ga watan Shawwal, mahaifiyata ta fara dafa abincin Sallah.
translation: The moment the Shawwal moon was sighted, my mother started cooking the Sallah food.

sentence: A ranar farko ta Shawwal, mun taru a filin Idi don sallah.
translation: On the first day of Shawwal we gathered at the Eid ground for the prayer.

sentence: Ina son azumi shida na Shawwal, amma kullum sai na kasa cika su.
translation: I love the six fasts of Shawwal, but every year I end up failing to complete them.

sentence: Kowace maraice mahaifiyata takan tuƙa tuwon masara mu ci da miyar kuka.
translation: Every evening my mother makes maize tuwo for us to eat with baobab-leaf soup.

sentence: A wurin biki mun ci tuwon shinkafa da miyar taushe har muka ƙoshi.
translation: At the wedding we ate rice tuwo with pumpkin stew until we were completely full.

sentence: Tuwon da aka kawo mini a gidan abinci ya yi sanyi, ban ci ba.
translation: The tuwo they brought me at the restaurant had gone cold, so I didn't eat it.

sentence: Kakata takan gaya mana cewa ladabi ya fi arziki muhimmanci a rayuwa.
translation: My grandmother always tells us that good manners matter more in life than wealth.

sentence: Da baƙi suka shigo, yaron ya miƙe tsaye ya gaishe da su cikin ladabi.
translation: When the guests came in, the boy stood up and greeted them politely.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin ɗalibi mai ladabi kamar shi ba a wannan makarantar.
translation: I have never seen a student as well-mannered as him in this school.

sentence: Mun tona rogo a gonar kakana, muka gasa shi da gishiri.
translation: We dug up cassava on my grandfather's farm and roasted it with salt.

sentence: Matan kauyen suna niƙa rogo su yi gari, su kai shi kasuwa.
translation: The village women grind cassava into garri and take it to the market.

sentence: Farashin rogo ya yi tashin gwauron zabi, talakawa sun daina saya.
translation: The price of cassava has shot right up, and poor people have stopped buying it.

sentence: Ɗan'uwana ya tafi Amirka domin karatu, tun daga lokacin bai dawo ba.
translation: My brother went to America to study, and he hasn't come back since.

sentence: Jakadan Amirka ya ziyarci Kano don tattaunawa kan harkokin kasuwanci.
translation: The American ambassador visited Kano for talks on trade matters.

sentence: Na daɗe ina zaton rayuwa a Amirka mai sauƙi ce, amma na yi kuskure.
translation: For a long time I assumed life in America was easy, but I was wrong.

sentence: Ba zan iya zuwa kotu ba, sai na naɗa wakili ya tsaya mini.
translation: I can't go to the court myself, so I appointed a representative to stand in for me.

sentence: Wakilin kamfanin ya zo kauyenmu don ya sayi auduga daga manoma.
translation: The company's agent came to our village to buy cotton from the farmers.

sentence: Mun zaɓe shi wakili, amma bai taɓa kawo mana ruwan sha ba.
translation: We elected him as our representative, but he has never once brought us drinking water.

sentence: Malamin makarantar allo ya ce mana ƙarya zunubi ne mai girma.
translation: The Quranic school teacher told us that lying is a serious sin.

sentence: Ya bar aikin banki don yana ganin cin riba babban zunubi ne.
translation: He left his job at the bank because he considers taking interest a grave sin.

sentence: Bayan ya cutar da marayu, zunubinsa yana damunsa har ya kasa barci.
translation: After he wronged the orphans, his sin troubled him so much that he couldn't sleep.

sentence: Kowace safiya muna shan alkama da madara kafin mu tafi makaranta.
translation: Every morning we have wheat porridge with milk before we set off for school.

sentence: Manoman Kano sun fara noman alkama a lokacin rani da ban ruwa.
translation: Farmers in Kano have started growing wheat in the dry season using irrigation.

sentence: Na damu da yadda farashin alkama ya tashi, yanzu ba ma iya sayen gurasa.
translation: It worries me how the price of wheat has risen; now we can't even afford bread.

sentence: Kullum kakana yana koka da ciwon gwiwa duk lokacin da damina ta zo.
translation: My grandfather complains about his knee pain every time the rainy season arrives.

sentence: Ma'aikatan asibiti sun koka kan jinkirin albashi a taron da suka yi jiya.
translation: The hospital staff complained about the delayed salaries at the meeting they held yesterday.

sentence: Maimakon ka zauna kana koka, sai ka tashi ka nemi wata hanya.
translation: Instead of sitting there complaining, get up and look for another way.

sentence: Yarima ya sauka daga doki, ya shiga fadar mahaifinsa sarki cikin gaggawa.
translation: The prince got down from his horse and hurried into his father the emir's palace.

sentence: A ranar Sallah yarima yakan jagoranci hawan dawakai zuwa filin Idi.
translation: On Sallah day the prince leads the horsemen's procession to the Eid ground.

sentence: Mutanen gari sun fi son yarima a kan ɗan'uwansa mai girman kai.
translation: The townspeople prefer the prince to his arrogant brother.

sentence: Yawanci mahaifiyata takan dafa abinci da wuri kafin yara su dawo daga makaranta.
translation: My mother usually cooks early, before the children get back from school.

sentence: Yawanci motocin haya sukan bar tasha kafin ƙarfe shida na safe.
translation: The passenger taxis mostly pull out of the motor park before six in the morning.

sentence: Yawanci ba na yarda da jita-jitar da ake yaɗawa a kasuwa.
translation: For the most part I don't believe the rumours people spread around the market.

sentence: A watan Nuwamba mukan fito da bargo domin sanyin safiya ya fara tsananta.
translation: In November we bring the blankets out, because the morning cold starts to bite.

sentence: Jarrabawar ƙarshen shekara za ta fara ranar goma ga watan Nuwamba.
translation: The end-of-year examinations will begin on the tenth of November.

sentence: Ban taɓa mantawa da ranar bikin aurenmu a watan Nuwamba ba.
translation: I have never forgotten the day of our wedding, back in November.

sentence: Maigini ya shata iyakar ɗakin a ƙasa kafin a fara tono harsashi.
translation: The builder marked out the outline of the room on the ground before they started digging the foundation.

sentence: Malamin ya shata taswirar Najeriya a kan allo don ɗalibai su gane iyakoki.
translation: The teacher drew the outline of Nigeria on the board so the pupils could make out the borders.

sentence: Mahaifina ya shata mini hanyar rayuwa tun ina ƙarami, ban taɓa ɓacewa ba.
translation: My father mapped out the path of life for me when I was small, and I have never gone astray.

sentence: Ruwan sama na watan Agusta ya cika rijiyarmu, sai muka daina zuwa rafi.
translation: The August rains filled our well, so we stopped trekking down to the stream.

sentence: Makarantu sukan rufe a watan Agusta, sai yara su koma gonar iyayensu.
translation: Schools usually close in August, and the children go back to their parents' farms.

sentence: Ina son watan Agusta domin duk gonakinmu sukan yi kore da kyau.
translation: I love the month of August, because all our farms turn a beautiful green.

sentence: Naman sa ya yi tsada a kasuwa, sai muka sayi kifi maimakon haka.
translation: Beef had got expensive at the market, so we bought fish instead.

sentence: Kuɗin haya ya yi tsada sosai, shi ya sa na koma bayan gari.
translation: Rent became so expensive that I moved out to the edge of town.

sentence: Komai ya yi tsada a wannan shekara, har albashina bai isa komai ba.
translation: Everything has become expensive this year, to the point where my salary no longer stretches to anything.

sentence: Kowace safiya yaron makiyayi yakan kai doki rafi domin ya sha ruwa.
translation: Every morning the herdsman's boy takes the horse down to the stream for a drink.

sentence: A ranar hawan Sallah, sarki ya hau doki mai fararen ƙafafu.
translation: On the day of the Sallah procession, the emir rode a horse with white legs.

sentence: Ina son doki fiye da mota, domin yana sanin hanyar gida da kansa.
translation: I prefer a horse to a car, because it knows the way home by itself.

sentence: Yaron ya sa babbar riga a jika, ya fita zuwa masallaci da sauri.
translation: The boy threw a big gown on and hurried out to the mosque.

sentence: Kafin su shiga wurin aiki, ma'aikata sukan sa kaya masu kauri a jika.
translation: Before they go onto the site, the workers put thick clothing on their bodies.

sentence: Da muka fito daga rafi, sai sanyi ya kama mu a jika.
translation: When we came up out of the stream, the cold gripped us all over.

sentence: Galibi ana kashe wutar lantarki da dare, sai mu kunna fitilar kananzir.
translation: The electricity is usually cut at night, so we light the kerosene lamp.

sentence: Galibi manoman wannan ƙauye suna noman gero, domin ruwan bai isa shinkafa ba.
translation: Most of the farmers in this village grow millet, because there isn't enough rain for rice.

sentence: Galibi ina jin kunya idan aka yabe ni a gaban jama'a.
translation: I mostly feel embarrassed when I'm praised in front of a crowd.

sentence: Kowace safiya kakata takan tafasa ti da citta kafin kowa ya tashi.
translation: Every morning my grandmother boils tea with ginger before anyone else is up.

sentence: Bayan taro, mun zauna a bakin titi muna shan ti da gurasa.
translation: After the meeting we sat at the roadside drinking tea with bread.

sentence: Ba na iya yin aiki da safe sai na sha ti mai zaki.
translation: I can't get any work done in the morning until I've had a sweet tea.

sentence: Bayan kwana bakwai, sai cibiya ta faɗi daga jikin jaririn.
translation: Seven days later the umbilical cord dropped off the baby.

sentence: Ungozoma ta yanke cibiya da almakashi mai tsabta, sannan ta ɗaure ta.
translation: The midwife cut the cord with clean scissors and then tied it off.

sentence: A garinmu, ana binne cibiya a bayan gida domin yaro ya so gida.
translation: In our town the cord is buried behind the house so that the child will love home.

sentence: Kakata takan ci tuwo da hannu, ba ta son cokali ko kaɗan.
translation: My grandmother eats her tuwo with her hand; she has no use for a spoon at all.

sentence: Mai shayi ya ba ni cokali mai datti, sai na wanke shi.
translation: The tea seller handed me a dirty spoon, so I washed it myself.

sentence: Raina ya ɓaci domin cokalin azurfa da mahaifiyata ta bar mini ya ɓace.
translation: I was upset because the silver spoon my mother left me has gone missing.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya bayyana mana yadda jihadin Shehu Usman ya sauya arewacin Najeriya.
translation: The history teacher explained to us how Usman dan Fodio's jihad transformed northern Nigeria.

sentence: A makarantar allo mun karanta littattafan da suka bayyana dalilan jihadin Sakkwato.
translation: At the Qur'anic school we read the books that set out the causes of the Sokoto jihad.

sentence: Limamin ya ce jihadin da ya fi wahala shi ne yaƙi da son rai.
translation: The imam said the hardest jihad of all is the struggle against one's own desires.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifiyata takan ɗebo ruwa daga rijiyar da ke bayan gida.
translation: Every morning my mother draws water from the well behind the house.

sentence: Matasan ƙauyen sun haƙa sabuwar rijiya bayan tsohuwar ta bushe a bazara.
translation: The young men of the village dug a new well after the old one dried up in the hot season.

sentence: Ina tsoron rijiyar nan domin bakinta a buɗe yake, kuma yara suna wasa kusa.
translation: That well frightens me, because its mouth is left open and children play right beside it.

sentence: Muna gasa masara a kan garwashi duk lokacin da damina ta fara.
translation: We roast maize over the coals whenever the rainy season begins.

sentence: Farashin masara ya tashi a kasuwar Dawanau, don haka mun sayi ɗan kaɗan.
translation: The price of maize has gone up at Dawanau market, so we only bought a little.

sentence: Manomin ya yi baƙin ciki saboda fari ya lalata masarar da ya shuka.
translation: The farmer was heartbroken because the drought destroyed the maize he had planted.

sentence: Da safe mukan sha fura da nono kafin mu tafi gona.
translation: In the mornings we drink fura with milk before we set off for the farm.

sentence: Matar Fulani tana sayar da nono a ƙarƙashin bishiyar kuka kowace Lahadi.
translation: The Fulani woman sells fresh milk under the baobab tree every Sunday.

sentence: Ban so nonon da aka sayar mini ba, domin ya yi tsami sosai.
translation: I didn't like the milk they sold me, because it had turned far too sour.

sentence: Kafin ta fita kasuwa, 'yar uwata takan sa hijabi mai launin shuɗi.
translation: Before she goes out to the market, my sister always puts on a blue hijab.

sentence: Jami'ar ta ba wa ɗalibai damar sanya hijabi a lokacin jarrabawa.
translation: The university allowed the students to wear the hijab during the examinations.

sentence: Ta ce hijabi yana ba ta kwanciyar hankali, ba wai tilastawa ba ne.
translation: She said the hijab gives her peace of mind; it is not something forced on her.

sentence: Yaran ƙauye sun taru a inuwar rimi don gujewa zafin rana.
translation: The village children gathered in the shade of the silk-cotton tree to escape the midday heat.

sentence: Mahaifina ya sassaƙa ƙwarya daga itacen rimi da ya sare bara.
translation: My father carved a bowl out of the kapok wood he felled last year.

sentence: Na yi kewar babban rimin da ya taɓa tsayawa gaban masallacin unguwarmu.
translation: I miss the great silk-cotton tree that once stood in front of our neighbourhood mosque.

sentence: Yaron ya ɓoye tsabar kuɗi a hannunsa yana cewa dabo ne.
translation: The boy hid the coin in his palm and told us it was magic.

sentence: A wajen bikin, wani mai dabo ya fitar da tsuntsu daga hular ango.
translation: At the wedding, a conjurer pulled a bird out of the groom's cap.

sentence: Ban yarda da dabon nan ba, tabbas ya ɓoye zaren a hannun rigarsa.
translation: I don't believe that trick for a moment; he must have hidden the thread in his sleeve.

sentence: Kawuna ya yi shekara uku yana aiki a Bagadaza kafin ya dawo Kano.
translation: My uncle spent three years working in Baghdad before he came back to Kano.

sentence: Malam ya gaya mana cewa Bagadaza ta kasance cibiyar ilimi a dā.
translation: The teacher told us that Baghdad was once a great centre of learning.

sentence: Ina fatan wata rana in ziyarci Bagadaza in ga kogin Dijla da kaina.
translation: I hope that one day I will visit Baghdad and see the Tigris with my own eyes.

sentence: Gonar kakanmu ta kasu kashi huɗu tsakanin 'ya'yansa bayan rasuwarsa.
translation: Our grandfather's farmland was divided into four portions among his children after he died.

sentence: Ɗaliban aji sun kasu gida biyu don su yi muhawara game da noma.
translation: The pupils in the class split into two groups in order to debate about farming.

sentence: Ban ji daɗin yadda unguwarmu ta kasu bisa siyasa a bana ba.
translation: I don't like the way our neighbourhood has split along political lines this year.

sentence: Idan ruwan sama ya fara, dau tufafin da ke kan igiya da sauri.
translation: If the rain starts, get the clothes off the line quickly.

sentence: Direban ya ce mu dau kayanmu kafin motar ta tashi da ƙarfe biyar.
translation: The driver told us to take our luggage before the bus left at five.

sentence: Kada ka dau abin da ba naka ba, ko da babu wanda ke gani.
translation: Don't take what isn't yours, even when nobody is watching.

sentence: Kakata ta bayyana min cewa muna da nasaba da iyalan sarkin garin.
translation: My grandmother explained to me that we are related to the town chief's family.

sentence: A wurin bikin, sai ya tambaye ni ko akwai nasaba tsakanina da amaryar.
translation: At the wedding he asked me whether I was any relation of the bride.

sentence: Ba na son a taimake ni saboda nasaba, ina son a duba ƙwarewata.
translation: I don't want to be helped because of family ties; I want my skill looked at.

sentence: Fitina ta ɓarke a gidan bayan an raba gadon mahaifinsu ba daidai ba.
translation: Trouble broke out in the household after their father's inheritance was shared out unfairly.

sentence: Wannan ɗan jarida yana kawo fitina tsakanin manoma da makiyaya a yankin.
translation: That journalist keeps stirring up trouble between the farmers and the herders in the area.

sentence: Na fi son yin shiru a taro, domin ƙaramar magana takan janyo babbar fitina.
translation: I would rather stay quiet in a meeting, because one small remark can drag in real trouble.

sentence: Bayan shekara biyu na husuma, ni da ƙanena mun yi sulhu a gaban kakanmu.
translation: After two years of bad blood, my younger brother and I made peace in front of our grandfather.

sentence: Dattawan unguwa sun yi sulhu tsakanin maƙwabta biyu kafin lamarin ya kai kotu.
translation: The neighbourhood elders settled the matter between two neighbours before it reached court.

sentence: Ina ganin sulhu ya fi shariʼa amfani, saboda yana barin zumunci a raye.
translation: I think reconciliation is worth more than a court case, because it leaves the kinship alive.

sentence: Waziri ya isa fadar sarki da safe don gabatar da koke-koken talakawa.
translation: The vizier reached the emir's palace in the morning to lay out the commoners' complaints.

sentence: A ranar Sallah, waziri yakan bi sarki a kan doki cikin taron jamaʼa.
translation: On Sallah day the vizier rides on horseback behind the emir through the crowd.

sentence: Kakana ya ce tsohon waziri ya fi wannan sauƙin kai da haƙuri.
translation: My grandfather says the old vizier was far more approachable and patient than this one.

sentence: Malam ya shiga tsakani lokacin da ɗalibai biyu suka fara faɗa a filin wasa.
translation: The teacher stepped in when two pupils started fighting on the playing field.

sentence: Bayan tsakani na wata biyu, ya sake bayyana a gidanmu ba zato ba tsammani.
translation: After a gap of two months he turned up at our house completely out of the blue.

sentence: A ganina, shiga tsakani ba tare da an neme ka ba yakan ƙara fitina.
translation: In my view, stepping into a quarrel uninvited usually makes the trouble worse.

sentence: Ka rubuta min lamba a takarda, domin wayata ta mutu tun jiya.
translation: Write the number down for me on paper, because my phone has been dead since yesterday.

sentence: Ɗan kasuwa ya nuna mini lamba a kan buhun shinkafa don tabbatar da inganci.
translation: The trader showed me the trademark on the rice sack to prove the quality.

sentence: Ina jin haushin asibitin nan, domin sai ka jira lamba kafin a duba ka.
translation: That hospital irritates me: you have to wait for your number before anyone examines you.

sentence: Jamʼiyyar adawa ta samu rinjaye a zaɓen ƙananan hukumomi na bara.
translation: The opposition party won a majority in last year's local government elections.

sentence: Ƙungiyarmu ta yi rinjaye a wasan ƙarshe duk da ƙarancin ʼyan wasa.
translation: Our team came out on top in the final despite being short of players.

sentence: Kwaɗayi ya yi rinjaye a zuciyarsa har ya sayar da gonar mahaifinsa.
translation: Greed got the upper hand in his heart until he sold his father's farm.

sentence: Manomi ya kori shanun da suka shiga gonarsa da tsakar dare.
translation: The farmer drove out the cattle that had got into his field in the middle of the night.

sentence: An kori maʼaikata biyu bayan an gano sun sace kayan kamfanin.
translation: Two workers were dismissed after it came out that they had stolen company property.

sentence: Na yi baƙin ciki da suka kori mai gadi ba gaira ba dalili.
translation: It upset me that they sacked the watchman for no reason whatsoever.

sentence: Kakata takan yi adduʼa kowace safiya domin Allah ya kiyaye mu daga sharri.
translation: My grandmother prays every morning that God will keep us safe from evil.

sentence: Maƙwabcinmu yana yaɗa sharri tsakanin mata, har suka daina zuwa wurin juna.
translation: Our neighbour spreads malice among the women, until they stopped visiting one another.

sentence: Malam ya ce duk wanda ya shuka sharri, ba zai girbi alheri ba.
translation: The teacher said that whoever sows wickedness will never harvest good.

sentence: Kowace safiya kakata takan tafasa ganye don ta yi shayin gargajiya.
translation: Every morning my grandmother boils leaves to make her traditional tea.

sentence: A kasuwar Kurmi, mata suna sayar da ganye tun kafin gari ya waye.
translation: At Kurmi market the women are selling greens before daybreak.

sentence: Ban ji daɗi ba don ganyen bishiyar mangwaro ya bushe gaba ɗaya.
translation: I felt awful because the leaves of the mango tree had dried up completely.

sentence: Cif Bello da kansa ya buɗe sabuwar makaranta ranar Litinin.
translation: Chief Bello opened the new school in person on Monday.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan gaishe da Cif Ojo duk lokacin da ya isa Legas.
translation: My father pays his respects to Chief Ojo whenever he gets to Lagos.

sentence: Ina girmama cif ɗinmu domin bai taɓa nuna son kai ba.
translation: I respect our chief because he has never once put himself first.

sentence: Yara sun ga hawainiya tana rarrafe a jikin bangon gidan kakarsu.
translation: The children saw a chameleon creeping along the wall of their grandmother's house.

sentence: Malamin kimiyya ya nuna mana yadda hawainiya ke sauya launi don ɓoyewa.
translation: The science teacher showed us how a chameleon changes colour in order to hide.

sentence: Kada ka amince da shi, don mutumin nan hawainiya ce a siyasa.
translation: Don't trust him — in politics that man is a chameleon.

sentence: Wani dattijo ya tsaya ya taimaka mana lokacin da motarmu ta lalace.
translation: An elderly gentleman stopped and helped us when our car broke down.

sentence: Dattijon unguwarmu yakan sasanta rigimar iyalai kafin ta kai kotu.
translation: The elder of our neighbourhood settles family quarrels before they ever reach court.

sentence: Mutuncinsa ya nuna cewa shi dattijo ne, ba ɗan ɓarna ba.
translation: His dignity showed that he was a gentleman, not a troublemaker.

sentence: Ambaliyar ruwa ta jefa manoman ƙauyenmu cikin hasara mai yawa bana.
translation: The flood threw the farmers of our village into heavy losses this year.

sentence: Ɗan kasuwa ya sha hasara sosai lokacin da farashin gyaɗa ya faɗi.
translation: The trader suffered a serious loss when the price of groundnuts collapsed.

sentence: Mutuwar malamin nan babbar hasara ce ga dukan mabiyansa.
translation: That teacher's death is a great loss to every one of his followers.

sentence: Hassadar maƙwabta ta sa mahaifiyata ta ɓoye labarin sabon aikina.
translation: The neighbours' envy made my mother keep quiet about my new job.

sentence: Tun da aka ɗaga shi, abokan aikinsa suna yi masa hassada a asirce.
translation: Ever since he was promoted, his colleagues have quietly envied him.

sentence: Kada ka bar hassada ta ci zuciyarka, domin kowa da rabonsa.
translation: Don't let envy eat away at your heart; everyone has his own portion.

sentence: Mun tashi da sassafe daga Kano, muka isa Rano kafin ƙarfe takwas.
translation: We set out from Kano at first light and reached Rano before eight.

sentence: Kakana ya yi shekaru talatin yana koyar da yara a makarantar Rano.
translation: My grandfather spent thirty years teaching children at the school in Rano.

sentence: Ina son kwanciyar hankalin Rano fiye da hayaniyar birnin Kano.
translation: I prefer the quiet of Rano to the racket of Kano city.

sentence: Kafin ya kwanta barci, kakana yakan yi salati sau ɗari.
translation: Before he lies down to sleep, my grandfather recites the blessing a hundred times.

sentence: Bayan sallar magariba, mutanen unguwar sukan taru su yi salati tare.
translation: After the sunset prayer the people of the quarter gather to recite the blessing together.

sentence: Duk lokacin da zuciyata ta damu, ina yin salati har in sami nutsuwa.
translation: Whenever my heart is troubled I recite the blessing until I find calm.

sentence: Kowace shekara mahaifina yakan fitar da zakkar hatsin da muka girbe.
translation: Every year my father pays out the zakat on the grain we harvested.

sentence: A masallacinmu, malamin ya koya mana yadda ake ƙidaya zakka kowace shekara.
translation: At our mosque the teacher taught us how zakat is calculated each year.

sentence: Ban gamsu ba domin sun raba zakka ga masu hannu da shuni.
translation: I wasn't satisfied, because they shared the zakat out among the well-off.

sentence: Ba ni da wata masaniya a kan inda suka kai kayan.
translation: I have no knowledge at all of where they took the goods.

sentence: Masaniyar da take da ita kan magungunan gargajiya ta ceci yaran ƙauyen.
translation: Her knowledge of traditional medicine saved the children of the village.

sentence: Na yi mamakin masaniyar tsohon nan a kan tarihin sarakunan Kano.
translation: I was astonished at that old man's knowledge of the history of Kano's emirs.

sentence: Yaron ya karya kwanon uwarsa, sai ya nemi gafara da hawaye.
translation: The boy broke his mother's bowl, then begged her forgiveness in tears.

sentence: Kafin watan azumi ya kama, maƙwabta sukan nemi gafara a wurin juna.
translation: Before the fasting month starts, neighbours in our quarter go and ask one another's pardon.

sentence: Ban yarda in yi masa gafara ba, sai da ya nuna nadama sosai.
translation: I refused to forgive him until he had shown real remorse.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta soya anta da albasa har gidan ya cika da ƙamshi.
translation: My mother fried liver with onions until the whole house smelled of it.

sentence: Za mu tsaya wurin suya mu sayi anta da tsire bayan aiki.
translation: We'll stop at the suya stand after work and buy liver and skewers.

sentence: Ba na son anta, amma kakata takan tilasta mini in ci ta.
translation: I don't like liver, but my grandmother always makes me eat it.

sentence: Yayata za ta tafi Madina makon gobe, muna tara mata kuɗin hanya.
translation: My older sister leaves for Medina next week, and we are pooling her travel money.

sentence: Malamin unguwarmu ya yi karatun addini a Madina kafin ya dawo Kano.
translation: The teacher in our quarter studied religion in Medina before coming back to Kano.

sentence: Ina fatan Allah Ya ba ni ikon ziyartar Madina kafin in tsufa.
translation: I hope God gives me the means to visit Medina before I grow old.

sentence: Kakana yakan ajiye mashi a bayan ƙofa don tsoron ɓarayi.
translation: My grandfather keeps a spear behind the door for fear of thieves.

sentence: Mahayan dawakai sun ɗaga mashi sama yayin bikin hawan sallah.
translation: The horsemen raised their spears aloft during the Sallah durbar.

sentence: Mafarauci ya riƙe mashi da hannaye biyu lokacin da ya ji rurin zaki.
translation: The hunter gripped his spear with both hands when he heard the lion roar.

sentence: Kafin baƙi su iso, mahaifiyata ta share falo ta shirya shi tsaf.
translation: Before the guests arrived, my mother swept the parlour and set it in perfect order.

sentence: Direba yakan wanke motar tsaf kowace safiya kafin ya ɗauki maigidansa.
translation: The driver washes the car spotless every morning before picking up his employer.

sentence: Na ajiye kuɗi a aljihu, amma washegari na tarar sun ƙare tsaf.
translation: I left money in my pocket, but the next day I found it completely gone.

sentence: Mahaifiyata tana dafa miya da yawa domin baƙi za su zo yau.
translation: My mother is cooking a big pot of stew because guests are coming today.

sentence: Matar maƙwabcinmu takan sayar da miya a kasuwa kowace Alhamis.
translation: Our neighbour's wife sells stew at the market every Thursday.

sentence: Miya ta yi daɗi ƙwarai har na sake ɗiban tuwo sau biyu.
translation: The stew was so good that I went back for tuwo twice more.

sentence: Da safiyar idi, yara sun sa sabbin kaya suna zagaya gidajen maƙwabta.
translation: On the morning of the holiday the children put on new clothes and went round the neighbours' houses.

sentence: Kafin idi, kasuwar Kano takan cika da mutanen da suke sayen kaya.
translation: Before the holiday, the Kano market fills up with people buying clothes.

sentence: Bana idi ba shi da daɗi, tun da kakata ta rasu a bara.
translation: The holiday brings no joy this year, since my grandmother died last year.

sentence: Mafarauta sun dawo daga daji da naman kanki, unguwarmu ta yi murna.
translation: The hunters came back from the bush with hartebeest meat, and our whole quarter rejoiced.

sentence: A dajin Yankari, mun ga kanki yana kiwo kusa da rafi.
translation: In the Yankari reserve we saw a hartebeest grazing near the stream.

sentence: Kakana ya ce kanki ya yi yawa a zamaninsa, amma yanzu ya ƙaranta.
translation: My grandfather says hartebeest were plentiful in his day, but now they have grown scarce.

sentence: Bayan shekaru goma na fatauci, mahaifina ya samu daula ya gina babban gida.
translation: After ten years of trading, my father came into wealth and built a big house.

sentence: Attajirin kasuwarmu yakan ce daula ba ta zuwa sai da haƙuri.
translation: The rich man in our market always says that wealth comes only through patience.

sentence: Ko da yake ɗan kasuwar yana da daula, bai sami kwanciyar hankali ba.
translation: Even though the trader has wealth, he has never found any peace of mind.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan tashe mu domin sallar asuba, sannan mu koma barci.
translation: My father wakes us for the dawn prayer, and afterwards we go back to sleep.

sentence: Mun isa Kaduna kafin sallar asuba, sai muka sauka a masallacin kan hanya.
translation: We reached Kaduna before the dawn prayer, so we stopped at the mosque by the roadside.

sentence: Jiya ban ji kiran sallar asuba ba, na farka da rana, na damu.
translation: Yesterday I never heard the call to the dawn prayer; I woke in broad daylight and felt awful.

sentence: Abokin yarintata ya iso daga Kano jiya, ya kwana a gidanmu.
translation: My childhood friend arrived from Kano yesterday and spent the night at our house.

sentence: Abokin aikina ya taimaka mini da rahoton da shugaba ya nema da gaggawa.
translation: My colleague helped me with the report the boss urgently asked for.

sentence: Na san shi tun sakandare, amma yanzu ba na ɗaukarsa a matsayin aboki.
translation: I have known him since secondary school, but I no longer count him as a friend.

sentence: Kowace shekara mukan kai ziyara masarautar Kano domin kallon hawan sallah.
translation: Every year we visit the Kano emirate to watch the sallah durbar.

sentence: Masarautar garinmu ta raba filaye ga manoman da ambaliya ta kora.
translation: Our town's emirate shared out farmland to the farmers the flood had driven from their homes.

sentence: Ina ganin masarauta tana da muhimmanci wajen shawo kan rikicin makiyaya da manoma.
translation: I think the traditional authority matters a great deal in settling the herder-farmer conflict.

sentence: Mun gayyaci liman ya zo ya raɗa wa jaririnmu suna a ranar bakwai.
translation: We invited the imam to come and name our baby on the seventh day.

sentence: Bayan sallar Juma'a, liman ya yi wa'azi game da haƙurin zama da maƙwabta.
translation: After the Friday prayer, the imam preached about being patient with one's neighbours.

sentence: Ina matuƙar girmama limaminmu, domin yakan ziyarci marasa lafiya a unguwarmu.
translation: I have great respect for our imam, because he visits the sick in our neighbourhood.

sentence: Kakana yakan ba mu labarin ranar da Sardauna ya ziyarci garinmu.
translation: My grandfather used to tell us about the day the Sardauna visited our town.

sentence: A jawabinsa, gwamna ya tuna da yadda Sardauna ya haɗa kan al'ummar Arewa.
translation: In his speech, the governor recalled how the Sardauna united the people of the North.

sentence: Sarkin Musulmi ya naɗa wani attajiri sarautar sardauna a fadar Sakkwato jiya.
translation: The Sultan conferred the title of sardauna on a wealthy man at the Sokoto palace yesterday.

sentence: Ruwan sama ya fara sauka, gara mu jira a ƙarƙashin bishiya.
translation: The rain has started coming down; we had better wait under a tree.

sentence: Tun da ba a biya mu ba, gara mu koka wa shugaban kamfanin.
translation: Since we have not been paid, we had better take our complaint to the head of the company.

sentence: Gara ka faɗa mini gaskiya yanzu da in ji ta daga wurin wani.
translation: Better that you tell me the truth now than that I hear it from someone else.

sentence: Bayan hatsarin mota, ƴan sanda sun ɗauke gawar direban zuwa asibiti.
translation: After the car crash, the police carried the driver's body away to the hospital.

sentence: Mun tarar da gawar akuya a gefen gona; kura ce ta kashe ta.
translation: We came upon a goat's carcass at the edge of the farm; it was a hyena that had killed it.

sentence: Duk iyalin sun yi kuka lokacin da aka kawo gawar mahaifinsu daga Kano.
translation: The whole family wept when their father's body was brought back from Kano.

sentence: Ɗan'uwana yakan kai ni makaranta da babur ɗinsa kowace safiya.
translation: My brother takes me to school on his motorcycle every morning.

sentence: Matashin nan yana yin achaba da babur don ya biya kuɗin makarantarsa.
translation: That young man works as a motorcycle taxi rider so he can pay his school fees.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ba ta son in hau babur ba tare da hular kwano ba.
translation: My mother does not want me riding a motorcycle without a helmet.

sentence: Ƙungiyar ma'aikata ta yi zanga-zanga kan wariyar da ake wa mata a kamfanin.
translation: The workers' union protested against the discrimination women face at the company.

sentence: Malaman makarantarmu ba sa nuna wariya tsakanin ɗalibai masu kuɗi da matalauta.
translation: The teachers at our school draw no line between the well-off pupils and the poor ones.

sentence: Wariyar launin fata da ya sha a Turai ta sa shi komawa gida.
translation: The racial discrimination he suffered in Europe is what made him go back home.

sentence: A ranar kasuwa, mutane daga ƙauyuka sukan kwaso shanu zuwa Jega.
translation: On market day, people from the villages drive their cattle over to Jega.

sentence: Motarmu ta lalace a hanya, sai muka kwana a Jega har safiya.
translation: Our car broke down on the road, so we spent the night in Jega until morning.

sentence: An haife ni a Jega, amma tun ina ƙarami muka ƙaura zuwa Sakkwato.
translation: I was born in Jega, but we moved to Sokoto when I was still small.

sentence: Raƙumin nan ya ɗauko buhunan gishiri daga hamada zuwa kasuwar garinmu.
translation: This camel carried sacks of salt all the way from the desert to our town's market.

sentence: A ranar sallah, wani raƙumi ya bi bayan sarki cikin hawan gargajiya.
translation: On the day of the festival, a camel walked behind the emir in the traditional procession.

sentence: Kada ka raina raƙumi, domin yana iya ɗaukar kaya fiye da jaki uku.
translation: Do not underrate a camel; it can carry more load than three donkeys.

sentence: Gobe ina da jarrabawar lissafi, don haka zan yi karatu har asuba.
translation: I have a maths exam tomorrow, so I'll be studying until dawn.

sentence: Malamin ya raba takardun jarrabawa, sannan ya rufe ƙofar aji.
translation: The teacher handed out the exam papers and then shut the classroom door.

sentence: Ban damu da jarrabawa ta Turanci ba, amma ta lissafi tana ba ni tsoro.
translation: The English exam doesn't worry me, but the maths one frightens me.

sentence: Kawuna ya zauna a Siriya shekara uku kafin yaƙin ya ɓarke.
translation: My uncle lived in Syria for three years before the war broke out.

sentence: Sabulun da muke saya a kasuwa ana kawo shi ne daga Siriya.
translation: The soap we buy at the market is brought in from Syria.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ji labarin Siriya a rediyo, sai zuciyata ta ɓaci.
translation: Whenever I hear the news from Syria on the radio, my heart sinks.

sentence: Kowace Jumaʼa mahaifiyata takan raba sadaka ga matalauta a gaban masallaci.
translation: Every Friday my mother hands out alms to the poor in front of the mosque.

sentence: Mun tara kuɗi a ofis, sannan muka kai sadaka gidan marayu.
translation: We collected money at the office and then took the charity to the orphanage.

sentence: Kakata ta ce sadaka tana kawar da balaʼi, shi ya sa take bayarwa kullum.
translation: My grandmother says charity wards off misfortune, which is why she gives every single day.

sentence: Malamin ya yi mana bayanin tashin kiyama har mutane suka yi kuka.
translation: The teacher described the resurrection to us until people broke down in tears.

sentence: Kakana yakan ce mana kowa zai tashi ranar kiyama, sarki da talaka.
translation: My grandfather used to tell us that everyone will rise on the Day of Resurrection, king and pauper alike.

sentence: Cunkoson mutane a kasuwar Kano ranar Talata kamar ranar kiyama yake.
translation: The crush of people at Kano market on a Tuesday is like the Day of Resurrection itself.

sentence: Mahaifina yana yin igiya da rama a bayan gida kowace maraice.
translation: My father makes rope out of hemp behind the house every evening.

sentence: Manoman ƙauyenmu sun sayar da rama a kasuwa kafin damina ta ƙare.
translation: The farmers of our village sold their hemp at the market before the rains ended.

sentence: Buhun rama ya fi na roba ƙarfi, amma yanzu ba a samunsa.
translation: A jute sack is stronger than a plastic one, but you can hardly find them now.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta zaɓi launin shuɗi don fentin ɗakin baƙi kafin bikin.
translation: My mother chose blue to paint the guest room before the wedding.

sentence: Maɗinki ya ce launin rigar ba zai canja ba ko da an wanke ta.
translation: The tailor said the gown's colour won't fade even after it is washed.

sentence: Wannan launi ya fi kama ido, shi ya sa na sayi rigar.
translation: This colour catches the eye better, and that is why I bought the gown.

sentence: Yaran makiyayi suna sara tofa don ciyar da shanu lokacin rani.
translation: The herdsman's boys are cutting elephant grass to feed the cattle in the dry season.

sentence: Mun yi shingen gonarmu da tofa, don haka awaki ba sa shiga.
translation: We fenced our farm with elephant grass, so the goats can't get in.

sentence: Tofa ta yi tsayi fiye da ni, sai da na ɓace a cikinta.
translation: The elephant grass had grown taller than me — I actually got lost inside it.

sentence: Bayan rasuwar kakana, ƙanensa ne ya zama magajin gidanmu a Kano.
translation: After my grandfather died, it was his younger brother who became the head of our household in Kano.

sentence: Sarkin garinmu ya bayyana cewa ɗansa na farko shi ne magajin sarauta.
translation: The emir of our town announced that his eldest son is the heir to the throne.

sentence: Sun yi ta jayayya a kotu kan wanda ya cancanci zama magaji.
translation: They argued in court for ages over who deserved to be the heir.

sentence: Kakata tana koya wa jikokinta kalmar shahada tun suna ƙanana.
translation: My grandmother teaches her grandchildren the words of the shahada while they are still small.

sentence: Wani baƙo ya karɓi Musulunci, ya furta shahada a gaban limamin masallaci.
translation: A stranger embraced Islam and pronounced the shahada before the mosque's imam.

sentence: Ɗan sanda ya mutu mutuwar shahada yayin da yake ceto yara daga gobara.
translation: The policeman died a martyr's death while rescuing children from a fire.

sentence: Bayan girbi mai kyau, wada ta shiga gidajen ƙauyenmu bana.
translation: After a good harvest, plenty came into the homes of our village this year.

sentence: Kakana ya ce wadar zuci ta fi dukiyar duniya kyau.
translation: My grandfather says contentment of heart is worth more than all the world's riches.

sentence: Ciniki ya haifar da wada a garinmu tun da aka gina sabuwar hanya.
translation: Trade has brought wealth to our town ever since the new road was built.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifina yakan tashi da wuri ya koma sansanin soja.
translation: Every morning my father gets up early and heads back to the army barracks.

sentence: Mun kwana biyu a sansanin 'yan gudun hijira muna raba abinci.
translation: We spent two nights at the refugee camp handing out food.

sentence: Ban taɓa mantawa da yadda muka sha wahala a sansanin ba.
translation: I have never forgotten how much we suffered in that camp.

sentence: Kakata takan ba mu labarin Adamu da Hauwa kafin mu kwanta barci.
translation: My grandmother used to tell us the story of Adam and Eve before we went to sleep.

sentence: Malamin makaranta ya yi mana bayanin yadda Hauwa da Adamu suka bar Aljanna.
translation: The schoolteacher explained to us how Eve and Adam came to leave Paradise.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda mutane suke zargin Hauwa ita kaɗai a kan wannan laifi.
translation: It amazes me how people blame Eve alone for that sin.

sentence: Yin asawaki kafin sallah sunna ce da nake ƙoƙarin kiyayewa.
translation: Using a chewing stick before prayer is a sunnah I try hard to keep up.

sentence: Malam ya bayyana mana cewa azumin Litinin sunna ce, ba wajibi ba.
translation: The teacher explained to us that fasting on Mondays is sunnah, not an obligation.

sentence: Kakana ya rasu yana bin sunnar Annabi cikin kowane ƙaramin abu.
translation: My grandfather died still following the Prophet's sunnah in every small thing.

sentence: Kowace safiya nakan ji kukan wala daga bishiyar mangwaro bayan gida.
translation: Every morning I hear a turtledove cooing from the mango tree behind the house.

sentence: Mafarauta sun kama wala biyu a jeji, suka sayar da su a kasuwa.
translation: The hunters caught two turtledoves out in the bush and sold them at the market.

sentence: Muryar wala tana sanya min kwanciyar hankali fiye da kowace waƙa.
translation: The sound of a turtledove settles my mind better than any song does.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta sayi tsoka kawai, saboda ba ma cin hanji a gida.
translation: My mother bought only lean meat, because we don't eat offal at home.

sentence: Bayan wata uku a wurin motsa jiki, tsokar hannunsa ta fara bayyana.
translation: After three months at the gym, the muscle in his arms began to show.

sentence: Yau ina jin ciwon tsoka a duk jikina bayan aikin gonar jiya.
translation: Today I ache in every muscle after yesterday's work on the farm.

sentence: Na cika fom ɗin neman fasfo, amma ban manna hoto ba.
translation: I filled in the passport application form, but I forgot to attach a photograph.

sentence: Kafin a shigar da yaro makaranta, dole a cika fom a biya kuɗi.
translation: Before a child can be enrolled in school, a form must be filled in and the fees paid.

sentence: Fom ɗin bankin ya cika da tambayoyi har na gaji kafin in ƙarasa.
translation: The bank's form had so many questions that I was worn out before I finished it.

sentence: Har yanzu ina jiran tabbatarwa daga bankin kafin in fitar da kuɗin.
translation: I am still waiting for confirmation from the bank before I take the money out.

sentence: Sun aiko mini da saƙon tabbatarwa bayan na biya kuɗin ɗakin otal.
translation: They sent me a confirmation message after I paid for the hotel room.

sentence: Tabbatarwar sakamakon jarrabawa ta faranta mini rai bayan watanni na damuwa.
translation: The confirmation of the exam results made me happy after months of worry.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan daka gero ta yi fura da safe kafin mu tashi.
translation: My mother pounds millet and makes fura in the morning before we are even up.

sentence: Bana ruwa bai isa ba, don haka gero bai yi kyau a gonarmu ba.
translation: The rains fell short this year, so the millet did poorly on our farm.

sentence: Ba na jin daɗin kunun masara; kunun gero ne kaɗai nake so.
translation: I don't enjoy maize porridge; millet porridge is the only one I like.

sentence: Mun sauka a Kaita don mu sayi tumaki kafin mu koma Katsina.
translation: We stopped off in Kaita to buy sheep before heading back to Katsina.

sentence: Kawuna malamin makaranta ne a Kaita, yana koyar da Hausa tun shekaru goma.
translation: My uncle is a schoolteacher in Kaita; he has been teaching Hausa for ten years.

sentence: Kasuwar Kaita tana ba ni sha'awa saboda yawan shanu da ake kawowa.
translation: Kaita's market fascinates me because of all the cattle people bring to it.

sentence: Ɗan uwana ya tafi Ikko neman aiki, tun bara bai dawo ba.
translation: My brother went to Lagos to look for work, and he hasn't been back since last year.

sentence: Motar da za ta kai mu Ikko tana tashi ƙarfe biyar na safe.
translation: The bus that takes us to Lagos leaves at five in the morning.

sentence: Cunkoson ababen hawa a Ikko ya sa na makara zuwa taron aiki.
translation: The traffic in Lagos made me late for the work meeting.

sentence: Jirgin ruwan ya yi ta zara a tafkin, har fasinjoji suka fara tsoro.
translation: The boat kept swaying from side to side on the lake until the passengers grew frightened.

sentence: Shugaban ya yi ta zara tsakanin shawara biyu har taron ya ƙare.
translation: The chairman kept wavering between two proposals until the meeting simply ended.

sentence: Ba na son zara; idan na yanke shawara, ba na sake tunani.
translation: I have no patience for dithering; once I have decided, I do not reconsider.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta ajiye kayan zinariya a cikin akwati har bikin ƙanwata.
translation: My mother kept the gold jewellery locked in a chest until my younger sister's wedding.

sentence: Maƙerin zinariya ya auna zoben a kasuwar Kurmi kafin ya faɗa mana farashi.
translation: The goldsmith weighed the ring at Kurmi market before quoting us a price.

sentence: Tun da aka gano zinariya a ƙauyen, na daina barci saboda ƙarar injuna.
translation: Ever since gold was found in the village, I have not slept properly because of the noise of the machines.

sentence: Amarya ta shafa kwalli da mishi kafin ta fito wajen bikin.
translation: The bride lined her eyes with kohl on the little stick before she came out to the ceremony.

sentence: Na sayi ƙaramin mishi a kasuwar Kano don shafa wa ʼyata kwalli.
translation: I bought a small kohl stick at Kano market for putting kohl on my daughter.

sentence: Kada ki yi amfani da mishi ɗaya da abokanki, cutar ido tana yaɗuwa.
translation: Don't share one kohl stick with your friends — eye infections spread that way.

sentence: Ya buɗe hannuwansa walau ya nuna mana ba shi da ko sisi.
translation: He spread his palms wide open to show us that he had not a single coin.

sentence: Mai gadi ya ce mu ɗaga hannuwanmu walau kafin mu shiga cikin fadar.
translation: The guard told us to raise our hands with the palms open before we entered the palace.

sentence: Bayan shekara uku a ƙasar waje, ya dawo gida hannu walau.
translation: After three years abroad, he came back home with nothing but open palms.

sentence: Malam ya rubuta adadi biyu a allo ya ce mu haɗa su.
translation: The teacher wrote two numbers on the board and told us to add them together.

sentence: Adadin masu jira a asibitin ya haura ɗari kafin ƙarfe tara.
translation: The number of people waiting at the clinic had passed a hundred before nine o'clock.

sentence: Ban damu da adadin baƙi ba, abincin da muka dafa zai ishe kowa.
translation: I'm not worried about how many guests turn up — the food we cooked will be enough for everyone.

sentence: Kakata ta dafa miyar ganyen tsamiya, ƙamshinta ya bazu a duk unguwar.
translation: My grandmother cooked tamarind-leaf soup, and the smell drifted right across the neighbourhood.

sentence: Manoma sukan huta a ƙarƙashin tsamiya bayan sun gama noma da rana.
translation: The farmers rest under the tamarind tree once they have finished the midday work on the farm.

sentence: Ba na son ʼyaʼyan tsamiya, amma yaran ƙauyen suna tsinta su duk yamma.
translation: I don't care for tamarind fruit, but the village children gather it up every evening.

sentence: Ɗan uwana yana karatun likitanci a Masar tun shekaru uku da suka wuce.
translation: My brother has been studying medicine in Egypt for the past three years.

sentence: Yawancin kayan kwalliyar da ake sayarwa a nan suna zuwa daga Masar.
translation: Most of the cosmetics sold here are brought in from Egypt.

sentence: Ina fatan zan ziyarci Masar in ga kogin Nilu da idona.
translation: I hope to visit Egypt one day and see the Nile with my own eyes.

sentence: Masu busa kakaki sun tsaya a ƙofar fada suna jiran sarki.
translation: The kakaki players stood at the palace gate, waiting for the emir to appear.

sentence: Da na ji karar kakaki daga nesa, sai na san hawan Sallah ya soma.
translation: When I heard the kakaki in the distance, I knew the Sallah durbar had begun.

sentence: A ganina, babu kayan kiɗa da ya kai kakaki ɗaukaka a ƙasar Hausa.
translation: To my mind, no instrument carries the prestige the kakaki does in Hausaland.

sentence: Kwano ɗaya tilo ya rage a gidan, sai muka ci abinci tare.
translation: A single bowl was all that was left in the house, so we ate together out of it.

sentence: Wannan ita ce hanya ɗaya tilo da ke kai mu ƙauyen bayan ruwa.
translation: This is the only road that gets us to the village once the rains have come.

sentence: Ta yi kuka lokacin da ɗanta tilo ya tashi zuwa aikin soja.
translation: She wept on the day her only son left for his posting with the army.

sentence: Ta sayi laba biyu na nama don abincin baƙin da suka sauka.
translation: She bought two pounds of meat to feed the guests who had just arrived.

sentence: Mai shago ya auna sukari laba ɗaya ya naɗe shi cikin takarda.
translation: The shopkeeper weighed out a pound of sugar and wrapped it up in paper.

sentence: Tun da farashi ya tashi, ba ma iya sayen laba biyu na nama.
translation: Since prices went up, we can no longer afford to buy two pounds of meat.

sentence: Ban sami izinin mahaifina ba, don haka na kwana a gida.
translation: I didn't get my father's permission, so I spent the night at home.

sentence: Dole in nemi izini a wurin manajan kafin in tafi asibiti.
translation: I have to get permission from the manager before I go to the hospital.

sentence: Na fusata domin sun sare bishiyar ba tare da izinina ba.
translation: I was furious because they cut the tree down without my permission.

sentence: Kakata ta rene maraya tun yana jariri har ya girma.
translation: My grandmother raised an orphan from infancy until he was grown.

sentence: Wani maraya ne ya lashe gasar karatun Alƙur'ani a garinmu bana.
translation: It was an orphan who won the Qur'an recitation contest in our town this year.

sentence: Zuciyata ta yi ciwo lokacin da maraya ya nemi abinci a kasuwa.
translation: My heart ached when an orphan came begging for food at the market.

sentence: Matata ta gano aibu a atamfar da ta saya jiya a kasuwa.
translation: My wife found a flaw in the wrapper cloth she bought at the market yesterday.

sentence: Makanikin ya duba motar sannan ya nuna mana aibu a birkinta.
translation: The mechanic looked the car over and then showed us a fault in its brakes.

sentence: Ba na son mutumin da yake fallasa aibun abokan aikinsa a gaban shugaba.
translation: I can't stand a man who exposes his colleagues' faults in front of the boss.

sentence: Yayata ta dafa tuwon dawa da miyar kuka don abincin dare.
translation: My elder sister cooked sorghum tuwo with baobab-leaf soup for dinner.

sentence: Manoma sun girbe dawa kafin ruwan sama ya lalata gonakinsu.
translation: The farmers harvested the sorghum before the rain could ruin their fields.

sentence: Farashin dawa ya tashi sosai a kasuwa, hakan ya dami iyaye da yawa.
translation: The price of sorghum has shot up at the market, and that worries a lot of parents.

sentence: Mun hau tsauni da safe don mu kalli garin daga sama.
translation: We climbed the hill in the morning to look down on the town from above.

sentence: Makiyaya suna kiwon shanu a bayan tsauni har zuwa faɗuwar rana.
translation: The herders graze their cattle behind the hill until the sun goes down.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na hau wannan tsauni, sai in tuna da kakana.
translation: Every time I climb this hill, I end up thinking about my grandfather.

sentence: Ki wanke kofi ki ajiye shi kan tebur kafin baƙi su zo.
translation: Wash a cup and set it on the table before the guests arrive.

sentence: Mai shayi ya zuba mini kofin shayi mai zafi kafin in shiga aiki.
translation: The tea seller poured me a hot cup of tea before I started work.

sentence: Ina ƙaunar wannan kofin domin abokina ne ya kawo mini shi daga Makka.
translation: I treasure this cup because my friend brought it back for me from Mecca.

sentence: Na kashe dubbai wajen gyara motata bayan haɗarin da ya faru.
translation: I spent thousands repairing my car after the accident.

sentence: Dubbai sun halarci jana'izar malamin a filin wasa na Kano.
translation: Thousands attended the scholar's funeral at the stadium in Kano.

sentence: Abin takaici, dubbai daga cikin yaran ƙauyen ba sa zuwa makaranta kwata-kwata.
translation: Sadly, thousands of the village children don't go to school at all.

sentence: Shagon nan ya samu tagomashi sosai tun bayan da suka rage farashin.
translation: That shop has become really popular since they lowered their prices.

sentence: Sabon shugaban ya samu tagomashi a wurin matasa saboda aikin da ya yi.
translation: The new leader has won favour among young people because of the work he did.

sentence: Tagomashin da mawaƙin ya samu bai canza halinsa ba ko kaɗan.
translation: The popularity the singer gained hasn't changed his character one bit.

sentence: Kowace Lahadi muna tashi da wuri mu je coci kafin ƙarfe takwas.
translation: Every Sunday we get up early so we can be at church before eight.

sentence: Sun gyara rufin cocin bayan iska ta kwashe shi a lokacin damina.
translation: They repaired the church roof after the wind tore it off in the rainy season.

sentence: Muryar mawaƙan cocin tana kwantar mini da hankali duk lokacin da na damu.
translation: The church choir's singing settles my mind whenever I'm troubled.

sentence: A lokacin annoba, mahaifiyata takan tafasa ruwa kafin mu sha shi.
translation: During the epidemic my mother would boil the water before we drank it.

sentence: Ma'aikatan lafiya sun yi allurar rigakafi don daƙile annobar sankarau a jihar.
translation: Health workers gave vaccinations to halt the meningitis epidemic in the state.

sentence: Annobar ta yi sanadin rufe makarantu, iyaye kuwa sun shiga damuwa matuƙa.
translation: The epidemic caused schools to close, and parents were deeply worried.

sentence: Kakata ta ce an yi mata girka tun tana ƙarama a Maradi.
translation: My grandmother says her initiation was performed for her back when she was a young girl in Maradi.

sentence: Masu ganga sun kwana bakwai suna kiɗa kafin a fara girka a unguwarmu.
translation: The drummers played for seven straight nights before the initiation could begin in our quarter.

sentence: Mahaifina ba ya son girka, yana cewa bai dace da addininmu ba.
translation: My father has no time for the initiation; he says it doesn't square with our faith.

sentence: Ɗanʼuwana ya yi dogo sosai, tufafinsa duk sun gajarta masa.
translation: My brother has shot up so tall that every one of his clothes is too short on him.

sentence: Layin bankin ya yi dogo, mun tsaya har rana ta yi zafi.
translation: The queue at the bank was long; we stood in it until the sun turned hot.

sentence: Malamin nan dogo ne kuma mai sanyin murya, ɗalibai suna sonsa ƙwarai.
translation: That teacher is tall and soft-spoken, and the students are really fond of him.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta nemi zare mai ruwan shuɗi don ta ɗinka maɓallin rigata.
translation: My mother went looking for blue thread so she could sew the button back onto my shirt.

sentence: Maɗinkin kasuwa ya ce zare ya ƙare, sai mu dawo gobe da safe.
translation: The tailor at the market said he had run out of thread, so we should come back tomorrow morning.

sentence: Kyanwa ta yi wasa da zare har ta warware saƙar kakata gaba ɗaya.
translation: The cat played with the thread until it had completely unravelled my grandmother's knitting.

sentence: Tukunyar ba ta da makama, sai na naɗe zani kafin in ɗauke ta.
translation: The pot has no handle, so I wrapped a cloth around it before lifting it.

sentence: Alƙali ya ce ƙarar ba ta da makama, sai ya kore ta.
translation: The judge said the suit had no grounds, and threw it out.

sentence: Dalilin da ya bayar ba shi da makama, na san yana ɓoye min gaskiya.
translation: The reason he gave holds no water; I know he is hiding the truth from me.

sentence: Yaron ya fusata mahaifiyarsa saboda ya sake karya faranti a kicin.
translation: The boy angered his mother by breaking yet another plate in the kitchen.

sentence: Direban mota ya fusata da fasinjan da ya ƙi biyan kuɗin hawa.
translation: The driver lost his temper with the passenger who refused to pay his fare.

sentence: Kada ka fusata idan na faɗa maka gaskiya, ni abokinka ne.
translation: Don't take offence when I tell you the truth — I'm your friend.

sentence: Kafin sallar Jumaʼa, baba yakan shafa turare ya sa hularsa.
translation: Before Friday prayers, father always puts on perfume and sets his cap on his head.

sentence: Amarya ta ƙona turare a ɗakin har baƙi suka ji ƙamshi daga waje.
translation: The bride burned incense in the room until the guests could smell it from outside.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ji wannan turare, sai in tuna da kakata.
translation: Every time I catch this scent, I find myself thinking of my grandmother.

sentence: Kawuna yana aiki a gonar inabi a Italiya, yana aiko mana kuɗi.
translation: My uncle works on a vineyard in Italy and sends money home to us.

sentence: ʼYan wasan Najeriya sun sha kaye a hannun Italiya a wasan ƙarshe.
translation: Nigeria's players were beaten by Italy in the final.

sentence: Ina fatan ziyartar Italiya domin in ga tsofaffin gine-ginen da malamina ya kwatanta.
translation: I hope to visit Italy so I can see the old buildings my teacher described to us.

sentence: Awaki sun shiga gonar kakata suka cinye duk ganyen alayyahu.
translation: The goats got into my grandmother's garden and ate every last spinach leaf.

sentence: A kasuwar dabbobi ta Kano, ana sayar da awaki masu ƙiba kafin sallah.
translation: At the livestock market in Kano they sell fattened goats in the run-up to Sallah.

sentence: Ina son kiwon awaki fiye da shanu domin ba sa buƙatar wuri mai faɗi.
translation: I would rather keep goats than cattle, because they don't need much space.

sentence: Malam ya bayyana cewa sallar asuba farali ce, ba nafila ba.
translation: The teacher explained that the dawn prayer is an obligation, not an optional act.

sentence: A makarantar allo, muna koyon abin da yake farali kafin mu koyi sunnah.
translation: At the Qurʼanic school we learn what is obligatory before we learn what is merely recommended.

sentence: Na ɗauki kula da iyayena a matsayin farali, ba wai zaɓi ba.
translation: I treat caring for my parents as a duty, not as a choice.

sentence: Tuhuma ta shiga zuciyata saʼad da na tarar da ƙofar a buɗe.
translation: Suspicion crept into my heart when I came upon the door standing open.

sentence: ʼYan sanda sun kama shi bisa tuhuma da sace wayar wani fasinja.
translation: The police arrested him on suspicion of stealing a passenger's phone.

sentence: Tuhuma ba tare da shaida ba tana ɓata zumunci tsakanin maƙwabta.
translation: Suspicion without any evidence ruins the bond between neighbours.

sentence: Maina ya shiga gidan sarki da safe yana neman mahaifinsa.
translation: The prince walked into the emir's palace at dawn looking for his father.

sentence: A ranar Sallah, maina yakan raba abinci ga talakawan garin.
translation: On Sallah day the prince hands out food to the poor of the town.

sentence: Ina ganin maina ya fi kowa hikima a cikin ʼyaʼyan sarki.
translation: To my mind the prince is the wisest of all the emir's children.

sentence: Kakata ta koya mini cewa kamala ta fi kuɗi daraja.
translation: My grandmother taught me that dignity is worth more than money.

sentence: Malamin ya ce kamala tana cikin yadda kake mutunta baƙi.
translation: The teacher said decency shows in the way you treat a guest.

sentence: Ya rasa kamala a idon mutane tun bayan ya ci amanar abokinsa.
translation: He lost his good name in people's eyes after he betrayed his friend.

sentence: Yusufu ya manta da mabuɗin gida, sai muka jira shi a bakin ƙofa.
translation: Yusufu forgot the house key, so we ended up waiting for him at the door.

sentence: Malam ya ba mu labarin Annabi Yusufu da ʼyanʼuwansa suka jefa a rijiya.
translation: The teacher told us the story of the prophet Joseph, whom his brothers threw into a well.

sentence: Ina son sunan Yusufu domin yana tunatar da ni haƙurin annabin.
translation: I like the name Yusufu because it reminds me of that prophet's patience.

sentence: Na kai riga wurin tela don ya gyara hannunta kafin Sallah.
translation: I took the gown to the tailor so he could fix its sleeve before Sallah.

sentence: Tela ya ɗinka mini kaftani cikin kwana uku kafin bikin ɗan uwana.
translation: The tailor sewed me a caftan in three days, in time for my brother's wedding.

sentence: Ban gamsu da aikin tela ba, don ya ɗinka wandona da faɗi sosai.
translation: I wasn't happy with the tailor's work, because he cut my trousers far too wide.

sentence: Kakana yana alfahari da zuriya mai yawa da Allah ya ba shi.
translation: My grandfather takes pride in the many descendants God has given him.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya bayyana yadda zuriya ɗaya ta kafa garuruwa da yawa.
translation: The history teacher explained how a single line of descendants founded many towns.

sentence: Ina fatan zuriya ta gaji sanaʼar saƙa da muka koya daga kakanninmu.
translation: I hope our descendants inherit the weaving trade we learned from our grandparents.

sentence: Yara suna tsotsar rake a gefen hanya bayan sun dawo daga makaranta.
translation: The children are chewing sugarcane by the roadside after getting back from school.

sentence: Mai sayar da rake ya rage mini kuɗi domin na sayi da yawa.
translation: The sugarcane seller cut the price for me because I bought so much.

sentence: Rake na bana bai yi zaƙi kamar na bara ba.
translation: This year's sugarcane hasn't come out as sweet as last year's.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan saka tafarnuwa da albasa a miya don ta yi ƙamshi.
translation: My mother puts garlic and onion in the stew to give it a good smell.

sentence: Na sayi tafarnuwa a kasuwar Sabon Gari, amma farashinta ya tashi sosai.
translation: I bought garlic at Sabon Gari market, but the price has shot right up.

sentence: Kakata ta ce tafarnuwa tana warkar da mura fiye da maganin asibiti.
translation: My grandmother says garlic cures a cold better than hospital medicine does.

sentence: Yara sukan taru a dandali da yamma domin su buga ƙwallo.
translation: The children gather in the town square in the evening to play football.

sentence: Sarkin garin ya yi jawabi a dandali gaban dubban mutane jiya.
translation: The town's emir gave a speech in the square before thousands of people yesterday.

sentence: Ina son zama a dandali da dare, ina sauraron tatsuniyar tsofaffi.
translation: I love sitting out in the square at night, listening to the old people's tales.

sentence: Kowace safiya nakan tashi in shayar da saniya kafin in tafi makaranta.
translation: Every morning I get up and water the cow before I set off for school.

sentence: Mahaifina ya sayi saniya a kasuwar dabbobi don bikin auren ʼyar uwata.
translation: My father bought a cow at the livestock market for my sister's wedding.

sentence: Ban taɓa tsoron saniya ba, sai da wata ta kore ni a gona.
translation: I was never afraid of a cow until one chased me across the farm.

sentence: Yarinyar ta ɗaura ƙyalle a kai, tana cewa ita sarauniya ce yau.
translation: The little girl tied a cloth round her head and announced that today she is the queen.

sentence: Sarauniya ta halarci bikin sarki, dukan matan gari suka yi mata rakiya.
translation: The queen attended the emir's celebration, and all the women of the town escorted her.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda sarauniya ta yi mulkin ƙasar nan cikin zaman lafiya.
translation: It amazes me how the queen ruled this country while keeping the peace.

sentence: Da ruwan sama ya fara, sai muka nemi mafaka a ƙarƙashin bishiyar kuka.
translation: When the rain started, we took shelter under the baobab tree.

sentence: Makarantar firamare ta zama mafaka ga iyalai da suka gudu daga rikici.
translation: The primary school became a refuge for families who had fled the fighting.

sentence: A gare ni, babu wata mafaka da ta fi ɗakin kakata a duniya.
translation: For me there is no safer haven in the world than my grandmother's room.

sentence: Limamai uku sun taru a masallaci don warware husuma tsakanin maƙwabta.
translation: Three imams met at the mosque to settle a quarrel between neighbours.

sentence: Limamai sukan yi waʼazi mai tsawo a ranar Jumaʼa kafin sallah.
translation: Imams usually give a long sermon on Friday before the prayer.

sentence: Ban gamsu ba, domin limamai da yawa sun yi shiru kan wannan matsalar.
translation: I am not satisfied, because many imams have stayed silent about this problem.

sentence: A watan Rajab, kakata takan yi azumi kwana uku a kowane mako.
translation: In the month of Rajab my grandmother fasts three days every week.

sentence: Mun daura auren ƙanwata a Rajab, kafin mutane su fara shirin Ramadan.
translation: We held my younger sister's wedding in Rajab, before people started preparing for Ramadan.

sentence: Ina son watan Rajab, don masallacin unguwarmu yakan cika da yara masu karatu.
translation: I love the month of Rajab, because our neighbourhood mosque fills up with children reciting.

sentence: Ɓarayi sun shiga gidanmu da daddare, suka kwashe kayan lantarki kaf.
translation: Thieves got into our house in the night and carried off every last appliance.

sentence: Yayin da nake gyaran keke, wani ya sace kuɗina kaf.
translation: While I was repairing the bicycle, somebody stole every last naira I had.

sentence: Na yi baƙin ciki sosai domin ambaliyar ta kwashe hatsin gonarmu kaf.
translation: I was heartbroken, because the flood swept away every bit of grain from our farm.

sentence: Ɗan uwana yana aiki a kamfanin mai da ke Fatakwal tun bara.
translation: My brother has been working at an oil company in Port Harcourt since last year.

sentence: Mun ɗauki bas ɗin dare zuwa Fatakwal, muka isa da sassafe.
translation: We took the night bus to Port Harcourt and arrived at daybreak.

sentence: Ban taɓa jin daɗin damina a Fatakwal ba, ruwan sama ba ya tsayawa.
translation: I have never enjoyed the rainy season in Port Harcourt; the rain simply does not stop.

sentence: Kakata takan zuba citta a cikin shayi domin ta rage tari.
translation: My grandmother puts ginger in the tea to ease a cough.

sentence: Matar da ke sayar da citta a kasuwa ta rage mini kuɗi jiya.
translation: The woman who sells ginger in the market knocked something off the price for me yesterday.

sentence: Ba na iya cin miya mai yawan citta, domin tana ƙona mini harshe.
translation: I cannot eat stew with a lot of ginger in it, because it burns my tongue.

sentence: A watan Fabrairu muna noman tumatir a fadama, saboda ruwan rijiya ya isa.
translation: In February we grow tomatoes on the floodplain, because the well water is enough.

sentence: Jarrabawar ƙarshen zangon farko za ta fara ranar goma ga Fabrairu.
translation: The first-term final exams will begin on the tenth of February.

sentence: Fabrairu gajeren wata ne, don haka albashi yakan ƙare kafin mu farga.
translation: February is a short month, so the salary runs out before we even notice.

sentence: Malam ya tunatar da mu cewa kowa zai fuskanci hisabi a ranar ƙiyama.
translation: The teacher reminded us that everyone will face the reckoning on the Day of Judgement.

sentence: Kakana yakan ce tsoron hisabi ne ke hana shi cin haƙƙin mutane.
translation: My grandfather says it is fear of the reckoning that stops him from taking what belongs to others.

sentence: Da ya ji waʼazin hisabi, sai ya mayar da kuɗin da ya karɓa.
translation: After hearing the sermon about the reckoning, he gave back the money he had taken.

sentence: Mun bi wani tafarki mai kunci har muka isa rijiyar ƙauye.
translation: We followed a narrow path until we reached the village well.

sentence: Direban ya bar babbar hanya, sai ya bi tafarki mai ƙura zuwa ƙauyen.
translation: The driver left the highway and took a dusty track towards the village.

sentence: Iyayena sun koya mini cewa haƙuri shi ne tafarki mafi sauƙi a rayuwa.
translation: My parents taught me that patience is the easiest path through life.

sentence: Mun sauka daga safa a Zariya don sayen abinci kafin mu ci gaba.
translation: We got down from the bus in Zaria to buy food before travelling on.

sentence: Safa ta cika da fasinjoji, don haka na tsaya har muka isa Kaduna.
translation: The bus was packed with passengers, so I stood the whole way to Kaduna.

sentence: Ba na son tafiya da safa da daddare, domin hanyar ba ta da tsaro.
translation: I don't like travelling by intercity bus at night, because the road isn't safe.

sentence: Kowane sashi na wannan birni yana da kasuwarsa da masallacinsa.
translation: Every district of this city has its own market and its own mosque.

sentence: Malam ya raba aji zuwa sashi uku don kowa ya samu damar magana.
translation: The teacher split the class into three sections so that everyone would get a chance to speak.

sentence: Sashi na farko na littafin ya fi ƙarshensa daɗi sosai.
translation: The first part of the book was far more enjoyable than its ending.

sentence: Kowace safiya nakan hau keke zuwa makaranta domin kuɗin mota ya yi yawa.
translation: Every morning I cycle to school because the bus fare has got too high.

sentence: Mahaifina yana gyara keke a bakin titi tun kafin a haife ni.
translation: My father has been mending bicycles at the roadside since before I was born.

sentence: Ban taɓa mantawa da ranar da kawuna ya sayo mini sabon keke ba.
translation: I have never forgotten the day my uncle bought me a new bicycle.

sentence: Na yi alwala a gida saboda ruwan masallaci ya ƙare.
translation: I did my ablutions at home because the mosque had run out of water.

sentence: Kafin sallar azahar, ɗalibai sukan yi alwala a bayan makarantar.
translation: Before the noon prayer, the students perform their ablutions behind the school.

sentence: Sanyin ruwan rijiya ya sa yin alwala da sassafe ya yi mini wuya.
translation: The cold well water made doing my ablutions at dawn hard for me.

sentence: Iyayena sun gudu daga garinsu lokacin da basasa ta ɓarke a arewa.
translation: My parents fled their town when the civil war broke out in the north.

sentence: Jaridar ta ce basasa ta tilasta wa dubban manoma barin ƙauyukansu.
translation: The newspaper said the civil war had forced thousands of farmers to abandon their villages.

sentence: Duk lokacin da aka ambaci basasa, kakata takan fashe da kuka.
translation: Whenever the civil war is mentioned, my grandmother bursts into tears.

sentence: Kowace Lahadi, kakata takan karanta labarin haihuwar Almasihu ga jikokinta.
translation: Every Sunday my grandmother reads her grandchildren the story of the Messiah's birth.

sentence: Malamin makarantar Lahadi ya bayyana wa yara yadda Almasihu ya warkar da makaho.
translation: The Sunday-school teacher explained to the children how the Messiah healed a blind man.

sentence: Musulmai da Kiristoci duk sun yarda cewa Almasihu zai dawo duniya wata rana.
translation: Muslims and Christians alike believe that the Messiah will return to the world one day.

sentence: Likita ya ce in riƙa shafa man zaitun a gashina duk mako.
translation: The doctor told me to rub olive oil into my hair every week.

sentence: A kasuwar Kano, mun sayi man zaitun mai tsada daga wani ɗan Larabe.
translation: At the Kano market we bought expensive olive oil from an Arab trader.

sentence: Itacen zaitun yana da tsawon rai fiye da mutumin da ya shuka shi.
translation: An olive tree outlives the person who planted it.

sentence: Abdu ya manta da mabuɗin gida, sai ya kwana a wurin abokinsa.
translation: Abdu forgot the house key, so he spent the night at his friend's place.

sentence: Kowace rana Abdu yakan tashi da ƙarfe biyar don ya kai kaya kasuwa.
translation: Every day Abdu is up by five so he can take the goods to the market.

sentence: Kowa a unguwar yana kiransa Abdu, ko da yake sunansa Abdullahi ne.
translation: Everyone in the neighbourhood calls him Abdu, even though his name is Abdullahi.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta zuba tuwo a cikin kwano, ta rufe shi har muka dawo.
translation: My mother put the tuwo in a bowl and kept it covered until we got back.

sentence: A kasuwa, na yi ciniki har na sayi kwano biyu kan naira dubu.
translation: At the market I haggled until I got two bowls for a thousand naira.

sentence: Yara sun yi ta bugun kwano suna waƙa har maƙwabta suka yi fushi.
translation: The children kept banging on a pan and singing until the neighbours got angry.

sentence: Yaya ya shigo gida da albishir cewa an ba shi aiki a bankin.
translation: My elder brother came home with the good news that he had been given a job at the bank.

sentence: Likitan ya fito ya ba mu albishir cewa mahaifiyarmu ta warke.
translation: The doctor came out and gave us the good news that our mother had recovered.

sentence: Bayan ya kawo mana albishir, sai ya tsaya yana jiran ladarsa.
translation: After bringing us the good news, he stood there waiting for his reward.

sentence: Bayan sallar isha, mukan zauna a farfajiya muna sauraron labaran kakata.
translation: After the night prayer we sit out in the courtyard listening to my grandmother's stories.

sentence: Kasuwar dare ba ta buɗewa sai bayan an gama sallar isha.
translation: The night market does not open until the Isha prayer is over.

sentence: Na kasa yin sallar isha da wuri domin barci ya kwashe ni.
translation: I couldn't pray Isha early because sleep carried me off.

sentence: Mahaifina yana rubuta lissafin shagonsa da ajami a cikin tsohon littafi.
translation: My father keeps his shop's accounts in Ajami in an old notebook.

sentence: Malamin makarantar allo yana koya wa yara rubutun ajami kowace safiya.
translation: The Quranic-school teacher teaches the children to write Ajami every morning.

sentence: Kakata ta yi kuka lokacin da muka karanta mata wasiƙar ajami.
translation: My grandmother wept when we read her the letter written in Ajami.

sentence: Na sha azaba da ciwon haƙori a daren jiya, ban yi barci ba.
translation: I went through agony with toothache last night and never slept at all.

sentence: Manoman ƙauyenmu sun sha azaba bana saboda ambaliyar ruwa.
translation: The farmers in our village suffered terribly this year because of the flood.

sentence: Zaman gidan yari azaba ce da ba zan taɓa mantawa da ita ba.
translation: Life in prison is a torment I will never be able to forget.

sentence: Ɗana ya makara, uzurinsa shi ne motar makaranta ta lalace a hanya.
translation: My son came home late; his excuse was that the school bus broke down on the way.

sentence: Na kawo uzurin rashin lafiya, amma shugaban aiki bai karɓa ba.
translation: I offered illness as my excuse, but the boss would not accept it.

sentence: Ba ni da wani uzuri da zan kawo, na manta ranar haihuwarki.
translation: I have no excuse to offer — I forgot your birthday.

sentence: Mijinta ya dawo da dare, ya ishe ta tana barci a falo.
translation: Her husband got back late at night and came upon her asleep in the sitting room.

sentence: Mun tashi daga kasuwa da latti, dare ya ishe mu a hanya.
translation: We left the market late, and night overtook us on the road.

sentence: Da na kai asibiti, na ishe mahaifiyata tana kuka a bakin ƙofa.
translation: When I got to the hospital I found my mother crying in the doorway.

sentence: Mama ta tashi tun kafin asuba don ta dafa mana kunu.
translation: Mum got up before dawn to cook us kunu.

sentence: Mama tana sayar da kayan miya a kasuwar Kurmi kowace Litinin.
translation: Mum sells soup ingredients at Kurmi market every Monday.

sentence: Ina kewar Mama sosai tun da na fara zama a Legas.
translation: I have missed Mum badly ever since I started living in Lagos.

sentence: Malam ya rubuta lugga a allo, sai ɗalibai suka yi shiru.
translation: The teacher wrote an obscure old word on the board and the students went silent.

sentence: Waƙoƙin tsofaffin mawaƙa suna cike da lugga da ba ma fahimta.
translation: The songs of the old poets are packed with arcane words we don't even understand.

sentence: Kakana yakan yi magana da lugga har mu kasa gane maganarsa.
translation: My grandfather peppers his speech with obscure words until we can't follow what he means.

sentence: Malam ya sa mu haddace baiti na farko kafin darasin gobe.
translation: The teacher made us memorise the first stanza before tomorrow's lesson.

sentence: Mawaƙin ya maimaita baiti na ƙarshe sau uku, mutane suka yi ta tafi.
translation: The singer repeated the last stanza three times and the crowd kept on clapping.

sentence: Kowane baiti a cikin waƙar nan yana tunatar da ni gidanmu na ƙauye.
translation: Every stanza in this song reminds me of our house back in the village.

sentence: A yau yayata ba za ta iya azumi ba saboda tana cikin haila.
translation: My elder sister cannot fast today because she is menstruating.

sentence: Malamar lafiya ta bayyana wa yaran mata yadda haila take faruwa kowane wata.
translation: The health teacher explained to the girls how menstruation happens each month.

sentence: Ciwon haila yakan dame ta har ta kasa zuwa aiki na kwana biyu.
translation: Period pain troubles her so badly that she can't get to work for two days.
