sentence: Akuyar makwabcinmu ta shiga gonarmu, ta cinye dukkan ganyen alayyafo.
translation: Our neighbour's goat got into our farm and ate every last spinach leaf.

sentence: Mahaifina ya sayi akuya mai ƙiba a kasuwar Wudil don bikin sallah.
translation: My father bought a fat goat at Wudil market for the Sallah feast.

sentence: Yaron yana kuka domin an yanka akuyar da ya taso da ita.
translation: The boy is crying because they slaughtered the goat he grew up with.

sentence: Likita bai gaya mana jinsin jaririn ba, mun so mu jira ranar haihuwa.
translation: The doctor didn't tell us the baby's sex; we wanted to wait for the birth.

sentence: A asibiti sun tambaye ni shekaruna da jinsi kafin su ba ni kati.
translation: At the hospital they asked my age and sex before giving me a card.

sentence: Ina ganin bai kamata a hana yarinya karatu saboda jinsinta ba.
translation: I don't think a girl should be kept out of school because of her sex.

sentence: Alhakin renon yara yana kan iyaye biyu, ba uwa kaɗai ba.
translation: The responsibility of raising children rests on both parents, not on the mother alone.

sentence: Ya ɗauki alhakin ɓarnar da almajiransa suka yi a kasuwar gari.
translation: He took responsibility for the damage his Qur'anic pupils caused in the town market.

sentence: Har yanzu alhakin ƙarya da na yi wa mahaifina yana damuna.
translation: Even now the guilt of the lie I told my father weighs on me.

sentence: Mun isa Takum da tsakar dare, ruwan sama yana ta sauka.
translation: We reached Takum at midnight with the rain still coming down.

sentence: Kasuwar Takum tana cika da mutane duk ranar Litinin da safe.
translation: Takum market fills up with people every Monday morning.

sentence: Ban taɓa mantuwa da bikin auren da muka yi a Takum ba.
translation: I have never forgotten the wedding celebration we held in Takum.

sentence: Awakin maƙwabcinmu sun tsallake shinge da daddare suka lalata gonar tumatir.
translation: Our neighbour's goats jumped the fence during the night and ruined the tomato plot.

sentence: Malamin ya sa yara su gyara shingen makarantar kafin ruwan sama ya fara.
translation: The teacher had the children repair the school fence before the rains began.

sentence: A ganina shingen katanga ya fi na ƙaya ƙarfi, amma yana da tsada.
translation: In my view a wall fence is stronger than a thorn one, but it costs a lot.

sentence: Yalwa ta dafa tuwon shinkafa da miyar kuka don baƙin da suka zo.
translation: Yalwa cooked rice tuwo with baobab-leaf soup for the guests who arrived.

sentence: Yalwa ce ta fi kowa maki a jarrabawar lissafi a ajinmu bana.
translation: It was Yalwa who scored higher than everyone in our class's maths exam this year.

sentence: Duk lokacin da Yalwa ta yi dariya, sai kowa a gida ya yi murmushi.
translation: Whenever Yalwa laughs, everyone in the house ends up smiling.

sentence: Yaron ya ɗauki banga ya fara buga shi da yatsunsa a gaban gida.
translation: The boy picked up the banga drum and started tapping it with his fingers in front of the house.

sentence: A ranar sallah, mawaƙan ƙauyen suna buga banga har tsakar dare.
translation: On the day of the festival the village musicians played the banga drum until midnight.

sentence: Ƙarar banga tana tuna min da bukukuwan ƙauyenmu lokacin da nake ƙarami.
translation: The sound of the banga drum reminds me of our village festivals when I was small.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta yi mana hani game da yin wasa kusa da rijiya.
translation: My mother forbade us from playing anywhere near the well.

sentence: Gwamnati ta sanya hani kan shigo da shinkafa, sai farashinta ya tashi.
translation: The government placed a ban on rice imports, and its price promptly shot up.

sentence: Duk da haninsu, matasan ƙauyen sun ci gaba da kaɗe-kaɗe da daddare.
translation: Despite their prohibition, the village youths went on drumming through the night.

sentence: Kullum mukan koma gida kafin magariba don kada duhu ya kama mu.
translation: We always head home before the sunset prayer so that darkness doesn't catch us out.

sentence: A watan Ramadan, kowa yana jiran magariba don a karya azumi da dabino.
translation: During Ramadan everyone waits for the sunset prayer so the fast can be broken with dates.

sentence: Ina son lokacin magariba domin sararin sama yana yin ja mai kyau.
translation: I love the hour of the sunset prayer, because the sky turns a beautiful red.

sentence: Mahaifina ya aiko mini da kuɗin makaranta kafin ranar biya ta ƙare.
translation: My father sent me the school fees before the payment deadline ran out.

sentence: Na yi ciniki da mai tumatir har ya rage kuɗin da naira ɗari.
translation: I haggled with the tomato seller until he knocked a hundred naira off the price.

sentence: Kuɗi ba ya sayen lafiya, amma rashinsa yana kawo damuwa mai yawa.
translation: Money does not buy health, but the lack of it brings a great deal of worry.

sentence: Na hau mashin daga kasuwa zuwa gida saboda ruwan sama ya fara.
translation: I took a motorbike from the market home because the rain had started.

sentence: Mashin ɗin niƙa ya tsaya da rana, sai muka koma gida hannu banza.
translation: The grinding machine broke down at midday, so we went home empty-handed.

sentence: Ina tsoron hawan mashin a hanyar Kano tun bayan hatsarin da na gani.
translation: I have been afraid of riding a motorbike on the Kano road ever since the crash I witnessed.

sentence: Da safe mun tarar da maciji a ƙarƙashin tabarma a ɗakin kaya.
translation: In the morning we came upon a snake under the mat in the storeroom.

sentence: Manomi ya kashe maciji da sanda kafin ya ci gaba da noman gonar.
translation: The farmer killed a snake with a stick before carrying on with hoeing the field.

sentence: Ina jin tsoron maciji fiye da kowace dabba, har ma a hoto.
translation: I fear snakes more than any other animal, even in a photograph.

sentence: Malam ya bayyana maʼanar ridda ga ɗalibai a makarantar allo jiya.
translation: The teacher explained the meaning of apostasy to the pupils at the Qurʼanic school yesterday.

sentence: A tarihin Musulunci, yaƙin ridda ya barke bayan rasuwar Annabi.
translation: In Islamic history, the wars of apostasy broke out after the Prophet's death.

sentence: Ya ji tsoro sosai lokacin da aka zarge shi da ridda.
translation: He was gripped by fear when they accused him of apostasy.

sentence: Iyayena sun ƙaura zuwa wani lardi mai nisa a arewacin ƙasar.
translation: My parents moved away to a far-off province in the north of the country.

sentence: Manoma sun kai koke ga hukumar lardi game da ƙarancin taki.
translation: The farmers took their complaint to the provincial authority about the fertiliser shortage.

sentence: A ganina, wannan lardi ya fi kowanne kyau saboda kwanciyar hankalinsa.
translation: To my mind this province beats all the others, because life here is peaceful.

sentence: Kowace Jumaʼa mukan je makabarta don yin adduʼa a kabarin kakana.
translation: Every Friday we go to the cemetery to pray at my grandfather's grave.

sentence: Mutane sun cika makabarta lokacin da aka binne tsohon limamin unguwarmu.
translation: People packed the cemetery when our neighbourhood's old imam was buried.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na wuce makabarta da dare, jikina yakan yi sanyi.
translation: Whenever I pass the cemetery after dark, a chill runs right through me.

sentence: Audu ya kwashe yini yana gyara keken mahaifinsa a ƙarƙashin bishiya.
translation: Audu spent the whole day under the tree mending his father's bicycle.

sentence: Malam ya tambayi Audu me ya sa bai zo makaranta jiya ba.
translation: The teacher asked Audu why he had not come to school yesterday.

sentence: Na yi farin ciki sosai da jin cewa Audu ya ci jarrabawar.
translation: I was overjoyed to hear that Audu had passed the examination.

sentence: A wurin shan shayi, Musa ya buga zi ya lashe wasan.
translation: At the tea stall Musa played a diamond and took the round.

sentence: A daren jiya muna wasan kati, sai Sani ya fitar da zi uku.
translation: Last night while we were playing cards, Sani laid down three diamonds.

sentence: Ban taɓa yin saʼa da zi ba, sai dai da baƙin kati.
translation: I have never had any luck with diamonds, only with the black suits.

sentence: Bayan ya gama cin abinci, sai kakana ya yi hamdala a hankali.
translation: When he had finished eating, my grandfather quietly gave thanks to God.

sentence: Da jin labarin haihuwar, dukan matan sun yi hamdala suka fara waƙa.
translation: On hearing news of the birth, all the women praised God and broke into song.

sentence: Ko a lokacin wahala, ya kamata mutum ya riƙa yin hamdala.
translation: Even in times of hardship, a person ought to keep giving thanks to God.

sentence: Amarya ta gaisa da kishiya cikin ladabi a ranar da ta shigo gidan.
translation: The bride greeted her co-wife respectfully on the day she came into the household.

sentence: Kishiyata takan taimaka mini da dafa abinci lokacin da nake jinya.
translation: My co-wife helps me with the cooking whenever I am unwell.

sentence: A gidanmu, kishiya ba maƙiya ba ce; muna zama lafiya tare.
translation: In our house a co-wife is no enemy; we live together in peace.

sentence: Da rana ta yi zafi, muka yanka kankana muka raba wa yara.
translation: When the afternoon grew hot, we cut a watermelon and shared it out among the children.

sentence: Mai sayar da ʼyaʼyan itace ya ce kankana ta yi tsada bana.
translation: The fruit seller said that watermelon has become expensive this year.

sentence: Babu abin da ya fi kankana mai sanyi daɗi a lokacin bazara.
translation: Nothing tastes better than chilled watermelon during the hot season.

sentence: Shugaban jamhuriya ya sanya hannu kan sabuwar dokar ilimi jiya da yamma.
translation: The president of the republic signed the new education law yesterday evening.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya bayyana yadda ƙasar ta zama jamhuriya bayan mulkin mallaka.
translation: The history teacher explained how the country became a republic after colonial rule.

sentence: Kakana yakan ce jamhuriya ba ta kawo wa talakawa sauƙi ba tukuna.
translation: My grandfather always says the republic has yet to bring ordinary people any relief.

sentence: Kowane mumini yakan tashi da sassafe domin yin sallar asuba.
translation: Every believer gets up before daybreak to perform the dawn prayer.

sentence: Limami ya tunatar da mu cewa mumini ba ya cutar da maƙwabcinsa.
translation: The imam reminded us that a believer does not do harm to his neighbour.

sentence: Na ji daɗi da na ga mumini yana taimaka wa baƙo cikin ruwan sama.
translation: It warmed my heart to see a believer helping a stranger out in the rain.

sentence: Ɗan uwana ya shafe shekaru uku yana kasuwanci a Kwango kafin ya dawo gida.
translation: My brother spent three years trading in Congo before he came back home.

sentence: Mun taru a gidan maƙwabci muka kalli yadda Najeriya ta doke Kwango.
translation: We crowded into the neighbour's house and watched Nigeria beat Congo.

sentence: Ban taɓa zuwa Kwango ba, amma ina son in ga dazuzzukanta.
translation: I have never been to Congo, but I would love to see its forests.

sentence: Amina tana da goyo, don haka ba za ta iya ɗaukar tulun ruwa ba.
translation: Amina has a baby on her back, so she can't carry the water pot.

sentence: Malamar makarantar ta zo aiki da goyo, don ba ta samu mai kulawa ba.
translation: The teacher came to work with her baby on her back, because she found nobody to mind him.

sentence: Wannan goyo ya yi girma sosai, kar ki ƙara ɗaure shi a baya.
translation: This child you carry has got far too big — stop tying him on your back.

sentence: Na sayi mujalla a tashar mota don in rage gajiyar tafiya.
translation: I bought a magazine at the motor park to make the journey less wearying.

sentence: Ina aiki a wata mujalla ta mako-mako, kuma ina rubuta labarin wasanni.
translation: I work at a weekly magazine, and I write the sports stories.

sentence: Ban ji daɗin wannan mujalla ba, domin labaranta duk na siyasa ne.
translation: I didn't enjoy this magazine, because its articles are all about politics.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta dafa hanta da albasa, muka ci ta da shinkafa.
translation: My mother cooked liver with onions, and we ate it with rice.

sentence: Mai suya ya yanka hanta gunduwa-gunduwa, sannan ya barbaɗa mata yaji.
translation: The suya seller cut the liver into chunks, then sprinkled the spice mix over it.

sentence: Likita ya gaya masa cewa shan giya ya lalata masa hanta.
translation: The doctor told him that drinking had ruined his liver.

sentence: Da safe mukan sha koko da kosai kafin mu tafi makaranta.
translation: In the mornings we would have koko porridge and bean cakes before setting off for school.

sentence: Mai koko ta zuba mini cikin ƙwarya, na sha shi tun yana da zafi.
translation: The koko seller poured mine into a calabash, and I drank it while it was still hot.

sentence: Wannan koko ya yi tsami sosai, na zubar da shi na koma kan shayi.
translation: This koko has gone really sour, so I threw it out and had tea instead.

sentence: Kawuna ya dawo daga Habasha makon jiya da buhun kofi mai ƙamshi.
translation: My uncle came back from Ethiopia last week with a sack of fragrant coffee.

sentence: Sahabbai sun yi hijira zuwa Habasha lokacin da aka tsananta musu a Makka.
translation: The Companions migrated to Ethiopia when they were being persecuted in Mecca.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda ƴan wasan Habasha suke gudu ba tare da gajiya ba.
translation: It amazes me how Ethiopian athletes can run and run without tiring.

sentence: Ƙasa ta yi santsi saboda ruwan sama, sai na zame na faɗi warwas.
translation: The ground was slippery from the rain, so I skidded and went down flat on my back.

sentence: Ɗan kokawa ya buga abokin karawarsa har ya faɗi warwas a dandali.
translation: The wrestler threw his opponent so hard the man landed flat on his back in the arena.

sentence: Bayan ya gama aikin gona, ya kwanta warwas a ƙarƙashin bishiya.
translation: When he had finished the farm work, he lay stretched out flat under a tree.

sentence: Gidan nan yana da fasali mai kyau, kowane ɗaki yana da taga.
translation: This house has a fine layout — every single room has a window.

sentence: Injiniya ya sauya fasali sau uku kafin mai gidan ya amince da shi.
translation: The engineer redid the design three times before the owner would agree to it.

sentence: Sabon fasali da jaridar ta ɗauka bai burge ni ba ko kaɗan.
translation: The new format the newspaper has adopted doesn't impress me in the least.

sentence: Kowace safiya ɗalibai kan taru a filin makaranta su ɗaga tuta.
translation: Every morning the pupils gather on the school field to raise the flag.

sentence: Magoya baya sun naɗe kansu da tuta suna rera waƙa a filin wasa.
translation: The fans wrapped themselves in the flag and sang all through the stadium.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ga tuta ina tuna ranar da muka samu ƴanci.
translation: Whenever I see the flag I think back to the day we won our independence.

sentence: Mun shiga safa da safe muka isa Kazaure kafin rana ta yi zafi.
translation: We took the early bus and reached Kazaure before the sun turned fierce.

sentence: Kasuwar Kazaure kan cika da mutane duk ranar Litinin, musamman masu sayar da shanu.
translation: Kazaure market fills with people every Monday, above all the cattle traders.

sentence: Kakana ya girma a Kazaure, yana fatan ya koma can bayan ya yi ritaya.
translation: My grandfather grew up in Kazaure, and he hopes to move back there once he retires.

sentence: Bayan ruwa ya tafasa, sai ka jira sakan talatin kafin ka zuba shayi.
translation: Once the water has boiled, wait thirty seconds before you pour the tea.

sentence: A gasar tseren makaranta, ya doke abokinsa da sakan biyu kacal.
translation: In the school race he beat his friend by just two seconds.

sentence: Yayin da nake jiran sakamakon jarrabawa, kowane sakan sai ka ce awa ɗaya.
translation: While I was waiting for the exam results, every second felt like a whole hour.

sentence: Kada ka zubar da datti a gaban gida, ka kai shi juji.
translation: Don't dump the rubbish in front of the house — take it to the tip.

sentence: Ranar Asabar, matasan unguwarmu sun tara dattin da ke kwance a kasuwa.
translation: On Saturday the young men of our neighbourhood cleared away all the filth lying about the market.

sentence: Dattin da ya cika magudanar ruwa yana ba mu haushi a lokacin damina.
translation: The filth clogging the gutter disgusts us every rainy season.

sentence: Kakata tana zaune a Yamai, muna kai mata ziyara duk lokacin sallah.
translation: My grandmother lives in Niamey, and we go and visit her every Sallah.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan sayo kayan ado a Yamai ya sayar da su a Kano.
translation: My father buys jewellery in Niamey and sells it in Kano.

sentence: Ban taɓa zuwa Yamai ba, amma ina son in ga Kogin Neja da idona.
translation: I have never been to Niamey, but I would love to see the River Niger with my own eyes.

sentence: Ɗan uwana ya yi shekara biyu yana aiki a Ankara, babban birnin Ghana.
translation: My brother has spent two years working in Accra, the capital of Ghana.

sentence: Za mu tashi daga Legas zuwa Ankara da bas, tafiyar kwana biyu ce.
translation: We are travelling from Lagos to Accra by bus; it is a two-day journey.

sentence: Iskar tekun Ankara ta fi ta Kano sanyi, shi ya sa nake son garin.
translation: The sea breeze in Accra is cooler than Kano's, and that is why I love the city.

sentence: Muna sa wa jaki takunkumi kafin mu shiga gona, don kada ya ci hatsi.
translation: We put a muzzle on the donkey before we go into the field so that it cannot eat the grain.

sentence: Ƙasashen Turai sun ƙaƙaba wa gwamnatin ƙasar takunkumin tattalin arziki bayan juyin mulki.
translation: The European countries imposed an economic embargo on the country's government after the coup.

sentence: Takunkumin da aka ƙaƙaba ya sa farashin man fetur ya haura, talakawa suna kuka.
translation: The embargo that was imposed has driven up the price of petrol, and ordinary people are complaining bitterly.

sentence: Bayan ya yi wanka daga janaba, sai ya kama hanyar masallaci don sallar asuba.
translation: After taking the ritual bath he set off for the mosque for the dawn prayer.

sentence: Malamin ya koya mana yadda ake yin wankan janaba a darasin fiƙihu.
translation: The teacher showed us how the ritual bath is performed in our jurisprudence lesson.

sentence: Ya damu sosai da ya tashi da janaba, ruwa kuwa ya ƙare a gida.
translation: He was very distressed to wake up in need of the ritual bath when the water at home had run out.

sentence: Kalamin kakana game da haƙuri yana nan a zuciyata har yau.
translation: My grandfather's words about patience have stayed in my heart to this day.

sentence: Kalami ɗaya daga bakin gwamna a taron ya ɓata wa manoma rai.
translation: A single remark from the governor at the meeting upset the farmers.

sentence: Kada ka furta kalami mai zafi cikin fushi, gobe za ka yi da-na-sani.
translation: Don't utter a harsh word in anger; tomorrow you will regret it.

sentence: Ilimi muhimmi ne, shi ya sa na sayar da gonata don karatun ɗana.
translation: Education matters, and that is why I sold my farm to pay for my son's schooling.

sentence: Gobe muna da muhimmin taro da manoma, kada ka makara ko kaɗan.
translation: Tomorrow we have an important meeting with the farmers — don't be even slightly late.

sentence: Rijistar haihuwa muhimmiyar takarda ce, kada ka bar ta a hannun yara.
translation: A birth certificate is an important document; don't leave it lying around with the children.

sentence: Kakata takan ba mu hikaya a gaban wuta kafin mu kwanta barci.
translation: My grandmother tells us a story by the fire before we go to bed.

sentence: Malamin ya rufe darasi da hikaya game da mutumin da ya ci amana.
translation: The teacher ended the lesson with a tale about a man who betrayed a trust.

sentence: Wannan hikaya ta sa na yi kuka, domin ta tuna mini da rayuwar mahaifina.
translation: That story made me weep, because it reminded me of my father's life.

sentence: Mun gina rumfa a bayan gida don mu huta a lokacin zafi.
translation: We built a shelter behind the house so we could rest during the hot season.

sentence: Mahaifina yana da rumfa a kasuwar Kurmi inda yake sayar da fatu.
translation: My father has a stall in Kurmi market where he sells hides.

sentence: Iska mai ƙarfi ta kwashe rumfar mai shayi, yanzu yana kuka bakin hanya.
translation: A strong wind carried off the tea seller's stall, and now he is weeping by the roadside.

sentence: Muna zaune a wata nahiya da ke nesa da babban birni.
translation: We live in a district a long way out from the city.

sentence: Kowace nahiya a jihar nan tana da asibiti ɗaya kawai.
translation: Every district in this state has just one hospital.

sentence: Jamaʼar wannan nahiya sun yi zanga-zanga saboda rashin ruwan sha.
translation: The people of this district protested because there is no drinking water.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifina yakan saurari tafsiri kafin ya tafi gona.
translation: Every morning my father listens to the tafsir before he heads out to the farm.

sentence: A watan azumi, jamaʼa suna cika masallaci don sauraron tafsiri.
translation: During the fasting month people pack the mosque to hear the tafsir.

sentence: Ban gane tafsiri sosai ba, don haka zan tambayi malam gobe.
translation: I did not really follow the tafsir, so I will ask the teacher tomorrow.

sentence: Kafin mu fara wasa, Musa ya lale kati sau uku.
translation: Before we started the game, Musa shuffled the cards three times.

sentence: Yara suna zaune a ƙarƙashin bishiya suna jiran Sani ya lale kati.
translation: The children are sitting under the tree waiting for Sani to shuffle the cards.

sentence: Ka lale kati sosai don kada wani ya yi zargin magudi.
translation: Shuffle the cards properly so that nobody accuses you of cheating.

sentence: Bayan sallar ishaʼi, kakata takan yi nafila kafin ta kwanta.
translation: After the isha prayer my grandmother prays nafl before she goes to bed.

sentence: Mun isa masallaci da wuri, muka yi nafila kafin a yi kiran sallah.
translation: We got to the mosque early and prayed nafl before the call to prayer went out.

sentence: Ina jin daɗin yin nafila da dare fiye da kowace ibada.
translation: I enjoy praying nafl at night more than any other act of worship.

sentence: Bayan mutuwar mijinta, tana zaman idda a gidan iyayenta.
translation: Since her husband died she has been keeping her iddah at her parents' house.

sentence: Malaman addini sun bayyana cewa idda takan ɗauki wata huɗu da kwana goma.
translation: The clerics explained that the iddah normally lasts four months and ten days.

sentence: Iyalinta suna damuwa domin ta gaji da zaman idda a gida.
translation: Her family is worried, because she has grown weary of sitting out the iddah at home.

sentence: Sarki ya naɗa ɗan uwansa wali a bikin da aka yi jiya.
translation: The emir installed his brother as vizier at the ceremony held yesterday.

sentence: Wali ya zauna a hannun dama na sarki lokacin da baƙi suka shigo.
translation: The vizier sat at the emir's right hand as the guests came in.

sentence: Manoma sun kai ƙara wurin wali kafin su je fadar sarki.
translation: The farmers took their complaint to the vizier before going on to the emir's palace.

sentence: Karen maƙwabcinmu mugu ne, yana korar yara kowace safiya.
translation: Our neighbour's dog is vicious; it chases the children every morning.

sentence: Alƙali ya ce mutumin nan mugu ne, don haka ya yanke masa hukunci.
translation: The judge said this man was wicked, and so passed sentence on him.

sentence: Ban san cewa abokina mugu ne ba har sai da ya ci amanata.
translation: I had no idea my friend was a bad man until he betrayed my trust.

sentence: Mun haye kogi da jirgin ruwa kafin mu isa tsibiri.
translation: We crossed the river by boat before we reached the island.

sentence: Masunta sukan kwana a tsibiri idan kamun kifi ya yi yawa.
translation: The fishermen stay overnight on the island whenever the catch is heavy.

sentence: Ba na son zama a tsibiri saboda babu asibiti ko makaranta.
translation: I would not want to live on an island, since there is neither a hospital nor a school.

sentence: Maroƙi ya buga kolo har sai da mutane suka fara rawa.
translation: The praise-singer beat the kolo drum until people got up and danced.

sentence: Kakana ya koya mini yadda ake buga kolo tun ina ƙarami.
translation: My grandfather taught me how to beat the kolo drum when I was still small.

sentence: Sautin kolo yana ba ni farin ciki fiye da kowace irin ganga.
translation: The sound of the kolo drum delights me more than any other kind of drum.

sentence: Bayan mun ƙidaya kuɗin kasuwa, jimla ta kai naira dubu goma.
translation: After we counted the market takings, the total came to ten thousand naira.

sentence: Malamin lissafi ya nemi mu rubuta jimla a ƙarshen kowane shafi.
translation: The maths teacher asked us to write the total at the bottom of every page.

sentence: Na yi mamaki lokacin da jimla ta wuce kuɗin da nake da su.
translation: I was taken aback when the total came to more than the money I had on me.

sentence: Kakata ba ta cin nama sai ta tabbatar cewa naman halal ne.
translation: My grandmother won't eat meat until she has made sure it was slaughtered halal.

sentence: A kasuwar Kano, dillalai suna rantsuwa cewa ribar da suke samu halal ce.
translation: In the Kano market the traders swear that the profit they make is lawful.

sentence: Na gwammace ƙaramin albashi na halal da dukiyar da aka sata.
translation: I would rather have a small lawful wage than wealth somebody has stolen.

sentence: Da aka buga tambari a fadar sarki, jama'a suka taru a ƙofar gida.
translation: When the royal drum was beaten at the emir's palace, the crowd gathered at the gate.

sentence: Duk shekara muna zuwa Zariya don mu ji tambari a ranar Sallah.
translation: Every year we travel to Zaria to hear the royal drum on the day of Sallah.

sentence: Amon tambari yana sa gashin jikina ya tashi a duk Sallah.
translation: The boom of the royal drum makes my hair stand on end every Sallah.

sentence: Likita ya ce hayaƙin taba ya lalata huhun kawuna a hankali.
translation: The doctor said cigarette smoke had slowly ruined my uncle's lungs.

sentence: Malamin ilmin halitta ya zana huhu a allo, yana bayanin numfashi.
translation: The biology teacher drew a lung on the board while he explained breathing.

sentence: Bayan na yi gudu zuwa makaranta, huhuna ya kusa fashewa da gajiya.
translation: After I ran all the way to school my lungs were ready to burst.

sentence: Alƙalin Shari'a ya umarci direban ya biya diyya ga iyalin marigayin.
translation: The Sharia judge ordered the driver to pay blood money to the dead man's family.

sentence: Dattawan ƙauye sun sayar da shanu don su biya diyyar da kotu ta yanke.
translation: The village elders sold cattle to pay the blood money the court had set.

sentence: Iyayen yaron sun ƙi karɓar diyya, domin kuɗi ba zai maido da ransa ba.
translation: The boy's parents refused the blood money, because money will not bring his life back.

sentence: Ban sayar da gonar ba don son rai, larura ce ta tilasta mini.
translation: I didn't sell the farm because I wanted to; it was necessity that forced me.

sentence: Direban ya ce ba ya tuƙi da dare sai in akwai larura.
translation: The driver said he never drives at night unless there is an emergency.

sentence: A wurina, mota larura ce ga likitar ƙauye, ba wai alfarma ba.
translation: To my mind a car is a necessity for a village doctor, not a luxury.

sentence: Mun sauka a Damagaram bayan tafiya ta kwana biyu daga Kano.
translation: We stopped in Zinder after a two-day journey from Kano.

sentence: 'Yan kasuwa daga Damagaram sukan kawo mana kayan lambu a kasuwar Jumma'a.
translation: Traders from Zinder bring us vegetables to the Friday market.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin bikin Sallah kamar wanda na gani a Damagaram ba.
translation: I have never seen a Sallah festival like the one I saw in Zinder.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan zuba kafur a ruwan wanka don kwantar da ƙaiƙayi.
translation: My mother puts camphor in the bathwater to calm the itching.

sentence: A kasuwar Kurmi, mai ganye ya auna mini kafur kaɗan cikin takarda.
translation: At Kurmi market the herb seller weighed me out a little camphor in a paper twist.

sentence: Ƙamshin kafur yana tunatar da ni jana'izar kakata a Sakkwato.
translation: The smell of camphor reminds me of my grandmother's funeral in Sokoto.

sentence: Igiyar rijiya ta tsinke da rana, sai muka nemi sabuwa a kasuwa.
translation: The well rope snapped in the middle of the day, so we went to the market for a new one.

sentence: Malam ya ɗaure buhun gyaɗa da igiya kafin a ɗora shi a mota.
translation: The man tied the sack of groundnuts with rope before it was loaded onto the lorry.

sentence: Ka riƙe igiyar nan sosai, don kada ragon ya sake ɓacewa.
translation: Hold this rope tight, so the ram doesn't go missing again.

sentence: Ina tashi kafin alfijir kowace rana don in yi alwala cikin nutsuwa.
translation: I get up before dawn every day so I can wash for prayer unhurried.

sentence: Direbobin Sokoto sukan tashi da alfijir don su guji zafin rana.
translation: The Sokoto drivers set out at dawn to escape the heat of the day.

sentence: Mun zauna muna addu'a har lokacin alfijir ya yi, sannan zazzaɓin ya sauka.
translation: We sat there praying until dawn came, and then the fever broke.

sentence: Baba ya kafe ƙusa a bango don ya rataya hoton kakanmu.
translation: Father drove a nail into the wall so he could hang our grandfather's photograph.

sentence: Ma'aikatan sun kafe sandunan tanti a ƙasa kafin guguwar yamma ta iso.
translation: The workers fixed the tent poles firmly in the ground before the evening storm arrived.

sentence: Ka kafe ƙugiyar ƙofa da kyau, ina tsoron kada barayi su shigo da dare.
translation: Fasten the door hook properly; I'm afraid thieves may get in during the night.

sentence: Kakana yakan ce mini cewa jahili ba ya sanin darajar littafi.
translation: My grandfather always tells me that an unlettered man has no idea what a book is worth.

sentence: Ya shiga makarantar dare don kada mutane su ci gaba da kiransa jahili.
translation: He enrolled in the evening literacy class so that people would stop calling him an illiterate.

sentence: Ya ɓata mini rai lokacin da ya kira ni jahili a gaban abokaina.
translation: It cut me deeply when he called me an ignoramus in front of my friends.

sentence: A watan Ramalan, mahaifiyata takan tashi da ƙarfe huɗu ta dafa koko.
translation: During Ramadan my mother gets up at four in the morning to cook the millet gruel.

sentence: Kasuwa takan cika da mutane kafin Ramalan, don kowa yana sayen dabino.
translation: The market is packed in the days before Ramadan, because everybody is buying dates.

sentence: Ina jin daɗin Ramalan domin duk iyalina sukan haɗu wajen buɗa baki.
translation: I love Ramadan because my whole family gathers together to break the fast.

sentence: Ba gaira ba dalili, ƙaramin yaronmu ya fara kuka a tsakiyar dare.
translation: For no reason whatsoever, our little boy started crying in the middle of the night.

sentence: Shugaba ya kore shi daga aiki ba gaira ba dalili bayan shekaru goma.
translation: The boss threw him out of the job without the slightest reason, after ten years there.

sentence: Na ji haushi saboda ta daina yi mini magana ba gaira ba dalili.
translation: It angers me that she stopped speaking to me without any reason at all.

sentence: Manoman Katsina sun fara girbin auduga bayan ruwan sama ya daina sauka.
translation: The Katsina farmers started the cotton harvest once the rains had stopped falling.

sentence: Maʼaikaciyar asibiti ta tsabtace raunin ɗana da auduga kafin ta daure shi.
translation: The nurse cleaned my son's wound with cotton wool before she bandaged it.

sentence: Na fi son rigar auduga a lokacin rani, domin ba ta ɗaukar zafi.
translation: I prefer a cotton gown in the hot season, because it does not hold the heat.

sentence: Yaran ƙauyen sukan yi rige har bakin kogi kowace safiya.
translation: The village children race each other all the way down to the river every morning.

sentence: Direbobin manyan motoci sukan yi rige a hanya, har su jawo haɗari.
translation: Lorry drivers race one another on the highway until they end up causing a crash.

sentence: Rige da abokina a karatu ya sa na tashi da ƙarfe biyar.
translation: Competing with my friend over our schoolwork is what got me up at five o'clock.

sentence: Mun isa Kano cikin salama, duk da ruwan saman da ya kama mu.
translation: We got to Kano safe and sound, despite the rain that caught us on the way.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan yi mini adduʼar salama duk lokacin da zan yi tafiya.
translation: My mother prays for my safety every single time I am about to travel.

sentence: Bayan shekaru na rikici, mutanen ƙauyen suna neman salama fiye da komai.
translation: After years of conflict, the villagers want peace and safety more than anything else.

sentence: Da gimbiya ta shiga zauren biki, sai kowa ya tashi tsaye.
translation: When the princess walked into the wedding hall, everyone rose to their feet.

sentence: Kakata takan ba mu labarin gimbiya da ta ƙi auren sarkin ƙasar waje.
translation: My grandmother tells us the story of the princess who refused to marry a foreign king.

sentence: Ita ba gimbiya ba ce, amma tana tafiya kamar ƴar sarki a kasuwa.
translation: She is no princess, yet she walks through the market like an emir's daughter.

sentence: Kakana yakan gyara mini lafazi idan na yi karatun Alƙurʼani da yamma.
translation: My grandfather corrects my pronunciation whenever I recite the Qur'an in the evening.

sentence: A gasar karatun Alƙurʼani, alƙalai suna ba da maki bisa lafazi da sauti.
translation: In the Qur'an recitation contest, the judges award marks for pronunciation and for voice.

sentence: Ina shaʼawar lafazi mai kyau, shi ya sa nake sauraron labaran rediyo.
translation: I admire clear, well-formed speech, and that is why I listen to the radio news.

sentence: Wani fasinja ya manta jakarsa a cikin motar, direba ya juyo da ita.
translation: A passenger left his bag behind in the bus, and the driver turned back with it.

sentence: Direba ya ƙi tashi daga tashar har sai ya sami fasinja na ƙarshe.
translation: The driver refused to pull out of the motor park until he had his last passenger.

sentence: Ba na son zama kusa da fasinja mai hayaniya a doguwar tafiya.
translation: I hate having to sit next to a noisy passenger on a long journey.

sentence: A ƙauyenmu, ana yin bori a filin sarki bayan an gama girbi.
translation: In our village the bori rite is performed in the chief's square once the harvest is in.

sentence: Masu kiɗan bori sun buga ganga har mutane suka cika filin da dare.
translation: The bori drummers played on until the crowd had filled the square that night.

sentence: Kakana bai yarda da bori ba, amma yana girmama tsofaffin alʼadunmu.
translation: My grandfather puts no faith in bori, but he still respects our old customs.

sentence: Kakana yakan ajiye taba a cikin battarsa ta fata kowace rana.
translation: My grandfather keeps his tobacco in his leather pouch every single day.

sentence: Wani dattijo ya sayar mini da batta a kasuwar Kano jiya.
translation: An old man sold me a leather pouch at the Kano market yesterday.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin batta mai kyau kamar wadda maƙwabcina ya saya ba.
translation: I have never seen a pouch as fine as the one my neighbour bought.

sentence: Babbar mota ta ɗauko ton ɗaya na shinkafa daga Kano zuwa Kaduna.
translation: A big lorry brought a ton of rice from Kano down to Kaduna.

sentence: Manoman ƙauyenmu sun girbe fiye da ton ɗaya na gyaɗa bana.
translation: The farmers in our village harvested more than a ton of groundnuts this year.

sentence: Na yi mamaki lokacin da suka ce jirgin ƙasa ya ɗauki ton ɗaya kawai.
translation: I was astonished when they said the train had carried only one ton.

sentence: Malamin ya nuna mana sigar aikatau a kan allo kafin mu fara rubutu.
translation: The teacher showed us the verb form on the board before we began writing.

sentence: Sigar takardar neman aiki ta canja, don haka na sake rubuta komai.
translation: The format of the job application has changed, so I had to write the whole thing again.

sentence: Ina son sigar wannan ginin, ya bambanta da sauran gidajen unguwarmu.
translation: I like the shape of this building; it is unlike the other houses in our neighbourhood.

sentence: Kakata takan karanta sura ɗaya bayan sallar magariba kowace yamma.
translation: My grandmother reads one sura after the sunset prayer every evening.

sentence: A watan Ramadan limaminmu yakan karanta doguwar sura a sallar tarawihi.
translation: During Ramadan our imam recites a long sura at the tarawih prayer.

sentence: Ban iya haddar wannan sura ba tukuna, kuma malam zai tambaye ni gobe.
translation: I still cannot recite this sura by heart, and the teacher will test me tomorrow.

sentence: Mun wuce wani tsohon kufai a hanyar zuwa ƙauyen kakana.
translation: We passed the ruins of an old abandoned town on the road to my grandfather's village.

sentence: Manoma sun bar ƙauyen saboda ambaliya, yanzu wurin ya zama kufai.
translation: The farmers left the village because of the flood, and now the place is a ruin.

sentence: Ganin kufai na gidan kakanninmu yakan sa ni baƙin ciki.
translation: Seeing the ruins of our grandparents' house always makes me sad.

sentence: Yaron ya kama ragamar jaki ya kai shi rijiyar ƙauye da safe.
translation: The boy took hold of the donkey's halter and led it to the village well in the morning.

sentence: Ragamar doki ta tsinke a kasuwa, sai dokin ya gudu cikin taro.
translation: The horse's halter snapped in the market, and the horse bolted into the crowd.

sentence: Kada ka saki ragama, in ba haka ba shanun za su shiga gonar.
translation: Don't let go of the halter, or the cattle will get into the farm.

sentence: Dokta Aisha za ta gabatar da bincikenta a jamiʼar Bayero gobe.
translation: Dr Aisha will present her research at Bayero University tomorrow.

sentence: Ɗalibai suna jiran Dokta Musa a ƙofar ofishinsa tun da sassafe.
translation: The students have been waiting for Dr Musa at his office door since early morning.

sentence: Bayan shekaru bakwai na karatu, yanzu kowa yana kiransa Dokta.
translation: After seven years of study, everyone now calls him Doctor.

sentence: Ƙaramin yaron yana da makero a kansa, don haka mahaifiyarsa ta aske gashinsa.
translation: The little boy has ringworm on his head, so his mother shaved off his hair.

sentence: Likita ya ce makero yana yaɗuwa cikin sauƙi idan yara suna raba hula.
translation: The doctor said ringworm spreads easily when children share caps.

sentence: Ina jin kunyar cire hula a makaranta tun da makero bai warke ba.
translation: I am ashamed to take my cap off at school because the ringworm has not healed.

sentence: Almajiri ya zo ƙofarmu da ƙwarya yana neman abinci da rana.
translation: An almajiri came to our door with his bowl at midday asking for food.

sentence: Malamin ya aiki almajiri ya kawo ruwan sha daga rijiyar unguwar.
translation: The Quranic teacher sent a pupil to fetch drinking water from the neighbourhood well.

sentence: Ina tausayin kowane almajiri da nake gani yana kwana a kasuwa.
translation: I pity every almajiri I see sleeping out in the market.

sentence: Wani attajiri ya sayi duk shinkafar da mahaifina ya kawo kasuwa.
translation: A wealthy man bought all the rice my father had brought to the market.

sentence: Ya yi shekaru ashirin yana sanaʼa kafin ya zama attajiri a Kano.
translation: He worked at his trade for twenty years before he became a rich man in Kano.

sentence: Ba kowane attajiri ne yake taimakon talakawan unguwarsa ba, abin takaici ne.
translation: Not every rich man helps the poor of his own neighbourhood, and that is a shame.

sentence: A ranar Sallah, galadima ya hau doki a hannun daman sarki.
translation: On Sallah day the galadima rode on horseback at the emir's right hand.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan kai ƙarar makwabtansa wurin galadima maimakon ya je kotu.
translation: My father takes his quarrels with the neighbours to the galadima instead of going to court.

sentence: Ba na jin galadima zai amince da shirin da ʼyan kasuwa suka kawo.
translation: I don't think the galadima will approve the plan the traders have brought.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifiyata takan share farfajiya da tsintsiya kafin mu farka.
translation: Every morning my mother sweeps the compound with a broom before we wake up.

sentence: Zan sayi sabuwar tsintsiya a kasuwa saboda tsohuwar tamu ta karye jiya.
translation: I'll buy a new broom at the market, because our old one broke yesterday.

sentence: Yara sun ɓoye tsintsiya don kada a sa su share ajin.
translation: The children hid the broom so nobody would make them sweep the classroom.

sentence: Malamin yana koyar da tauhidi kowace Asabar a ƙarƙashin bishiyar masallaci.
translation: The teacher teaches tawhid every Saturday under the tree in the mosque yard.

sentence: A makarantar allo mun haddace tauhidi tun kafin mu iya rubutu.
translation: At Qur'anic school we had memorised tawhid before we could even write.

sentence: Ban fahimci tauhidi sosai ba tukuna, amma ina karatu kowane dare.
translation: I still don't properly understand tawhid, but I study it every night.

sentence: Yaron ya yi sujjada mai tsawo har limamin ya jira shi.
translation: The boy's prostration went on so long that the imam had to wait for him.

sentence: Malam zai koya muku yadda ake yin sujjada kafin sallar magariba.
translation: The teacher will show you how the prostration is done before the maghrib prayer.

sentence: Cikin sujjada kaɗai nake samun natsuwa bayan duk damuwar yini.
translation: It is only in prostration that I find any calm after the whole day's worries.

sentence: Gwamnati za ta kafa kwamiti domin yin bahasi kan asarar kuɗin makarantar.
translation: The government will set up a committee to hold an inquiry into the school's missing money.

sentence: Bayan dogon bahasi tsakanin malamai, sai suka amince da shawarar ɗalibin.
translation: After a long debate among the teachers, they came round to the student's suggestion.

sentence: Wannan bahasi bai gamsar da iyayen ɗaliban ba ko kaɗan.
translation: This inquiry did not satisfy the students' parents in the slightest.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan gyara katangar gidanmu da tubali duk bayan damina.
translation: My father repairs our compound wall with bricks after every rainy season.

sentence: Masu ginin suna jera tubali a gefen hanya suna jiran motar siminti.
translation: The builders are stacking bricks by the roadside while they wait for the cement lorry.

sentence: Ruwan sama ya narkar da tubali kafin mu ɗora rufin, aikinmu ya ɓaci.
translation: The rain dissolved the bricks before we got the roof on, and our work was ruined.

sentence: Yayata takan yanke min farce duk Jumaʼa kafin mu tafi wurin kakarmu.
translation: My older sister cuts my fingernails every Friday before we go to our grandmother's.

sentence: Likita ya ce farce mai tsawo yana ɗauke da ƙwayoyin cuta.
translation: The doctor said that long fingernails carry germs.

sentence: Na karya farce yayin da nake ɗaga buhun shinkafa, har yanzu yana ciwo.
translation: I broke a fingernail while lifting the sack of rice, and it still hurts.

sentence: Kakana ya bar wasiyya cewa a raba gonarsa tsakanin ʼyaʼyansa huɗu.
translation: My grandfather left a will saying his farm should be divided among his four children.

sentence: Alƙali zai karanta wasiyya a gaban dangi duka ranar Talata mai zuwa.
translation: The judge will read the will in front of the whole family next Tuesday.

sentence: Ba tare da wasiyya ba, ʼyanʼuwa sukan yi faɗa kan gadon mamaci.
translation: Without a will, siblings usually end up quarrelling over the dead man's inheritance.

sentence: Nakan bi turba mai kunci zuwa gonarmu kafin rana ta yi zafi.
translation: I take the narrow path down to our farm before the sun gets hot.

sentence: Ruwan sama ya lalata turba, don haka babu motar da ta shiga ƙauyen.
translation: The rain wrecked the track, so no vehicle managed to get into the village.

sentence: Ina son turba da ke ratsa gonaki fiye da babbar hanyar mota.
translation: I like the path that cuts through the farms better than the main motor road.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya ce Gobir tana daga cikin ƙasashen Hausa bakwai na asali.
translation: The history teacher said Gobir is one of the seven original Hausa states.

sentence: Muna kan hanyar zuwa bikin naɗin Sarkin Gobir sai motarmu ta lalace.
translation: We were on our way to the turbaning of the Emir of Gobir when our car broke down.

sentence: Kakana yakan yi fahariya da cewa kakanninmu mayaƙan Gobir ne a zamanin baya.
translation: My grandfather likes to boast that our forefathers were the warriors of Gobir in the old days.

sentence: Duk lokacin da wuta ta tafi, ƙanena yakan yi raki ya ƙi fita waje.
translation: Whenever the power goes out, my little brother turns coward and refuses to step outside.

sentence: Malamin ya ce raki ne ya hana ni yin tambaya a gaban ajin.
translation: The teacher said it was cowardice that stopped me from asking a question in front of the class.

sentence: Ba na son raki, gara ka faɗi gaskiya ko da za ka sha wahala.
translation: I have no time for cowardice; better to tell the truth even if it costs you.

sentence: Kawuna ya kwashe shekaru bakwai yana karatu a Misira, yanzu ya dawo Kano.
translation: My uncle spent seven years studying in Egypt, and now he has come back to Kano.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan sayo tufafi daga Misira ya kawo kasuwar Kurmi kowace shekara.
translation: My father buys clothes in Egypt every year and brings them to Kurmi market.

sentence: Ban taɓa zuwa Misira ba, amma ina fatan in ziyarci tsofaffin gine-ginenta wata rana.
translation: I have never been to Egypt, but I hope to visit its ancient buildings one day.

sentence: Kamin mu fita zuwa gona, mahaifiyata takan dafa koko da ƙosai.
translation: Before we set out for the farm, my mother usually makes koko and bean cakes.

sentence: Direban bai tashi daga tasha ba kamin motar ta cika da fasinjoji.
translation: The driver would not leave the station before the vehicle had filled up with passengers.

sentence: Ina tsoron kada damina ta shigo kamin mu gama rufe ɗakin.
translation: I am afraid the rains will arrive before we finish putting the roof on the room.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta dafa miyar kabewa da nama, sai muka ci ta da tuwo.
translation: My mother cooked pumpkin stew with meat, and then we ate it with tuwo.

sentence: A kasuwar Dawanau, mata suna sayar da kabewa mai girma kan naira ɗari biyar.
translation: At Dawanau market the women sell big pumpkins for five hundred naira each.

sentence: Ba na son kabewa sam, amma ƙanwata takan ce ita ce mafi daɗi.
translation: I don't like pumpkin at all, but my younger sister insists it is the tastiest thing there is.

sentence: A watan Muharram kakana yakan yi azumi, yana cewa ladansa yana da yawa.
translation: In the month of Muharram my grandfather fasts, saying the reward for it is great.

sentence: Liman ya tunatar da mu cewa Ashura tana zuwa goma ga watan Muharram.
translation: The imam reminded us that Ashura falls on the tenth of Muharram.

sentence: Watan Muharram ne ke buɗe sabuwar shekarar musulunci, don haka muna girmama shi.
translation: Muharram is the month that opens the new Islamic year, which is why we hold it in such regard.

sentence: Bayan girbi, hatsi yakan yi rahusa a kasuwarmu, sai mu sayi buhu biyu.
translation: After the harvest grain goes cheap in our market, so we buy two sacks of it.

sentence: Ta zaɓi wannan kanti saboda kayansa suna da rahusa, ko da yana da nisa.
translation: She chose that shop because its goods are cheap, even though it is a long walk away.

sentence: Farashin wayar ya yi rahusa har na ji tsoro, ina ganin jabu ce.
translation: The phone was so cheap it made me uneasy; I think the thing is a fake.

sentence: Mafarauci ya cika bindigarsa da harsashi, sannan ya nufi dajin da sassafe.
translation: The hunter loaded his gun with bullets and then headed into the bush at first light.

sentence: Gwamna ya kafa harsashin ginin sabon asibiti a gaban mutanen garin duka.
translation: The governor laid the foundation stone of the new hospital in front of the whole town.

sentence: Harsashi ɗaya kaɗai ya isa ya kawo baƙin ciki ga iyali gaba ɗaya.
translation: A single bullet is enough to bring grief to an entire family.

sentence: Motarmu ta lalace a Maru, sai muka kwana a masaukin baƙi.
translation: Our car broke down in Maru, so we spent the night at a guesthouse.

sentence: Abokina yana koyar da lissafi a wata makarantar sakandare da ke Maru.
translation: My friend teaches mathematics at a secondary school in Maru.

sentence: Kasuwar Maru takan cika da shanu da awaki, ina son hayaniyarta ƙwarai.
translation: Maru market fills up with cattle and goats, and I love the noise of the place.

sentence: Kakata takan ba mu labarin aljani da yake zaune ƙarƙashin babbar bishiyar.
translation: My grandmother used to tell us the story of a jinn that lived under the big tree.

sentence: Mutanen ƙauyen sun yi imani cewa aljani ne ke hana ruwan rijiyar fitowa.
translation: The villagers believe it is a jinn that is keeping the water from rising in the well.

sentence: Ban yarda da maganar aljani ba; ina ganin ɓarawo ne ya ɗauki kuɗin.
translation: I don't believe this talk of a jinn; I reckon it was a thief who took the money.

sentence: Mahawara ta ɓarke tsakanin ni da ƙanena kan wa zai wanke tukwane.
translation: An argument broke out between me and my younger brother over who would wash the pots.

sentence: Ɗalibai sun yi mahawara mai zafi kan ko ya kamata a haramta shan taba.
translation: The students held a heated debate on whether smoking ought to be banned.

sentence: Ban ji daɗin yadda mahawara ta gudana ba, kowa yana ihu, babu mai sauraro.
translation: I did not like the way the discussion went: everyone was shouting and nobody was listening.

sentence: Kakana yakan ba mu labarin mujaddadi duk daren Juma'a a gidan ƙauye.
translation: My grandfather tells us the story of the great reformer every Thursday night at the village house.

sentence: Malamin ya ce Shehu Usman ɗan Fodiyo mujaddadi ne a ƙarninsa.
translation: The teacher said that Shehu Usman dan Fodio was a religious reformer in his own century.

sentence: Ba kowane malami ne mujaddadi ba, ko da yana da mabiya dubbai.
translation: Not every preacher is a reformer, even if he has thousands of followers.

sentence: Kowace Talata mahaifiyata takan sayi auduga mai arha a kasuwar Funtuwa.
translation: Every Tuesday my mother buys cheap cotton at the market in Funtua.

sentence: Motarmu ta lalace a hanya kafin mu isa Funtuwa da tsakar dare.
translation: Our car broke down on the road before we reached Funtua at midnight.

sentence: Na fi son zama a Funtuwa fiye da Kaduna; mutanenta ba sa gaggawa.
translation: I would rather live in Funtua than in Kaduna; its people are never in a hurry.

sentence: A gidanmu, cin nama kowace rana alatu ne, ba al'ada ba.
translation: In our house, eating meat every single day is a luxury, not a habit.

sentence: Tun da ya sami aiki a banki, sai ya fara sayen kayan alatu.
translation: Ever since he got a job at the bank, he has started buying luxury goods.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan ce duk wani alatu yana kawo bashi a ƙarshe.
translation: My father always says that every luxury ends up bringing debt with it.

sentence: Kafin gari ya waye, kakata ta hura wuta a murhu, ta dafa koko.
translation: Before daybreak my grandmother blew the fire alive in the hearth and cooked porridge.

sentence: Mata sun zauna kewaye da murhu suna soya kosai har dare ya yi.
translation: The women sat around the hearth frying bean cakes until night had fallen.

sentence: Abincin murhu ya fi na gas daɗi, ko da yana ɗaukar lokaci.
translation: Food cooked over the hearth stones tastes better than gas-cooked food, even if it takes longer.

sentence: Mun sayi buhun dabino daga Barno, ya ishe mu duk watan azumi.
translation: We bought a sack of dates from Borno, and it lasted us the whole of Ramadan.

sentence: Yayana yana koyarwa a wata makaranta a Barno tun bara.
translation: My elder brother has been teaching at a school in Borno since last year.

sentence: Ban taɓa zuwa Barno ba, amma ina fatan in ga Tafkin Chadi wata rana.
translation: I have never been to Borno, but I hope to see Lake Chad there one day.

sentence: Ɗan uwana kurma ne, don haka muka koyi harshen kurame tun muna yara.
translation: My brother is deaf, so we learned sign language back when we were children.

sentence: A wurin aiki muna rubuta wa abokinmu kurma saƙo a takarda.
translation: At work we write our deaf colleague messages down on paper.

sentence: Kurma ba wawa ba ne; sai ka ba shi lokaci ya fahimce ka.
translation: A deaf person is not a fool; you simply have to give him time to understand you.

sentence: Oga ya ce mu gama rahoton kafin ya dawo daga Legas.
translation: The boss told us to finish the report before he gets back from Lagos.

sentence: Direban tasi ya kira ni oga don ya ƙara kuɗin mota.
translation: The taxi driver called me boss just so he could raise the fare.

sentence: Ba na son oga da yake tsawa a gaban duk ma'aikatansa.
translation: I cannot stand a boss who shouts at you in front of all his staff.

sentence: Mahayin ya ja linzami, sai dokin ya tsaya kusa da rijiya.
translation: The rider pulled on the bridle and the horse stopped beside the well.

sentence: A ranar Sallah, mun goge sirdi da linzami kafin hawan gari.
translation: On Sallah day we polished the saddle and the bridle before the durbar ride.

sentence: Maɗinkin ya ɗauki mako guda yana ɗinka linzami a wuyar sabuwar rigata.
translation: The tailor spent a whole week stitching the triangular embroidery at the neck of my new gown.

sentence: Kakata ta buɗe ƙofa tana cewa marhabin, ku shigo ku huta.
translation: My grandmother opened the door saying, welcome, come in and rest.

sentence: Marhabin da zuwa! Mun daɗe muna jiran ku tun bayan sallar magariba.
translation: Welcome! We have been waiting for you ever since the sunset prayer.

sentence: A garinmu, ana ce wa baƙo marhabin ko da ba a san shi ba.
translation: In our town a stranger is told welcome even when nobody there knows him.

sentence: Ɗan sanda ya tsayar da mu, ya nemi mahaifina ya nuna lasisi.
translation: A policeman stopped us and asked my father to show his driving licence.

sentence: Ba za a bar ka ka buɗe shago ba sai ka biya kuɗin lasisi.
translation: They will not let you open a shop until you have paid the licence fee.

sentence: Na koyi tuƙi tun ina ƙarami, amma har yanzu ban sami lasisi ba.
translation: I learned to drive when I was still a boy, but I still have no licence.

sentence: Baffa ya kawo mana buhun gero daga gona jiya, mahaifiyata ta yi godiya.
translation: Uncle brought us a sack of millet from the farm yesterday, and my mother thanked him.

sentence: Baffana ne ya biya kuɗin makarantar ƙanena bayan mahaifinmu ya rasu.
translation: It was my paternal uncle who paid my younger brother's school fees after our father died.

sentence: Ina son baffana domin yakan ba ni shawara duk lokacin da na shiga matsala.
translation: I love my paternal uncle, because he gives me advice whenever I land in trouble.

sentence: Ambaliyar ruwa ta shiga gidanmu, sai muka kwana a makarantar firamare.
translation: The flood water got into our house, so we spent the night at the primary school.

sentence: Manoman ƙauyen sun rasa gonakinsu bayan ambaliya ta lalata shinkafar da suka shuka.
translation: The village farmers lost their fields after the flood destroyed the rice they had planted.

sentence: Ina tsoron ambaliya a duk shekara, domin gidanmu yana gefen kogi.
translation: I dread the flooding every single year, because our house stands right beside the river.

sentence: Malamin makaranta ya nuna mana inda Sham take a taswirar duniya.
translation: The schoolteacher showed us where Syria lies on the map of the world.

sentence: Kakana ya yi shekara uku yana karatun Larabci a ƙasar Sham.
translation: My grandfather spent three years studying Arabic in Syria.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ji labarin yaƙin Sham a rediyo, zuciyata takan yi nauyi.
translation: Whenever I hear news of the war in Syria on the radio, my heart grows heavy.

sentence: Kawu ya zo da naman rago ranar Sallah, muka gasa shi tare.
translation: Uncle turned up with mutton on Sallah day, and we grilled it together.

sentence: Na tafi Kaduna domin in taimaka wa kawuna a shagon kayan gini.
translation: I travelled to Kaduna to help my maternal uncle in his building-materials shop.

sentence: Kawuna ne kaɗai ke tunawa da ranar haihuwata, hakan yakan faranta min rai.
translation: My maternal uncle is the only one who remembers my birthday, and that always lifts my spirits.

sentence: Sadau ta ci jarrabawar shiga kwaleji, saboda haka mahaifinta ya kashe rago.
translation: Sadau passed the college entrance exam, so her father slaughtered a ram.

sentence: Kowace safiya Sadau takan tafi kasuwa ta sayo wa kakarta kayan miya.
translation: Every morning Sadau goes to the market to buy soup ingredients for her grandmother.

sentence: Har yanzu ina tunawa da waƙar da Sadau ta rera a bikin ƙawarta.
translation: I still remember the song Sadau sang at her friend's wedding.

sentence: Mahaifiyata tana dafa miyar lalo da kifi, ƙamshinta ya cika gidan duka.
translation: My mother is cooking jute-leaf soup with fish, and the smell has filled the whole house.

sentence: Mata suna sayar da lalo bushasshe a kasuwar Dala duk ranar Litinin.
translation: Women sell dried jute leaves at Dala market every Monday.

sentence: Ban taɓa son miyar lalo ba tun ina yaro, amma yau na gama farantina.
translation: I never liked jute soup as a child, but today I finished my whole plate.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan tashe mu da ƙarfe uku don mu ci sahur tare.
translation: My mother wakes us at three in the morning so that we can eat suhur together.

sentence: Bayan mun gama sahur, sai muka zauna muna jiran sallar asuba a masallaci.
translation: Once we had finished suhur, we sat waiting for the dawn prayer at the mosque.

sentence: Na rasa sahur saboda barci, don haka azumin yau ya yi mini wuya.
translation: I missed suhur because I overslept, so today's fast has been hard on me.

sentence: Ministan harkokin waje ya ce diflomasiyya ce kaɗai za ta kawo ƙarshen yaƙin.
translation: The foreign minister said that only diplomacy will bring the war to an end.

sentence: Ƙanwata tana karatun diflomasiyya, tana burin zama jakadar Najeriya a Masar.
translation: My younger sister is studying diplomacy; she hopes to become Nigeria's ambassador in Egypt.

sentence: A ganina, diflomasiyya ta fi faɗa amfani wajen warware rikicin manoma da makiyaya.
translation: To my mind, diplomacy works better than fighting for settling disputes between farmers and herders.

sentence: Na saya wa yara lemo mai sanyi bayan sun dawo daga makaranta.
translation: I bought the children a cold soft drink after they got back from school.

sentence: A kasuwar Wudil ana sayar da lemo goma kan naira ɗari biyu.
translation: At Wudil market they sell ten oranges for two hundred naira.

sentence: Lemo ɗin da na sha jiya ya yi tsami, har na zubar da shi.
translation: The orange drink I had yesterday was so sour that I ended up pouring it away.

sentence: Ban sami izni daga shugaban makaranta ba, don haka ban halarci wasan ba.
translation: I did not get permission from the headmaster, so I missed the match.

sentence: Yaron ya nemi izni a wurin mahaifinsa kafin ya tafi biki a Kaduna.
translation: The boy asked his father's permission before going off to a wedding in Kaduna.

sentence: Kada ka shiga ɗakina ba tare da izni ba, hakan yana ɓata mini rai.
translation: Don't come into my room without permission; it really upsets me.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan tashe ni da asubahi domin mu tafi masallaci tare.
translation: My father wakes me at dawn so that we can walk to the mosque together.

sentence: Ladan ya yi kiran asubahi, sai duk unguwar ta farka daga barci.
translation: The muezzin gave the call for the dawn prayer, and the whole neighbourhood woke up.

sentence: Sanyin damina yana da wuya, amma natsuwar sallar asubahi tana faranta mini rai.
translation: The rainy-season cold is hard to bear, but the stillness of the dawn prayer lifts my heart.

sentence: Kakana yana kamun kifi a Kogin Binuwai tun kafin a haifi mahaifina.
translation: My grandfather has been fishing in the Benue River since before my father was born.

sentence: Manoman Jihar Binuwai sun kai buhunan doya kasuwar Makurdi da safe.
translation: Farmers from Benue State took sacks of yam to the Makurdi market early in the morning.

sentence: Ambaliyar Binuwai ta ruguza gonakinmu bara, har yanzu ba mu farfaɗo ba.
translation: The Benue flood wrecked our farms last year, and we still haven't recovered.

sentence: A garinmu, kowa yana girmama tsohon nan don sharif ne daga zuriyar Annabi.
translation: In our town everyone respects that old man, because he is a sharif descended from the Prophet.

sentence: Kakata ta ce mini kakanta sharif ne, wanda ya zo daga Makka.
translation: My grandmother told me that her own grandfather was a sharif who came from Mecca.

sentence: Ba na son yadda wasu ke ɗaukar kansu sharif don neman girma.
translation: I hate the way some people pass themselves off as sharifs just to be looked up to.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta zuba rairayi a bakin ƙofa domin kada ruwa ya shiga ɗaki.
translation: My mother poured fine sand along the doorway so the rain wouldn't run into the room.

sentence: Magina sun haɗa rairayi da siminti kafin su fara ginin bangon makaranta.
translation: The builders mixed sand with cement before they started on the school wall.

sentence: Ban ji daɗin zama a bakin kogi ba, don rairayi ya shiga cikin abincinmu.
translation: I didn't enjoy sitting by the river, because the fine sand got into our food.

sentence: Ɗana yana koyon arabiyya a makarantar allo kowace yamma bayan sallar laʼasar.
translation: My son studies Arabic at the Qurʼanic school every evening after the afternoon prayer.

sentence: Malamin ya rubuta jimloli da arabiyya a allo, sai ɗalibai suka kwafa.
translation: The teacher wrote sentences in Arabic on the board, and the students copied them down.

sentence: Ina jin kunya idan baƙi suka yi magana da arabiyya, don ban iya ba.
translation: I get embarrassed when guests speak to me in Arabic, because I can't manage it.

sentence: Birgediya Janar ya ziyarci sansanin sojoji da ke Maiduguri, ya yaba musu.
translation: The brigadier general visited the army camp at Maiduguri and praised the soldiers there.

sentence: Ɗan uwana ya zama birgediya bayan shekara talatin, sai muka yi babban biki.
translation: My brother made brigadier after thirty years of service, so we threw a huge celebration.

sentence: Mun ji daɗi lokacin da birgediya ya sauƙaƙa dokar hana fita a garinmu.
translation: We were relieved when the brigadier eased the curfew in our town.

sentence: Gobe hakimi zai kira taro a fada domin a sasanta manoma da makiyaya.
translation: Tomorrow the district head will call a meeting at the palace to reconcile the farmers and the herders.

sentence: Mahaifina ya kai ƙararsa gaban hakimi bayan maƙwabci ya ƙwace masa gona.
translation: My father took his complaint before the district head after a neighbour seized his farmland.

sentence: Ina girmama hakimi saboda yakan saurari talakawa kafin ya yanke hukunci.
translation: I respect the district head because he hears the ordinary people out before passing judgement.

sentence: A ranar Sallah, matasa sun taru a filin dambe suna bugun ganga.
translation: On Sallah day the young men gathered at the dambe ground, drumming as they went.

sentence: Kakana ya yi dambe tun yana ƙarami, har hannunsa ya karye sau biyu.
translation: My grandfather boxed dambe from boyhood on, until he had broken his hand twice.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ba ta son dambe, tana cewa wasa ne mai haɗari ga yara.
translation: My mother doesn't like dambe; she says it's a dangerous sport for children.

sentence: Guga ya kubce mini a rijiya, sai na ji tsundum a ƙasan ruwa.
translation: The bucket slipped out of my hands at the well, and I heard the plop far down in the water.

sentence: Yara suna wasa a bakin kogi, suna jefa duwatsu su ji tsundum.
translation: The children are playing at the riverbank, throwing stones just to hear the plop.

sentence: Na tsorata sosai lokacin da wayata ta yi tsundum cikin bahon wanka.
translation: I was terrified when my phone went plop into the washing basin.

sentence: Bayan sallah, kakata takan roƙi Allah ya biya mana muradi.
translation: After the prayer my grandmother always asks God to grant us our heart's desire.

sentence: Kowane ɗalibi yana da muradi, amma ba kowa ne yake cimma nasa ba.
translation: Every student has an ambition, but not everyone gets to reach his own.

sentence: Muradi ɗaya nake da shi, wato in ga ƙanwata ta gama jamiʼa.
translation: I have just one wish: to see my little sister finish university.

sentence: Na je kanti da safe don in sayi sabulu, amma ya rufe.
translation: I went to the shop first thing this morning to buy soap, but it was shut.

sentence: Mahaifina yana da kanti a kasuwar Kurmi inda yake sayar da yadi.
translation: My father runs a shop in Kurmi market where he sells cloth.

sentence: Ba na son kantin nan domin mai shi yakan ƙara wa baƙi farashi.
translation: I don't like that shop, because the owner always charges strangers more.

sentence: Bayan da muka yi aure, mun sami mazauni kusa da gidan kakata.
translation: After we got married, we found a place to live near my grandmother's house.

sentence: A ofishin ƙidayar jamaʼa, sun tambaye ni sunana da kuma mazaunina.
translation: At the census office they asked me for my name and my place of residence.

sentence: Tsohon nan ba ya son barin mazauninsa duk da cewa rufin ya tsufa.
translation: That old man refuses to leave his dwelling, even though the roof is falling apart.

sentence: Kakata ta shimfiɗa tabarma a ƙarƙashin bishiyar mangwaro kafin baƙi su zo.
translation: My grandmother spread a mat under the mango tree before the guests arrived.

sentence: A masallaci, mun zauna a kan tabarma muna jiran limamin ya zo.
translation: In the mosque we sat on the mat, waiting for the imam to arrive.

sentence: Tabarmar da mahaifiyata ta saƙa tana da daɗin kwanciya fiye da katifa.
translation: The mat my mother wove is more comfortable to lie on than a mattress.

sentence: Na yi barci a tsakiyar laccar tarihi domin jiya ban huta ba.
translation: I fell asleep in the middle of the history lecture because I got no rest yesterday.

sentence: Farfesan ya jinkirta laccar safe har zuwa Litinin saboda taron malamai.
translation: The professor pushed the morning lecture back to Monday because of the staff meeting.

sentence: Laccar da muka ji jiya ta fi kowace daɗi a wannan zangon.
translation: Yesterday's lecture was the most enjoyable one we've had all term.

sentence: Mun dasa duma a bayan gida, yanzu ganyensa ya rufe katangar.
translation: We planted a gourd behind the house, and now its leaves have covered the whole wall.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta sayi duma biyu a kasuwa don ta dafa miya da yamma.
translation: My mother bought two gourds at the market so she could cook soup that evening.

sentence: Ina son miyar duma fiye da kowace miya da mahaifiyata takan dafa.
translation: I like gourd soup better than any other soup my mother makes.

sentence: Ta wanke ƙasan ɗakin har ya yi fes kafin baƙi su iso.
translation: She scrubbed the floor of the room until it was spotless before the guests turned up.

sentence: Ranar Sallah, mahaifina ya sa riga fara fes ya tafi masallaci.
translation: On the day of the festival my father put on a snow-white gown and went to the mosque.

sentence: Ina son yadda mahaifiyata take wanke tukwane har su yi fes kowace safiya.
translation: I love the way my mother scours the pots until they gleam every single morning.

sentence: Nas ɗin ta auna zafin jikin yaron kafin likita ya shigo ɗakin.
translation: The nurse took the boy's temperature before the doctor came into the room.

sentence: Ƙanwata tana karatun aikin nas a jamiʼar Bayero tun bara.
translation: My younger sister has been studying nursing at Bayero University since last year.

sentence: Nas ɗin da ta kula da ni a asibiti tana da haƙuri ƙwarai.
translation: The nurse who looked after me in hospital was extraordinarily patient.

sentence: Malamin ya gargaɗe mu kada mu kira wani kafiri saboda bambancin addini.
translation: Our teacher warned us never to call anyone an unbeliever just because his religion differs.

sentence: A cikin littafin tarihi, an yi bayanin yadda ake amfani da kalmar kafiri.
translation: The history book explains how the word for unbeliever came to be used.

sentence: Ban ji daɗi ba lokacin da ya kira maƙwabcinmu kafiri a gaban kowa.
translation: I felt terrible when he called our neighbour an unbeliever in front of everybody.

sentence: Mun hau mota da safe zuwa Bici, amma hanya ta cika da cunkoso.
translation: We caught a car to Bichi in the morning, but the road was jammed with traffic.

sentence: Kakana yana da gona a Bici inda yake noman gyaɗa duk shekara.
translation: My grandfather has a farm in Bichi where he grows groundnuts every year.

sentence: Kasuwar Bici ta fi ta Kano nutsuwa, shi ya sa nake son zuwa.
translation: Bichi market is calmer than the one in Kano, and that's why I like going there.

sentence: Sallar asuba farilla ce, don haka kakana yakan tashi kafin alfijir.
translation: The dawn prayer is an obligation, so my grandfather always gets up before first light.

sentence: Malam ya bayyana mana bambanci tsakanin farilla da sunna a darasin jiya.
translation: In yesterday's lesson the teacher explained to us the difference between an obligation and a recommended act.

sentence: Ban san cewa azumin Ramadan farilla ce ba sai da na girma.
translation: I didn't realise that fasting in Ramadan was an obligation until I was grown.

sentence: Kakana yana kiwon danda a bayan gida tun kafin haihuwata.
translation: My grandfather has been keeping a piebald horse behind the house since before I was born.

sentence: A ranar babbar sallah, sarki ya hau danda a gaban sauran mahaya.
translation: On the day of the great festival, the emir rode a piebald horse ahead of the other riders.

sentence: Ina son wannan danda fiye da kowane doki da ke gidan sarki.
translation: I like this piebald horse better than any other horse in the emir's stables.

sentence: Bayan gidan ya ƙone, mahaifiyata ta ce ƙaddara ce, ba laifin kowa ba.
translation: After the house burned down, my mother said it was fate, and nobody's fault.

sentence: A makarantar allo, malamin ya gaya mana cewa ƙaddara da ƙoƙari suna tafiya tare.
translation: At the Qur'anic school, the teacher told us that destiny and hard work go hand in hand.

sentence: Ban gamsu da sakamakon jarabawa ba, amma ƙaddara ce, sai haƙuri.
translation: I wasn't happy with my exam results, but it's fate, so all I can do is be patient.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta ajiye talle a kan murhu, sannan ta fara yanka albasa.
translation: My mother set the little soup pot on the hearth and then started slicing onions.

sentence: A kasuwar Kurmi, na sayi sabon talle domin miyar da za mu dafa gobe.
translation: At Kurmi market I bought a new soup pot for the stew we're cooking tomorrow.

sentence: Ina son miyar da aka dafa a talle fiye da ta babbar tukunya.
translation: I prefer stew cooked in a small pot to stew from a big cauldron.

sentence: Motarmu ta lalace a hanya, don haka mun kwana a Musawa.
translation: Our car broke down on the road, so we spent the night in Musawa.

sentence: An tura mahaifina Musawa domin ya koyar a sabuwar makarantar sakandare.
translation: My father was posted to Musawa to teach at the new secondary school.

sentence: Kasuwar Musawa ta fi ta garinmu yawan mutane, amma farashi yana da sauƙi.
translation: Musawa's market is far more crowded than our town's, but the prices are cheap.

sentence: Bayan mun idar da sallar azahar, sai muka koma gona don shuka.
translation: After we finished the noon prayer, we went back to the farm to sow.

sentence: Maigidan ya rufe shagon da azahar, ya ce za mu buɗe da yamma.
translation: The shop owner closed up at noon-prayer time and said we would open again in the evening.

sentence: Ba na son yin barci kafin azahar, domin ina jin nauyi bayan tashi.
translation: I don't like sleeping before the noon prayer, because I feel heavy when I wake up.

sentence: Da tsakar dare, fitilar mota ta yi wal a tagar ɗakinmu.
translation: In the middle of the night, a car's headlight flashed across our bedroom window.

sentence: Yayin da maƙerin ke walda, ƙarfen ya yi wal har na rufe idona.
translation: While the smith was welding, the metal flashed so brightly that I shut my eyes.

sentence: Na tsorata sosai lokacin da wal ya haskaka sararin sama kafin ruwan sama.
translation: I was really frightened when a sudden flash lit up the whole sky before the rain.

sentence: Akwai wani amo a rufin gida, kamar bera yana gudu.
translation: There's some noise up in the roof, as if a rat were running around.

sentence: Malam ya umarci ɗalibai su rage amo domin jarabawa za ta fara.
translation: The teacher told the students to keep the noise down because the exam was about to start.

sentence: Ina son shiru na ƙauye, saboda amo a birni yana ba ni haushi.
translation: I love the quiet of the village, because the noise in the city irritates me.

sentence: Mun sauka a Wudil don shan shayi kafin mu ci gaba zuwa Kano.
translation: We stopped in Wudil for a glass of tea before carrying on to Kano.

sentence: Ƙanwata tana karatun aikin gona a kwalejin da ke Wudil, kusa da Kano.
translation: My younger sister is studying agriculture at the college in Wudil, near Kano.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ratsa Wudil, ina tuna kakata da gonar rake.
translation: Every time I pass through Wudil, I think of my grandmother and her sugarcane field.

sentence: Na nemi hama a cikin akwatin kayan aiki don gyara ƙofar ɗakina.
translation: I looked for a hammer in the toolbox so I could fix my bedroom door.

sentence: A bita, kafintan ya buga ƙusa da hama har katakon ya kama sosai.
translation: In the workshop, the carpenter drove the nail in with a hammer until the plank held firm.

sentence: Ba na son a ba ƙaramin yaro hama, domin zai iya jikkata kansa.
translation: I don't like giving a small child a hammer, because he could hurt himself with it.

sentence: A gidan namun daji na Kano, yara suna kallon alade cikin mamaki.
translation: At the Kano zoo, the children stared at the pig in amazement.

sentence: Manomin ya gina katanga don kada alade ya shiga gonar dawa.
translation: The farmer built a wall to stop the pig from getting into the guinea-corn field.

sentence: Musulmi ba sa cin naman alade, domin addini ya haramta shi.
translation: Muslims do not eat pork, because their religion forbids it.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifiyata takan soya waina da manja kafin mu tashi.
translation: Every morning my mother fries waina in palm oil before we get up.

sentence: Farashin manja ya tashi sosai a kasuwa, don haka mun sayi kaɗan.
translation: The price of palm oil has shot up at the market, so we only bought a little.

sentence: Ban taɓa son abincin da aka dafa da manja mai yawa ba.
translation: I have never liked food that has been cooked with a lot of palm oil.

sentence: Karenmu yana kaɗa wutsiya duk lokacin da na dawo daga makaranta.
translation: Our dog wags his tail every single time I get back from school.

sentence: Malamin kimiyya ya nuna mana yadda kadangare yakan yanke wutsiya ya tsere.
translation: The science teacher showed us how a lizard sheds its tail and escapes.

sentence: A wurina, wutsiya ta fi daɗi a duk sassan naman shanu.
translation: For my money, the tail is the tastiest part of the whole cow.

sentence: Na sa barkono da yawa a miyar kuka, sai kowa ya yi atishawa.
translation: I put too much chilli in the kuka soup, and everyone started sneezing.

sentence: Yayata takan sayar da barkono busasshe a kasuwar Sabon Gari.
translation: My older sister sells dried chilli peppers at Sabon Gari market.

sentence: Ba na iya cin abinci mai barkono, domin cikina yakan yi zafi.
translation: I can't eat spicy food, because my stomach starts burning.

sentence: Na kwaɓa alli sannan na shafa bangon ɗakin har ya zama fari fat.
translation: I mixed up the whitewash and coated the bedroom wall until it was gleaming white.

sentence: Angon ya sa sabon kaftani fari fat, kowa kuwa yana kallonsa a bikin.
translation: The groom wore a brand-new kaftan, dazzling white, and everyone at the wedding was staring at him.

sentence: Gashin kansa ya zama fari fat tun bayan rasuwar matarsa.
translation: His hair has turned snow white ever since his wife passed away.

sentence: Kakana yakan gaya mana cewa mutumin da ba ya aiki wofi ne.
translation: My grandfather always tells us that a man who doesn't work is a good-for-nothing.

sentence: Duk ƙoƙarinmu ya zama aikin wofi bayan ambaliyar ta lalata gonar.
translation: All our effort came to nothing after the flood destroyed the farm.

sentence: Bayan shekaru uku ba tare da aiki ba, yana jin kamar wofi ne.
translation: After three years without a job, he feels like a complete waste of space.

sentence: A lokacin zafi mukan shafa wa jariri hoda bayan mun yi masa wanka.
translation: In the hot season we dust the baby with powder after we have bathed him.

sentence: Mata suna sayar da hoda da turare a kasuwar Kurmi kowace Jumaʼa.
translation: Women sell face powder and perfume at Kurmi market every Friday.

sentence: A ganina hoda mai yawa ba ta dace da fuskar yarinyar ba.
translation: To my eye, that much powder does not suit the girl's face at all.

sentence: Mahaifina ya yi danga da kara don kada awaki su shiga gonar.
translation: My father built a cornstalk fence so that the goats couldn't get into the farm.

sentence: Bayan girbi maƙwabtanmu sukan haɗa kai su gyara danga kewaye da ƙauyen.
translation: After the harvest our neighbours join forces to repair the fence around the village.

sentence: Iskar dare ta rushe danga, yanzu kowa yana ganin abin da ke gidanmu.
translation: The night wind brought the fence down, and now anyone can see what is inside our compound.

sentence: Maƙerinmu yakan narkar da tama don ya ƙera fartanya da lauje.
translation: Our blacksmith melts iron ore down so he can forge hoes and sickles.

sentence: Kamfanin nan yana haƙar tama a Itakpe tun shekarar da ta wuce.
translation: That company has been mining iron ore at Itakpe since last year.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda tama mai kama da dutse take zama ƙarfe mai wuya.
translation: It amazes me how ore that looks just like a stone turns into hard iron.

sentence: Yara sun cinye dukan anabi kafin baƙi su isa gidan.
translation: The children finished off all the grapes before the guests reached the house.

sentence: A watan Ramadan mukan sha ruwan anabi bayan mun karya azumi da dabino.
translation: During Ramadan we drink grape juice after breaking the fast with dates.

sentence: Na fi son anabi fiye da lemu, amma yana da tsada a kasuwarmu.
translation: I like grapes better than oranges, but they are expensive in our market.
