sentence: Kakana ya ba mu labarin damisa da ta kashe akuya a ƙauyensu.
translation: My grandfather told us the story of a leopard that killed a goat in their village.

sentence: Maʼaikatan gandun dajin Yankari sun ga damisa tana shan ruwa da safe.
translation: The staff at the Yankari game reserve saw a leopard drinking water in the morning.

sentence: Ina jin tsoron damisa fiye da zaki, domin tana farauta cikin duhun dare.
translation: I am more afraid of a leopard than of a lion, because it hunts in the dark of night.

sentence: Kakata takan zuba kanumfari a cikin shayi don ya rage mata ciwon haƙori.
translation: My grandmother drops cloves into her tea to ease her toothache.

sentence: Mai sayar da kayan yaji ya auna mini kanumfari a kasuwar Kano.
translation: The spice seller weighed out cloves for me at the Kano market.

sentence: Ƙamshin kanumfari a cikin miya yana tunatar da ni bikin ƙanwata.
translation: The smell of cloves in the stew takes me straight back to my younger sister's wedding.

sentence: Mahaifina yana da farar shadda da yakan sa a ranar Sallah.
translation: My father owns a white brocade outfit that he wears on Sallah day.

sentence: Na kai shadda wurin maɗinki don ya ɗinka min riga kafin bikin.
translation: I took the brocade to the tailor so he could sew me a gown before the wedding.

sentence: Shadda tana da tsada ƙwarai, don haka na sayi atamfa maimakonta.
translation: Brocade is far too expensive, so I bought printed cloth instead.

sentence: Motar Abuja ta sauke mu a Garki kafin lokacin azahar ya yi.
translation: The Abuja bus dropped us off in Garki before the time of the noon prayer.

sentence: Kawuna yana zaune a Garki, kuma yakan kira mu kowace Jumaʼa.
translation: My uncle lives in Garki, and he rings us every Friday.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin cunkoso kamar na kasuwar Garki a ranar Asabar ba.
translation: I have never seen a crush of people like the one at Garki market on a Saturday.

sentence: Siket ɗin da na saya a kasuwa jiya ya yi mini ƙarami.
translation: The skirt I bought at the market yesterday turned out too small for me.

sentence: Makarantar tana buƙatar kowace yarinya ta sa siket mai launin shuɗi.
translation: The school requires every girl to wear a blue skirt.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ba ta son in sa siket gajere idan za mu biki.
translation: My mother doesn't like me wearing a short skirt when we go to a celebration.

sentence: Da na dawo daga gona, matata ta yi mini tausa a bayana.
translation: When I came back from the farm, my wife massaged my back for me.

sentence: Likita ya shawarce ni da yin tausa kowace safiya don ciwon kafaɗa.
translation: The doctor advised me to have a massage every morning for my shoulder pain.

sentence: Tausa tana sa in yi barci mai kyau, don haka nakan biya kuɗinta.
translation: A massage makes me sleep well, so I don't mind paying for one.

sentence: Ɓarawon ya lula da wayata kafin mu iya kama shi a kasuwa.
translation: The thief made off with my phone before we could catch him in the market.

sentence: Da ɗan sanda ya bayyana, yaran da suke wasa a titi suka lula.
translation: The moment the policeman appeared, the boys playing in the street bolted.

sentence: Bayan rikicin, mutane da yawa sun lula zuwa ƙauyukan da ke kusa.
translation: After the unrest, a great many people fled to the villages nearby.

sentence: Gidan kakanmu ya zama kango tun bayan da muka ƙaura zuwa birni.
translation: Our grandfather's house has been a ruin ever since we moved to the city.

sentence: Yaran unguwa suna wasan ƙwallo kusa da kango da ke bayan makarantar.
translation: The neighbourhood boys play football beside the derelict building behind the school.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na wuce kango da dare, sai gashin jikina ya tashi.
translation: Every time I pass a ruined building at night, the hair on my body stands up.

sentence: Na tarar da tsutsa a cikin ɗayan mangwaron da kake ci.
translation: I found a worm inside one of the mangoes you are eating.

sentence: Likita ya ce tsutsa ce ke damun yaron, sai ya rubuta masa magani.
translation: The doctor said it was a worm troubling the boy, and he prescribed him medicine.

sentence: Ba na iya kallon tsutsa tana motsi, sai na ji tashin zuciya.
translation: I can't watch a worm wriggling without my stomach turning.

sentence: Yaron ya yi tusa a cikin motar, sai kowa ya fashe da dariya.
translation: The boy farted inside the car and everyone burst out laughing.

sentence: Malam ya ce duk wanda ya yi tusa dole ne ya sake alwala.
translation: The teacher said that anyone who farts must do his ablution again.

sentence: Kunya ta kama ni sosai lokacin da tusa ta kuɓuce mini a taro.
translation: I was mortified when a fart slipped out of me during the meeting.

sentence: Kakana yana kiwon tantabara a saman rufin gidansa tun ina ƙarama.
translation: My grandfather has kept pigeons on his roof since I was a little girl.

sentence: Mun sayi tantabara biyu a kasuwa domin dafa miya ga baƙi.
translation: We bought two pigeons at the market to cook a stew for the guests.

sentence: Muryar tantabara da safe tana sa in tuna ƙauyen da na girma.
translation: The cooing of a dove in the morning makes me think of the village where I grew up.

sentence: Wani akawu a banki ya ce mun makara, amma ya karɓi takardunmu.
translation: A clerk at the bank told us we had come too late, but he took our papers anyway.

sentence: Sabon akawu a ofishinmu yana rubuta sunayen kowa a babban littafi.
translation: The new clerk in our office writes everybody's name into a big ledger by hand.

sentence: Na gaji da jira, domin akawu bai buɗe taga ba har tsakar rana.
translation: I was worn out with waiting, because the clerk did not open his window until midday.

sentence: Kowane taliki yana neman abincinsa da safe, har da kyanwar bakin ƙofa.
translation: Every creature goes out looking for its food in the morning, even the cat by the doorway.

sentence: Limamin ya faɗa mana cewa kowane taliki yana da rabonsa a duniya.
translation: The imam told us that every living creature has its own portion in this world.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin taliki mai haƙuri kamar kakata a duk rayuwata ba.
translation: In my whole life I have never met a creature as patient as my grandmother.

sentence: Kakata takan cika tulu da ruwan rijiya kafin rana ta yi zafi.
translation: My grandmother fills the water pot from the well before the sun gets hot.

sentence: Na sayi tulu a kasuwar Kurmi domin ruwan sha ya yi sanyi.
translation: I bought a clay water pot at Kurmi market so the drinking water would stay cool.

sentence: Ruwan tulu ya fi na firji daɗi a ganina, musamman lokacin bazara.
translation: To my taste, water from a clay pot is nicer than water from the fridge, especially in the hot season.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan tafi safara bayan girbi, ya dawo da riguna da gishiri.
translation: After the harvest my father goes off trading and comes back with cloth and salt.

sentence: Kakana ya yi safara zuwa Kano da rakuma kafin a gina hanyar mota.
translation: My grandfather traded his way to Kano with camels, back before the motor road was built.

sentence: Safara ta gajiyar da shi, don haka ya buɗe shago a garinsu.
translation: The travelling trade wore him out, so he opened a shop in his home town.

sentence: ʼYan sanda sun kai samame a kasuwar bayan gari da tsakar dare.
translation: The police raided the market outside town in the middle of the night.

sentence: A zamanin da, samame yakan zo da dare, sai mutane su gudu zuwa duwatsu.
translation: In the old days a raid would come by night, and people would run for the hills.

sentence: Wannan samame ya tsoratar da yara, har yanzu ba sa fita da dare.
translation: That raid frightened the children so badly that they still will not go out after dark.

sentence: Mun sauka a Gwandu da yamma, muka nemi masauki kusa da babban masallaci.
translation: We arrived in Gwandu in the evening and looked for lodging near the great mosque.

sentence: Motar haya takan tashi daga Birnin Kebbi zuwa Gwandu kowace safiya da ƙarfe shida.
translation: The passenger van leaves Birnin Kebbi for Gwandu every morning at six o'clock.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya ce Gwandu ta yi ƙarfi sosai a zamanin daular Sakkwato.
translation: The history teacher said Gwandu was very powerful in the days of the Sokoto Caliphate.

sentence: Lokacin da nake rashin lafiya, mahaifiyata takan dafa min romo mai zafi.
translation: Whenever I was ill, my mother would cook me a bowl of hot broth.

sentence: Mai dafa abinci ya zuba romo a kwano kafin ya kawo mana nama.
translation: The cook ladled the broth into a bowl before he brought us the meat.

sentence: Ban taɓa jin daɗin romo kamar wanda muka sha bayan azumi ba.
translation: I have never enjoyed a broth as much as the one we drank when we broke the fast.

sentence: Da na zuba nama a tukunya, sai mai ya yi ca ya ƙone hannuna.
translation: As I dropped the meat into the pot, the oil spat and burned my hand.

sentence: Mai sayar da ƙosai ya ja da baya saʼad da man ya yi ca.
translation: The bean-cake seller pulled back when the hot oil spat out of the pan.

sentence: Duk lokacin da man ya yi ca, ƙaramar yarinya takan yi tsalle da tsoro.
translation: Every time the oil spits, the little girl jumps back in fright.

sentence: Ban so in zama munafuki ba, don haka na faɗa wa shugaban gaskiya.
translation: I did not want to be a hypocrite, so I told the boss the truth.

sentence: Limamin ya yi waʼazi cewa munafuki yana da alamu uku a hadisi.
translation: The imam preached that the hadith names three signs of a hypocrite.

sentence: Munafuki yakan yaba maka a gaba, ya zage ka a bayanka.
translation: A hypocrite praises you to your face and insults you behind your back.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta yanka abarba ta ajiye ta a firji har yara su dawo.
translation: My mother sliced the pineapple and kept it in the fridge until the children came home.

sentence: A kasuwar Jos, mata suna sayar da abarba mai zaƙi kan naira ɗari biyar.
translation: In the Jos market the women sell sweet pineapples for five hundred naira each.

sentence: Abarba tana sa min ciwon baki, amma ba zan iya barinta ba.
translation: Pineapple always makes my mouth sting, but I still cannot give it up.

sentence: Kowace yamma mahaifiyata takan dama fura da nono don mu sha.
translation: Every evening my mother mixes up fura with cultured milk for us to drink.

sentence: A kasuwar Kano ʼyan mata suna sayar da fura cikin ƙwarya da rana.
translation: At the Kano market girls sell fura out of calabashes all afternoon.

sentence: Bayan dogon azumi babu abin sha da ya fi fura da nono daɗi.
translation: After a long day of fasting there is no drink sweeter than fura and nono.

sentence: Bayan shekaru a kan wuta, tukunyar nan ta zama duna kamar gawayi.
translation: After years over the fire, that pot has turned as black as charcoal.

sentence: Cikin shanun garkenmu, duna ce ta fi kowace bayar da madara.
translation: Of all the cattle in our herd, it is the jet-black one that gives the most milk.

sentence: Abokan makaranta sun yi wa ƙanena laƙabi da duna, hakan ya ɓata masa rai.
translation: His schoolmates nicknamed my little brother "the black one", and it hurt his feelings.

sentence: Kakana yakan sayo sanka daga wurin mai sayar da taba duk ranar Alhamis.
translation: My grandfather buys a bunch of tobacco leaves from the tobacco seller every Thursday.

sentence: Manomin ya ɗaura sanka a kan babur kafin ya kama hanyar kasuwa.
translation: The farmer strapped the bundle of tobacco leaves onto his motorbike before setting off for the market.

sentence: Farashin sanka ya yi tsada bana, don haka masu shan taba suna gunaguni.
translation: The price of a bundle of tobacco has gone up this year, so the smokers are grumbling.

sentence: Direban ya yi mini ishara da hannu cewa in tsallaka hanyar da sauri.
translation: The driver signalled to me with his hand to cross the road quickly.

sentence: Ishara ɗaya daga wurin shugaban ta isa, sai kowa ya miƙe tsaye.
translation: One signal from the chairman was enough, and everyone rose to their feet.

sentence: A cikin taro na yi masa ishara ya yi shiru, amma bai kula ba.
translation: During the meeting I signalled him to be quiet, but he took no notice of me.

sentence: Bayan doguwar tafiya, mahaifiyata ta murza mini ƙafafuwa har ciwon ya ragu.
translation: After the long journey my mother massaged my feet until the ache eased off.

sentence: Tsohon ɗan kokawa yakan murza jikin ʼyan wasan da mai kafin gasar.
translation: The old wrestler rubs the young fighters down with oil before the contest.

sentence: Duk lokacin da ya damu, yakan murza goshinsa yana kallon ƙasa.
translation: Whenever he is worried, he rubs his forehead and stares at the ground.

sentence: Na manta da yis jiya, shi ya sa burodin bai kumbura ba ko kaɗan.
translation: I forgot the yeast yesterday, and that is why the bread did not rise at all.

sentence: Mai yin burodi yakan sayi yis mai yawa kafin ranar Sallah.
translation: The baker buys yeast in bulk before the Sallah holiday.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ba ta amincewa da yis, tana cewa burodin gargajiya ya fi lafiya.
translation: My mother does not trust yeast; she says traditional bread is healthier.

sentence: Ta buɗe gwangwani, ta zuba tumatirin cikin miyar da take dafawa.
translation: She opened a tin and poured the tomatoes into the stew she was cooking.

sentence: Mai sayar da gyaɗa yakan yi awo da gwangwani maimakon sikeli a kasuwarmu.
translation: The groundnut seller measures things out with a tin rather than a scale at our market.

sentence: Kada ka jefar da gwangwani, zan yi masa fenti in shuka fure a ciki.
translation: Don't throw the tin away; I'll paint it and plant a flower in it.

sentence: Mun cika akwati da tufafi kafin mu tashi zuwa Kaduna da safe.
translation: We filled the trunk with clothes before setting off for Kaduna in the morning.

sentence: Direban ya sauke akwati mai nauyi daga motar, sannan ya ɗaura shi a keke.
translation: The driver lifted a heavy crate down from the lorry and then tied it onto a bicycle.

sentence: Har yau duk hotunan kakata suna cikin wani tsohon akwati a ƙarƙashin gado.
translation: To this day all my grandmother's photographs sit in an old box under the bed.

sentence: Kowace safiya ʼyan mata sukan cika randa da ruwan rijiya kafin su tafi makaranta.
translation: Every morning the girls fill the water pot from the well before they go to school.

sentence: A ganina, ruwan randa ya fi ruwan firji sanyi a lokacin zafin bazara.
translation: To my mind, water from the clay pot is colder than fridge water in the hot season.

sentence: Yaron ya buga randa da ƙwallo, sai ta fashe ruwa ya zuba ƙasa.
translation: The boy hit the water pot with his ball; it cracked and the water spilled on the ground.

sentence: Alaramma yakan tashi da ƙarfe huɗu don ya yi karatun Alƙurʼani kafin sallar asuba.
translation: The alaramma gets up at four o'clock to recite the Quran before the dawn prayer.

sentence: Iyaye sun kai ʼyaʼyansu wurin alaramma domin ya koya musu haddar Alƙurʼani.
translation: The parents took their children to the alaramma so that he would teach them to memorise the Quran.

sentence: A garinmu ana girmama alaramma fiye da kowa a lokacin watan azumi.
translation: In our town the alaramma is honoured above everyone else during the fasting month.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta cika buta da ruwan sanyi kafin baƙi su iso.
translation: My mother filled the water jug with cold water before the guests arrived.

sentence: Kowane safe yakan ɗauki buta ya je masallaci domin yin alwala.
translation: Every morning he takes the ewer and goes to the mosque to perform his ablutions.

sentence: Yaron ya karya buta a bakin rijiya, yanzu yana jin tsoron komawa gida.
translation: The boy broke a water jug at the well, and now he is afraid to go home.

sentence: Ɗan kasuwa ya yi wa mahaifina zamba, ya sayar masa da wayar ƙarya.
translation: A trader defrauded my father — he sold him a fake phone.

sentence: ʼYan sanda sun kama matashin da ya yi wa tsofaffi zamba ta waya.
translation: The police arrested the young man who had been swindling elderly people over the phone.

sentence: Kada ka ba wa kowa lambar asusunka, zamba ta yawaita a wannan zamani.
translation: Don't give anyone your account number; fraud has become common these days.

sentence: Jirgin ruwan kifi ya shafe kwana uku a bahar kafin ya dawo tashar.
translation: The fishing boat spent three days at sea before it came back to the harbour.

sentence: Kakana yakan ce ruwan bahar ya fi na rijiya gishiri sosai.
translation: My grandfather always says that sea water is far saltier than well water.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin bahar ba sai da na kai Legas, na tsorata da girmansa.
translation: I had never seen the sea until I got to Lagos, and its vastness frightened me.

sentence: Injiniya ya gano aibi a injin motar bayan ya buɗe murfin gaba.
translation: The mechanic found a fault in the car's engine after he opened the bonnet.

sentence: Malamin ya ce babu wanda ba shi da aibi, sai mu yafe wa juna.
translation: The teacher said that nobody is without fault, so we should forgive one another.

sentence: Rigar da na saya tana da ƙaramin aibi, amma ban mayar da ita ba.
translation: The gown I bought has a small flaw, but I didn't take it back.

sentence: Jamiʼan sansan sun zo unguwarmu da safe, suna ƙidaya mutanen kowane gida.
translation: The census officials came to our neighbourhood in the morning, counting the people in every household.

sentence: Gwamnati ta dage sansan har bayan damina saboda hanyoyin ƙauyuka sun lalace.
translation: The government postponed the census until after the rainy season because the village roads are ruined.

sentence: Ban yarda da sakamakon sansan ba, domin ba a ƙidaya mutanenmu duka ba.
translation: I don't accept the census results, because our people were not all counted.

sentence: Duk lokacin da kawuna ya dawo daga Kano, yakan kawo mana kilishi.
translation: Whenever my uncle comes back from Kano, he brings us kilishi.

sentence: Mai sayar da kilishi ya shimfiɗa naman a kan tabarma ƙarƙashin rana.
translation: The kilishi seller spread the meat out on a mat under the sun.

sentence: Ban taɓa cin kilishi mai daɗi kamar wanda muka saya a Zariya ba.
translation: I have never eaten kilishi as good as the batch we bought in Zaria.

sentence: Jiya da yamma ƙanƙara ta sauko, yara suka fita suna tara ta.
translation: Hail came down yesterday evening, and the children went out gathering it.

sentence: Mai sayar da kifi ya rufe kwandonsa da ƙanƙara don kada nama ya lalace.
translation: The fish seller covered his basket with ice so that the flesh would not spoil.

sentence: Ba na son shan ruwa mai ƙanƙara, domin makogwarona kan yi ciwo daga baya.
translation: I don't like drinking iced water, because my throat aches afterwards.

sentence: Na kwana biyu ina jira a ofishin fasfo kafin su ɗauki hotona.
translation: I spent two days waiting at the passport office before they took my photograph.

sentence: Ka duba ranar ƙarewar fasfo kafin ka sayi tikitin jirgin sama.
translation: Check the expiry date on your passport before you buy your plane ticket.

sentence: Ya rasa fasfo a filin jirgin sama, sai tafiyarsa ta ci tura.
translation: He lost his passport at the airport, and the whole trip fell through.

sentence: Bora tana dafa abinci a baya, yayin da ƙishiyarta ke zaune da mijinsu.
translation: The less-favoured wife is cooking out at the back while her co-wife sits with their husband.

sentence: Malamin ya gargaɗi miji cewa kada ya mayar da wata matarsa bora.
translation: The malam warned the husband not to turn one of his wives into a neglected one.

sentence: Ta shafe shekaru tana ganin kanta a matsayin bora a gidan mijinta.
translation: She spent years feeling like the unloved wife in her husband's house.

sentence: Da yamma mukan taru wurin mai suya, muna hira har dare ya yi.
translation: In the evening we gather at the suya stall and chat until night falls.

sentence: Bayan mun gama aiki, sai muka sayi suya da albasa a bakin hanya.
translation: After we finished work, we bought suya with onions at the roadside.

sentence: Ƙanshin suya ya bazu unguwar, har yunwa ta kama ni sosai.
translation: The smell of suya spread through the neighbourhood until hunger really took hold of me.

sentence: Kasuwar Jibiya takan cika da ʼyan kasuwa daga Nijar kowace Talata.
translation: The Jibia market fills up with traders from Niger every Tuesday.

sentence: Mahaifina ya girma a Jibiya kafin ya ƙaura zuwa Kano don kasuwanci.
translation: My father grew up in Jibia before he moved to Kano for trade.

sentence: Ina kewar Jibiya sosai, musamman ranar kasuwa lokacin da kowa ke murna.
translation: I miss Jibia badly, especially on market day when everyone is in high spirits.

sentence: A gidanmu, yin ban kwana kafin fita sara ce da kowa ya gada.
translation: In our house, saying goodbye before you go out is a custom everyone has inherited.

sentence: Shugaba ya gargaɗe mu cewa yawan makara sara ce marar kyau a ofis.
translation: The boss warned us that turning up late all the time is a bad habit in an office.

sentence: Ban ji daɗin sara irin ta ɗan uwana ba, kullum yana katse magana.
translation: I have never liked my brother's habit; he is forever cutting in on people.

sentence: Lokacin damina ana samun mangwaro birjik a kasuwar garinmu.
translation: In the rainy season there are mangoes in abundance at our town's market.

sentence: Mutane sun taru birjik a filin, suna jiran jawabin gwamna.
translation: People had gathered in crowds on the field, waiting for the governor's speech.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin taurari birjik haka ba sai da muka kwana a ƙauye.
translation: I had never seen stars scattered so thickly until the night we spent in the village.

sentence: Kakata takan tafasa ganyen aduwa domin maganin ciwon ciki.
translation: My grandmother boils desert date leaves to make medicine for a stomach ache.

sentence: Mun huta ƙarƙashin wata babbar aduwa har rana ta sassauta.
translation: We rested under a big desert date tree until the sun let up.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan sayar da aduwa a kasuwar Litinin don biyan kuɗin makaranta.
translation: My mother sells desert dates at the Monday market to pay the school fees.

sentence: Kakana yakan ɗaure gashin tsuntsu a bayan kowace kibiya kafin farauta.
translation: My grandfather ties a feather to the back of every arrow before a hunt.

sentence: Mafarauci ya harba kibiya, amma barewar ta tsere zuwa cikin daji.
translation: The hunter loosed an arrow, but the gazelle escaped into the bush.

sentence: Maganarsa ta soke ni kamar kibiya, har ban iya amsawa ba.
translation: His words went through me like an arrow, and I could not even answer.

sentence: Kawuna ya koya mini kaɗa molo tun ina ƙarami a ƙauyenmu.
translation: My uncle taught me to play the molo back when I was small in our village.

sentence: Mawaƙin ya ɗauki molo ya fara waƙa a wajen bikin auren ƙanwata.
translation: The singer picked up his molo and started to sing at my little sister's wedding.

sentence: Sautin molo da daddare yakan tuna mini ƙuruciyata a ƙauye.
translation: The sound of a molo at night always reminds me of my childhood in the village.

sentence: Mun yi shirka da ɗan uwana wajen sayar da shinkafa a kasuwa.
translation: My cousin and I went into partnership selling rice at the market.

sentence: Shirka tsakanina da Musa ta ƙare lokacin da ya ɓoye riba.
translation: The partnership between Musa and me ended when he hid the profit.

sentence: A huɗubar Jumaʼa malam ya tuna mana cewa shirka babban zunubi ne.
translation: In the Friday sermon the malam reminded us that idolatry is a grave sin.

sentence: Wata ri ta shanu ta ratsa hanya, sai dukan motoci suka tsaya.
translation: A moving herd of cattle cut across the road, and every car had to stop.

sentence: Da wasan ƙwallo ya ƙare, ri ta mutane ta malalo daga filin.
translation: When the football match ended, a throng of people came streaming out of the ground.

sentence: Har yanzu ina tunawa da ri ta raƙuma da muka gani a hamada.
translation: I still remember the train of camels we saw out in the desert.

sentence: Bayan sallar asuba kakana yakan zauna yana zikiri har rana ta fito.
translation: After the dawn prayer my grandfather sits doing dhikr until the sun comes up.

sentence: A daren Jumaʼa maƙwabta kan taru a masallaci suna zikiri tare.
translation: On Thursday nights the neighbours gather at the mosque and do dhikr together.

sentence: Duk lokacin da damuwa ta kama ni, ina zikiri har in natsu.
translation: Whenever worry takes hold of me, I recite dhikr until I settle down.

sentence: Kawuna kwamanda ne a rundunar ʼyan sanda, don haka yakan makara da dare.
translation: My uncle is a commander in the police force, so he often gets home late at night.

sentence: Sabon kwamanda ya ziyarci shingen bincike a hanyar Maiduguri jiya.
translation: The new commander inspected the checkpoint on the Maiduguri road yesterday.

sentence: Muryar kwamanda ta sa kowa ya yi shiru a filin atisaye.
translation: The commander's voice made everyone fall silent on the parade ground.

sentence: Shayin da mahaifiyata ta zuba yana da zafi zau, sai na jira.
translation: The tea my mother poured is piping hot, so I had to wait.

sentence: Ruwan zuma da muka saya a kasuwar Kano yana da zaƙi zau.
translation: The honey we bought at the Kano market is unbelievably sweet.

sentence: Ban iya shan miyar ba, tana da zafi zau har hawaye suka zubo.
translation: I couldn't get the stew down; it was so scalding hot my eyes watered.

sentence: Na buɗe taswirar birnin a kan gado don neman hanyar asibiti.
translation: I spread the city map out on the bed to find the road to the hospital.

sentence: Malam ya rataya taswirar Afirka a bango kafin ya fara darasi.
translation: The teacher hung the map of Africa on the wall before starting the lesson.

sentence: Ban san inda muke ba, domin taswirar da nake da ita ta tsufa.
translation: I have no idea where we are, because the map I'm carrying is out of date.

sentence: Maʼaikatan kamfanin sun yi amfani da nakiya wajen tsage duwatsun kan hanya.
translation: The company's workmen used explosives to break up the rocks blocking the road.

sentence: Sojoji sun cire nakiya daga gonar kafin manoma su koma noma.
translation: Soldiers cleared the explosives out of the field before the farmers went back to work.

sentence: Ƙarar nakiya a maʼadinan dutse ta tsorata yara, suka gudu gida.
translation: The blast of explosives at the stone quarry frightened the children, and they ran home.

sentence: Kacar kekena ta tsinke a hanya, sai na tura shi har gida.
translation: My bicycle chain snapped on the way, so I pushed the bike the whole way home.

sentence: Makanike ya shafa mai a kaca kafin ya mayar da ita wurinta.
translation: The mechanic oiled the chain before slipping it back into place.

sentence: Ba na son hawan wannan keken, domin kacarsa takan fita a kowane tudu.
translation: I hate riding that bicycle, because its chain comes off on every slope.

sentence: A watan Zulhajji ne mahaifina ya tafi aikin Hajji a Makka.
translation: It was during Dhu al-Hijjah that my father left for the pilgrimage in Mecca.

sentence: Kasuwar rago takan yi cunkoso ƙwarai kafin goman farko na Zulhajji.
translation: The ram market gets packed just before the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

sentence: Ina son watan Zulhajji, domin iyalinmu duka sukan taru don Babbar Sallah.
translation: I love the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, because our whole family gathers for Eid al-Adha.

sentence: Malamin ya karya allin sau biyu yayin da yake rubutu a allo.
translation: The teacher snapped the chalk twice while he was writing on the board.

sentence: Yara sun ɗauki alli suka zana gidaje a kan siminti a gaban ƙofa.
translation: The children took chalk and drew houses on the concrete by the front door.

sentence: Likita ya ce yaron yana buƙatar alli, don haka mukan ba shi madara.
translation: The doctor said the boy needs calcium, so we give him milk every day.

sentence: Samanja ya tsaya gaban sojoji yana kirga su kafin darasin motsa jiki.
translation: The sergeant major stood in front of the troops counting them before the drill.

sentence: Kawuna ya yi ritaya a matsayin samanja, yanzu yana noma a ƙauye.
translation: My uncle retired as a sergeant major; these days he farms out in the village.

sentence: Muryar samanja tana da tsanani har sabbin sojoji sukan yi rawar jiki.
translation: The sergeant major's voice is so harsh that the new recruits shake when they hear it.

sentence: Kakata ta ɗauki gitta ta tsattsaga itace don girkin abincin dare.
translation: My grandmother picked up the little axe and split firewood for the evening meal.

sentence: Mafarauci yakan sa gitta a jakarsa kafin ya shiga cikin daji.
translation: A hunter always packs a small axe in his bag before heading into the bush.

sentence: Ban sami gitta ba a ɗakin kaya, sai na yanke rassan da wuƙa.
translation: I couldn't find the little axe in the storeroom, so I cut the branches with a knife.

sentence: A gidan tarihi na Jos mun ga gunkin dutse mai shekaru ɗari uku.
translation: At the museum in Jos we saw a stone idol three hundred years old.

sentence: Kakanninmu sun daina bautar gunki tun lokacin da Musulunci ya isa garin.
translation: Our forefathers gave up worshipping idols back when Islam reached the town.

sentence: Malamin ya ce kuɗi ya zama gunki a zukatan mutane da yawa.
translation: The teacher said money has become an idol in the hearts of a great many people.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta kai ɗanʼuwana wurin boka kafin mu tafi asibiti.
translation: My mother took my brother to the traditional healer before we went to the hospital.

sentence: Bokan ƙauyen yana sayar da ganyaye da ɓawon itace a kasuwar Litinin.
translation: The village herbalist sells leaves and tree bark at the Monday market.

sentence: Ban amince da boka ba, amma maganinsa na ganye ya rage mini zazzaɓi.
translation: I don't trust the herbalist, but his leaf medicine did bring my fever down.

sentence: Da safe hazo ya rufe hanya, har muka yi jinkirin tafiya gona.
translation: In the morning the fog covered the road, so we set out late for the farm.

sentence: Hazo ya rufe filin jirgin Kano, jirginmu bai tashi ba sai da rana.
translation: Haze closed in over Kano airport, and our plane did not take off until midday.

sentence: Tun da ya tsufa, hazo ya rufe idanunsa, ba ya ganin fuskata sosai.
translation: Since he grew old a haze has covered his eyes, and he can no longer see my face clearly.

sentence: Mun shafe tsawon yini a mota kafin mu isa Akure da yamma.
translation: We spent the whole day on the bus before we reached Akure in the evening.

sentence: Ɗan uwana ya bar Kano zuwa Akure domin karatun injiniya a jamiʼa.
translation: My cousin left Kano for Akure to study engineering at the university there.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin ruwan sama kamar na Akure ba, ko da watan Disamba.
translation: I have never seen rain like the rain in Akure, not even in December.

sentence: Mahaifina ya shuka maiwa a gonar kudu, gero kuma a ta arewa.
translation: My father planted late millet in the southern field and early millet in the northern one.

sentence: Mata sun kai maiwa kasuwar Dawanau, amma farashinta ya faɗi sosai.
translation: The women took the late millet to Dawanau market, but its price had fallen badly.

sentence: Na fi son furar maiwa, domin tana da daɗi fiye da ta gero.
translation: I prefer fura made with late millet, because it tastes better than the kind made with early millet.

sentence: Kowace Alhamis malam yakan yi mana shifta kafin mu tashi daga aji.
translation: Every Thursday the teacher gives us a dictation before we leave the classroom.

sentence: Shifta ta jiya ta ba ni wahala, na yi kurakurai guda bakwai.
translation: Yesterday's dictation gave me real trouble; I made seven mistakes in it.

sentence: Shugabar makaranta ta ce shifta tana taimaka wa yara wajen inganta rubutu.
translation: The headmistress says dictation helps the children improve their spelling.

sentence: Sojoji sun dawo daga yaƙi da ganima mai yawa, suka raba ta a tsakaninsu.
translation: The soldiers came back from the war with a great deal of loot and shared it out among themselves.

sentence: Bayan hadari, yara sun tattara mangwaron da suka faɗi kamar ganima.
translation: After the storm the children gathered up the fallen mangoes like spoils of war.

sentence: Malam ya gargaɗe mu cewa dukiyar da aka sata ba ganima ba ce.
translation: The teacher warned us that stolen property is not lawful booty.

sentence: Na sayi gam a kasuwa domin in manne shafukan littafin da suka tsage.
translation: I bought glue at the market so I could stick back the torn pages of the book.

sentence: Yara suna liƙa hotuna da gam a bangon aji don bikin makaranta.
translation: The children are sticking pictures on the classroom wall with glue for the school celebration.

sentence: Gam ɗin ya bushe a cikin kwalba, don haka kujerar ta sake karyewa.
translation: The glue had dried up inside the bottle, so the chair came apart again.

sentence: A ranar bikinta ta sa sarƙar murjani da mahaifiyarta ta ba ta.
translation: On her wedding day she wore the coral necklace her mother had given her.

sentence: Mahaifina yana sayar da murjani a kasuwar Kurmi tun kafin a haife ni.
translation: My father has been selling coral in Kurmi market since before I was born.

sentence: Murjani na gaskiya ya fi tsada, amma launinsa ba ya ɓacewa ko kaɗan.
translation: Real coral costs more, but its colour does not fade in the least.

sentence: Kakana ya yi almajiranci a Kano kafin ya koma gonar mahaifinsa.
translation: My grandfather went through almajiri schooling in Kano before he went back to his father's farm.

sentence: Gwamnati ta ce za ta gyara almajiranci, ba za ta hana shi ba.
translation: The government says it will reform the almajiri system rather than ban it.

sentence: Mutane da yawa suna zargin almajiranci, alhali matsalar ita ce rashin tallafi.
translation: Many people blame the almajiri system, when the real problem is the lack of support for it.

sentence: Kowace Jumaʼa mahaifiyata takan ba miskini abinci a ƙofar masallaci.
translation: Every Friday my mother gives food to a poor man at the mosque gate.

sentence: Wani miskini ya zauna a gaban shago yana roƙon kuɗin magani.
translation: A pauper sat down in front of the shop, begging for money for medicine.

sentence: Kada ka raina miskini, domin dukiya tana zuwa tana kuma tafiya.
translation: Do not look down on a poor man, because wealth comes and wealth goes.

sentence: Malam ya sa mu haddace jadawalin ninkawa har zuwa goma sha biyu.
translation: The teacher made us memorise the multiplication tables all the way up to twelve.

sentence: Da yamma nakan zauna da ɗana muna maimaita jadawali kafin cin abinci.
translation: In the evenings I sit with my son and we go over the times tables before supper.

sentence: Tun ina ƙarami na haddace jadawali, har yau ba na buƙatar kalkuleta.
translation: I learned the times tables by heart as a child, and to this day I need no calculator.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta ɗora shinkafa a kan mizanin kasuwa kafin ta biya.
translation: My mother put the rice on the market scales before she paid.

sentence: Mai sayar da nama ya ce mizaninsa ba ya yin ƙarya.
translation: The butcher insists that his scales never lie.

sentence: A ranar sakamako, malam yakan auna kowane ɗalibi da mizani ɗaya.
translation: On results day the teacher measures every pupil by the same standard.

sentence: Da tsakar dare muka tafi gidan ungozoma, saboda matata ta shiga naƙuda.
translation: At midnight we went to the midwife's house, because my wife had gone into labour.

sentence: Ungozomar ƙauyenmu ta taimaka wa ɗaruruwan mata a shekara talatin da suka wuce.
translation: Our village midwife has helped hundreds of women over the past thirty years.

sentence: Kowace mace a unguwar tana girmama ungozomar da ta karɓi ɗanta.
translation: Every woman in the neighbourhood honours the midwife who delivered her child.

sentence: Aminina Sani yakan kawo mini fura duk lokacin da ya dawo daga gona.
translation: My close friend Sani brings me fura every time he comes back from the farm.

sentence: Ya bar shagon a hannun amininsa lokacin da ya tafi aikin hajji.
translation: He left the shop in the hands of his trusted friend when he went on the pilgrimage.

sentence: Amini na gaskiya ba ya yaɗa asirin da ka faɗa masa.
translation: A true friend does not spread the secret you told him.

sentence: Sarki ya sanya alkyabbar zinariya kafin ya fito wajen hawan sallah.
translation: The emir put on his gold cloak before riding out for the Sallah procession.

sentence: Kakana ya ajiye alkyabbarsa a akwati, yakan fitar da ita ranar biki.
translation: My grandfather keeps his cloak in a trunk and brings it out on wedding days.

sentence: Ina jin kunya in sanya alkyabba, don ban kai matsayin ba tukuna.
translation: I would be embarrassed to wear the cloak, because I have not yet earned that rank.

sentence: Aninin rigar makarantar ɗana ya faɗi, sai na ɗinka shi da hannu.
translation: The button on my son's school shirt came off, so I sewed it back on by hand.

sentence: Maɗinkin kasuwar Kurmi ya ɗinka mini anini a kan sabuwar rigata.
translation: The tailor at Kurmi market sewed a button onto my new gown for me.

sentence: A lokacin hirar aiki, na riƙa jujjuya aninin rigata don tsoro.
translation: During the job interview I kept twisting the button on my shirt out of nerves.

sentence: Da wutar lantarki ta yanke, mahaifina ya kunna fitilar kananzir a tsakiyar ɗakin.
translation: When the power went off, my father lit the kerosene lamp in the middle of the room.

sentence: Ɗalibai suna karatu ƙarƙashin fitilar titi domin babu wuta a gida.
translation: The students are studying under the street lamp because there is no electricity at home.

sentence: Ina son fitilar da kakata takan kunna lokacin da ake ba da labari.
translation: I love the lamp my grandmother lights when the storytelling begins.

sentence: Motar da za ta Ringim tana tashi daga tasha ƙarfe bakwai.
translation: The bus bound for Ringim leaves the motor park at seven.

sentence: Mun sayi shanu a kasuwar Ringim, sannan muka koma Dutse da yamma.
translation: We bought cattle at the Ringim market, then went back to Dutse in the evening.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na koma Ringim, ina jin daɗin shiru da nake samu.
translation: Every time I go back to Ringim, I relish the quiet I find there.

sentence: Mun shuka dauro a farkon damina, ba za mu girbe shi ba sai Oktoba.
translation: We planted late millet at the start of the rains; we will not harvest it until October.

sentence: Kakata takan dama fura da garin dauro don mu sha da nono.
translation: My grandmother mixes fura from late-millet flour so we can drink it with sour milk.

sentence: Dauro yakan fi gero daɗi, amma yana jinkirin nunawa sosai.
translation: Late millet tastes better than early millet, but it takes far longer to ripen.

sentence: Mutane kan ziyarci kabarin waliyyin nan don neman albarka.
translation: People visit that holy man's grave to seek a blessing.

sentence: Malam ya ba mu labarin wani waliyyi da ya warkar da makaho a kasuwa.
translation: The teacher told us the story of a saint who healed a blind man in the market.

sentence: Tsohuwar ta rantse cewa waliyyi ne ya cece ta daga ambaliyar.
translation: The old woman swore it was a holy man who saved her from the flood.

sentence: Mahaifiyata tana juya tuwo da cibin itace har ya yi kauri.
translation: My mother is stirring the tuwo with a wooden spoon until it thickens.

sentence: Ba a cin tuwo da cibi a nan, da hannu ake ci.
translation: People here do not eat tuwo with a spoon; they eat it with the hand.

sentence: Yaron ya ƙi cin magani sai da na ba shi cibin zuma.
translation: The boy refused his medicine until I gave him a spoonful of honey.

sentence: Yara sun jefa bal ɗin a cikin rijiyar makwabcinmu, yanzu suna kuka.
translation: The children threw the ball down our neighbour's well, and now they're in tears.

sentence: Malamin wasanni ya ɗauko sabon bal daga kasuwar Kano ranar Litinin.
translation: The sports teacher brought back a new ball from Kano market on Monday.

sentence: Ban ji daɗi ba lokacin da babban yayana ya karɓe mini bal ɗin.
translation: I was hurt when my eldest brother snatched the ball away from me.

sentence: Kada ka zama sakarai wanda yake barin aikin gona ga ƙanensa.
translation: Don't turn into a good-for-nothing who dumps the farm work on his little brother.

sentence: Maigidan ya ce masa sakarai ne, don ba ya iya rufe shago da kansa.
translation: The boss called him a useless fellow, since he can't even lock up the shop on his own.

sentence: Na ji kunya sosai lokacin da mahaifina ya kira ni sakarai gaban baƙi.
translation: I felt deeply ashamed when my father called me a useless person in front of guests.

sentence: Mun huta a inuwar giginya har rana ta karkata yamma.
translation: We rested in the shade of the deleb palm until the sun leaned towards the west.

sentence: Kafinta ya yi amfani da katakon giginya wajen rufin sabon rumbunmu.
translation: The carpenter used deleb-palm beams for the roof of our new grain store.

sentence: Giginyar da kakana ya dasa a bayan gida ta fi kowace tsayi.
translation: The deleb palm my grandfather planted behind the house is taller than any other.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan sa daddawa a miyar kuka don ta yi ƙamshi.
translation: My mother always puts locust-bean condiment in the baobab-leaf soup to give it its aroma.

sentence: Mun sayi daddawa a kasuwar Kurmi, amma farashinta ya tashi sosai.
translation: We bought locust-bean condiment at Kurmi market, but its price has shot up.

sentence: Baƙon nan bai saba da ƙamshin daddawa ba, sai ya ƙi cin miyar.
translation: The guest wasn't used to the smell of locust-bean condiment, so he refused the soup.

sentence: Yayana yakan kai ni makaranta a kan basukur kowace safiya.
translation: My older brother takes me to school on his bicycle every morning.

sentence: Mai gyaran basukur ya gyara min taya cikin minti goma kacal.
translation: The bicycle repairman fixed my tyre for me in barely ten minutes.

sentence: An sace min basukur a gaban masallaci, har yanzu ina baƙin ciki.
translation: My bicycle was stolen outside the mosque, and I'm still sick about it.

sentence: Na biya rabi yau, sauran balas ɗin zan kawo ranar Jumaʼa.
translation: I paid half today; I'll bring the rest of what I owe on Friday.

sentence: Maginin ya ƙi ci gaba da aiki har sai mun biya balas ɗinsa.
translation: The builder refused to carry on working until we paid him the money still owed.

sentence: Har yanzu ina jiran balas ɗin aikin da na yi wa kamfanin watan jiya.
translation: I'm still waiting on the balance for the job I did for the company last month.

sentence: Jaririn ya yi ƙiba sumul tun da mahaifiyarsa ta fara ba shi madara.
translation: The baby has filled out and looks wonderfully well since his mother started giving him milk.

sentence: Mai sayar da dabbobi ya ce raƙumin nan sumul ne, ba shi da cuta.
translation: The livestock trader says this camel is in prime condition, with nothing wrong with it.

sentence: Na yi farin ciki ganin ɗana ya dawo daga makarantar kwana sumul.
translation: It gladdened me to see my son come home from boarding school looking so healthy.

sentence: Likitan ya bayyana wa ɗalibai yadda azzakari yake aiki a jikin namiji.
translation: The doctor explained to the students how the penis functions in the male body.

sentence: Malamin lafiya ya koya wa maza tsaftar azzakari domin kariya daga cututtuka.
translation: The health worker taught the men penile hygiene as a protection against disease.

sentence: Ya ji kunyar tambaya, amma ciwon azzakari ya tilasta masa zuwa asibiti.
translation: He was too embarrassed to ask, but the pain in his penis forced him to the hospital.

sentence: Da safe mun ga dinya biyu suna iyo a fadamar bayan gonarmu.
translation: In the morning we saw two knob-billed ducks swimming in the marsh behind our farm.

sentence: Mafarauci ya ɓoye a cikin ciyawa yana jiran dinya ta sauka kan ruwa.
translation: The hunter crouched in the grass, waiting for a knob-billed duck to settle on the water.

sentence: Kakana yakan ce tun da daɗewa dinya na cika fadamar nan lokacin damina.
translation: My grandfather likes to say that long ago knob-billed ducks filled this marsh in the rainy season.

sentence: Mun isa Katagum da misalin ƙarfe biyar, sai ruwan sama ya fara sauka.
translation: We reached Katagum at about five o'clock, and then the rain started coming down.

sentence: Sarkin Katagum ya buɗe sabon asibiti a Azare ranar Talata da yamma.
translation: The Emir of Katagum opened the new hospital in Azare on Tuesday evening.

sentence: Ina kewar Katagum, musamman kasuwar Litinin da ƙamshin waina da safe.
translation: I miss Katagum, especially the Monday market and the smell of rice cakes in the morning.

sentence: Da muka ji ƙarar igwa, sai muka san lokacin buɗa baki ya yi.
translation: When we heard the cannon go off, we knew it was time to break the fast.

sentence: Sojoji sun ja igwa zuwa bakin ƙofar birni kafin gari ya waye.
translation: The soldiers dragged the cannon to the city gate before daybreak.

sentence: Ƙarar igwa ta tsorata yara, don haka mahaifiyarsu ta rungume su.
translation: The boom of the cannon terrified the children, so their mother pulled them into her arms.

sentence: Masu busa algaita sun bi dokin sarki har ƙofar fada.
translation: The algaita players followed the emir's horse all the way to the palace gate.

sentence: Da yamma kakana yakan busa algaita a gaban gidanmu har dare ya yi.
translation: In the evening my grandfather plays the algaita in front of our house until night falls.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ji algaita, sai in tuna bikin auren ʼyarʼuwata.
translation: Every time I hear an algaita, I think back to my sister's wedding.

sentence: A bikin sarauta, yaron nan yana bugun kuge da ƙaramin ƙaho.
translation: At the coronation festival, that boy is beating the kuge with a little horn.

sentence: Yaran unguwa sun aro kuge namu, amma ba su mayar da shi ba.
translation: The neighbourhood boys borrowed our kuge and never brought it back.

sentence: Ƙarar kuge ta fi ta ganga daɗi a kunnena, amma tana da tsanani.
translation: The clang of the kuge pleases my ear more than the drum does, though it is harsh.

sentence: Motar da za ta Badun tana tashi daga tasha da misalin ƙarfe shida.
translation: The bus for Ibadan pulls out of the station at around six o'clock.

sentence: Kanina yana sayar da kayan lambu a kasuwar Badun tun bara.
translation: My younger brother has been selling vegetables in the Ibadan market since last year.

sentence: Ban taɓa zuwa Badun ba, amma abokina ya ce ana ruwa sosai a can.
translation: I have never been to Ibadan, but my friend says it rains heavily there.

sentence: Sista ta ce mu jira a waje har sai an gama tiyata.
translation: The nurse told us to wait outside until the operation was over.

sentence: Kowace safiya sista takan auna zafin jikin marasa lafiya sannan ta rubuta shi.
translation: Every morning the nurse takes the patients' temperature and then writes it down.

sentence: Muna girmama sista da ke makarantar mishan fiye da kowane malami.
translation: We respect the sister at the mission school more than any of the teachers.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan tafasa saiwar rawaya domin mu sha idan an yi zazzaɓi.
translation: My mother boils rawaya root for us to drink whenever someone comes down with a fever.

sentence: Marina suna sayen rawaya a kasuwar Kano don rina rigunan aure.
translation: The dyers buy rawaya at the Kano market to dye wedding gowns.

sentence: Kakata tana cewa rawaya ta fi kowane magani, amma ban yarda ba.
translation: My grandmother insists rawaya beats every other medicine, but I'm not convinced.

sentence: Isiyaku ya kwana a gidanmu bayan motarsa ta lalace a kan hanya.
translation: Isiyaku spent the night at our house after his car broke down on the road.

sentence: Malamin ya karanta labarin Isiyaku da mahaifinsa a coci ranar Lahadi.
translation: The teacher read the story of Isaac and his father at church on Sunday.

sentence: Ina son yadda Isiyaku ke yin haƙuri, ko da yara sun bata masa rai.
translation: I love how patient Isiyaku stays, even when the children get on his nerves.

sentence: Limam ya jinkirta sallar magariba har manoma suka dawo daga gona.
translation: The imam held the sunset prayer back until the farmers got in from the fields.

sentence: Bayan sallar Jumaʼa, limam yakan zauna ya saurari matsalolin mutanen unguwa.
translation: After Friday prayers the imam sits down and listens to the neighbourhood's troubles.

sentence: Ban gamsu da abin da limam ya faɗa game da auren wuri ba.
translation: I wasn't convinced by what the imam said about marrying young.

sentence: Da tsakar rana muna shan kindirmo da fura, don zafi ya yi yawa.
translation: At midday we drink kindirmo with fura, because the heat is just too much.

sentence: Matan Fulani sukan kawo kindirmo kasuwarmu kafin rana ta yi tsanani.
translation: The Fulani women bring kindirmo to our market before the sun turns fierce.

sentence: A gaskiya, kindirmo da Hadiza take yi ya fi na kowa daɗi.
translation: Honestly, the kindirmo Hadiza makes tastes better than anyone else's.

sentence: An gina wannan makarantar a shekara ta alif ɗari tara da hamsin.
translation: This school was built in the year nineteen fifty.

sentence: Takardar haihuwar mahaifina ta nuna an haife shi a alif ɗari tara da arbaʼin.
translation: My father's birth certificate shows that he was born in nineteen forty.

sentence: Tsofaffi suna cewa zamanin alif ɗari tara da sittin ya fi na yanzu.
translation: Old people say the nineteen-sixties were a better time than today.

sentence: Omo ya ƙare a gida, don haka ban wanke kayan yara ba.
translation: The detergent ran out at home, so I didn't wash the children's clothes.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta aike ni kasuwa in sayo omo da sabulu.
translation: My mother sent me to the market to bring back detergent and soap.

sentence: Ban gamsu da wannan omo ba, domin ba ya cire ƙazantar riga.
translation: I'm not happy with this detergent — it doesn't get the dirt out of a gown.

sentence: Kakata ta tara kuɗi shekaru uku kafin ta tafi umra a Makka.
translation: My grandmother saved up for three years before she went on umrah in Mecca.

sentence: Malaminmu ya yi umra a watan Ramadan, sai muka tarbe shi a filin jirgi.
translation: Our teacher performed umrah during Ramadan, and we went to meet him at the airport.

sentence: Umra ba wajibi ba ce kamar hajji, amma tana da lada mai yawa.
translation: Umrah isn't obligatory the way the hajj is, but it carries a great reward.

sentence: Shirwa ta sauko cikin gida ta cafke ɗan tsako a gaban yara.
translation: A kite dropped into the compound and snatched a chick right in front of the children.

sentence: A wurin suya, shirwa kan sauko ta ƙwace nama daga hannun mutane.
translation: At the suya stand, kites swoop down and grab the meat out of people's hands.

sentence: Mutane suna ƙin shirwa, amma ita ma tana neman abincin ʼyaʼyanta ne.
translation: People hate the kite, but it too is only hunting food for its chicks.

sentence: Yaron ya riƙe akala sosai kada raƙumin ya gudu cikin cunkoson kasuwa.
translation: The boy gripped the lead rope tightly so the camel wouldn't bolt into the market crowd.

sentence: Fatake sun ɗaura akala a wuyan raƙuma kafin su kama hanyar Agadez.
translation: The traders tied lead ropes round the camels' necks before setting out for Agadez.

sentence: Akala ta tsinke, sai raƙumin ya bar mu a tsakiyar hamada.
translation: The lead rope snapped, and the camel left us stranded in the middle of the desert.

sentence: Mowa ce ke dafa abincin bikin, sauran matan kuma suna taimakonta.
translation: It's the favourite wife who cooks the wedding food, and the other wives help her.

sentence: Kowa a unguwarmu ya san wace ce mowa saboda kyaututtukan da take samu.
translation: Everyone in our neighbourhood knows which one is the favourite wife, from the gifts she gets.

sentence: Uwargida ta ce ba ta jin haushin mowa, amma idonta ya nuna gaskiya.
translation: The senior wife says she bears the favourite no grudge, but her eyes tell the truth.

sentence: Kakata ta ɗaura wa jaririn laya a hannu don kariya daga cuta.
translation: My grandmother tied a Qur'anic charm on the baby's arm to protect him from illness.

sentence: Mafarautan unguwarmu suna sanya laya a wuya kafin su shiga daji.
translation: The hunters in our neighbourhood wear a charm round the neck before they go into the bush.

sentence: Wasu na ganin laya tsafi ce, wasu kuma sun tabbata ayoyin Alƙurʼani ne.
translation: Some regard the charm as juju; others are certain it is nothing but verses of the Qur'an.

sentence: Rimaye masu tsayi sun yi inuwa a hanyar da muke bi zuwa gona.
translation: Tall silk-cotton trees shade the path we take out to the farm.

sentence: Dattawan ƙauyen sukan zauna ƙarƙashin rimaye su tattauna alʼamuran gari.
translation: The village elders sit under the silk-cotton trees to talk over the town's affairs.

sentence: An sare rimaye da yawa a garinmu, yanzu babu inuwa a kasuwa.
translation: Many silk-cotton trees have been felled in our town, and now there's no shade at the market.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan soya funkaso da safe, mu ci shi da shayi mai zaƙi.
translation: My mother fries funkaso in the morning and we eat it with sweet tea.

sentence: A lokacin azumi, muna sayen funkaso da ƙosai kafin lokacin buɗa baki.
translation: During the fast we buy funkaso and bean cakes before it's time to break the fast.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ji ƙamshin funkaso sai in tuna gidan kakata.
translation: Every time I catch the smell of funkaso, I think of my grandmother's house.

sentence: Mai ruwa ya ɗaura sarka a jakinsa, yana kai ruwa gida-gida.
translation: The water seller straps the waterskin onto his donkey and delivers water house to house.

sentence: Matafiya kan cika sarka da ruwan rijiya kafin su shiga hamada.
translation: Travellers fill the waterskin from the well before they head into the desert.

sentence: Sarka ta yi yoyo, ruwan ya zube, sai muka rasa abin sha.
translation: The waterskin sprang a leak, the water drained away, and we were left with nothing to drink.

sentence: Kunama ta ɓuya cikin takalmina, sai da na kaɗa shi kafin in sanya.
translation: A scorpion was hiding in my shoe; I had to shake it out before putting it on.

sentence: Yayin da muke tsintar gyaɗa, kunama ta harbi hannun ƙanena.
translation: While we were picking groundnuts, a scorpion stung my little brother's hand.

sentence: Tun da kunama ta harbe ni, nakan girgiza barguna kafin in kwanta.
translation: Ever since a scorpion stung me, I shake out the blankets before I lie down.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta niƙa tattasai da albasa don miyar da za mu ci yau.
translation: My mother ground red peppers and onions for the stew we're eating today.

sentence: Farashin tattasai ya tashi a kasuwar Kurmi tun bayan ruwan sama.
translation: The price of red peppers has climbed at Kurmi market ever since the rains came.

sentence: Miya ba tare da tattasai ba ba ta da daɗi, in ji kakata.
translation: Stew without red peppers has no taste at all, so my grandmother says.

sentence: Iska ta buɗe tagar falo da ƙarfi, har gilashinta ya fashe.
translation: The wind flung the sitting-room window open so hard that its glass broke.

sentence: A ofishinmu, ni kaɗai nake da tebur kusa da taga mai kallon titi.
translation: At our office I'm the only one with a desk beside a window looking onto the street.

sentence: Ina kallon wata ta tagar ɗakina har sai barci ya ɗauke ni.
translation: I watch the moon through my bedroom window until sleep finally carries me off.

sentence: A ajin tarihi, malam ya ce Daular Farisa ta yi mulkin ƙasashe da yawa.
translation: In history class the teacher said the Persian Empire ruled over a great many countries.

sentence: Wani ɗan kasuwa daga Farisa ya sayar mana da kayan yaji a Kano.
translation: A trader from Persia sold us spices here in Kano.

sentence: Ina son karanta labarun tsofaffin sarakunan Farisa fiye da kowane littafi.
translation: I would rather read stories about the old kings of Persia than any other book.

sentence: Kyaftin ɗin ya umarci sojoji su tsaya a ƙofar barikin har safe.
translation: The captain ordered the soldiers to stand at the barracks gate until morning.

sentence: Kanena ya zama kyaftin bayan shekaru goma a rundunar sojin ƙasa.
translation: My younger brother made captain after ten years in the army.

sentence: Mun fi son sabon kyaftin ɗin, domin yana sauraron korafin sojoji.
translation: We prefer the new captain, because he actually listens to the soldiers' complaints.

sentence: Ɗana ya yi kissa da abokinsa don su fita ba tare da izina ba.
translation: My son and his friend cooked up a scheme to slip out without my permission.

sentence: Sun yi wa shugaban ƙungiyar kissa har aka kore shi daga muƙaminsa.
translation: They schemed against the association's chairman until he was driven out of his post.

sentence: Ya sami wannan aiki ne da kissa, ba don ya cancanta ba.
translation: He got this job through underhand dealing, not because he deserved it.

sentence: Mun shafa fenti mai launin yalo a bangon falo, sai ɗakin ya haskaka.
translation: We painted the sitting-room wall yellow, and the whole room brightened up.

sentence: Duk motocin haya na garinmu yalo ne, don haka baƙi ba sa ɓacewa.
translation: Every taxi in our town is yellow, so visitors never get lost.

sentence: Ba na son rigar yalo, amma ƙanwata ta ce tana ƙayatarwa.
translation: I don't like the yellow gown, but my little sister says it's lovely.

sentence: Kakanmu ya bar mana gandu mai faɗi a bayan ƙauyen, muna nomansa tare.
translation: Our grandfather left us a wide family farm behind the village, and we work it together.

sentence: Da sassafe mukan tafi gandu don shuka gero kafin rana ta yi zafi.
translation: At first light we head out to the family farm to plant millet before the sun turns hot.

sentence: A ganina, gandu ya fi aikin ofis daraja, domin abinci daga ƙasa yake.
translation: To my mind a family farm is worth more than an office job, since food comes out of the ground.

sentence: Saratu ta dafa tuwon shinkafa kafin mahaifinta ya dawo daga masallaci.
translation: Sarah cooked rice tuwo before her father got back from the mosque.

sentence: Saratu ce ta fi kowa maki a jarabawar lissafi a ajinmu.
translation: It was Sarah who scored higher than anyone else in our class's maths exam.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda Saratu take yin haƙuri da surukarta duk da maganganu.
translation: I'm amazed at how patiently Sarah puts up with her mother-in-law, whatever people say.

sentence: Mun je wurin shehi don ya yi mana adduʼa kafin tafiyar hajji.
translation: We went to the sheikh so that he would pray for us before the hajj journey.

sentence: Kowace Alhamis, shehi yakan koyar da tafsiri a babban masallacin unguwarmu.
translation: Every Thursday the sheikh teaches Qur'anic exegesis at our neighbourhood's main mosque.

sentence: Maganar shehi ta kwantar min da hankali fiye da duk shawarar da na samu.
translation: The sheikh's words settled my mind more than any advice I had been given.

sentence: Manomin ya zana shaci a tsakanin gonarsa da ta maƙwabcinsa don gujewa husuma.
translation: The farmer drew a boundary line between his field and his neighbour's to head off a quarrel.

sentence: ʼYan sanda sun yi shaci a kan hanya don direbobi su rage gudu.
translation: The police marked out a zone on the road so that drivers would slow down.

sentence: Ruwan sama ya share shaci da muka yi, yanzu ba mu san iyaka ba.
translation: The rain washed away the line we had marked, and now we don't know where the boundary runs.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifiyata takan sayi ayaba a kasuwar Sabon Gari.
translation: Every morning my mother buys bananas at the Sabon Gari market.

sentence: Matan da ke sayar da ayaba a tashar mota sun ƙi rage farashi.
translation: The women selling bananas at the motor park refused to bring the price down.

sentence: Ban taɓa cin ayaba mai zaƙi irin wannan ba tun ina yaro.
translation: I have not eaten a banana this sweet since I was a boy.

sentence: Yayata tana aiki a wani asibiti a Abeokuta tun bara.
translation: My older sister has been working at a hospital in Abeokuta since last year.

sentence: Mun sha wahalar hanya kwana biyu kafin mu isa Abeokuta daga Kano.
translation: We endured two nights of hard travelling before we reached Abeokuta from Kano.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ziyarci Abeokuta, sai in ji daɗin sanyin safiyarta.
translation: Whenever I visit Abeokuta, I savour the coolness of its mornings.

sentence: Kafin ya fara karatu, malamin ya nemi tsari daga sharrin Iblis.
translation: Before starting the lesson, the teacher sought protection from the evil of Satan.

sentence: Kakata takan ce mana Iblis yana nan a duk inda ake yin husuma.
translation: My grandmother used to tell us that Satan is present wherever people quarrel.

sentence: Ba na jin Iblis ne ke da laifin kowane mugun aiki da muke yi.
translation: I do not think Satan is to blame for every wicked thing we do.

sentence: Ƙanena yakan yi mini tsokana har sai na fusata, sannan ya gudu.
translation: My little brother provokes me until I lose my temper, and then he runs off.

sentence: Na yi shiru a taron, don na san maganarsa tsokana ce kawai.
translation: I kept quiet at the meeting, because I knew his remark was only a provocation.

sentence: Na yi haƙuri da yawa, amma tsokanar da yake yi mini ta wuce misali.
translation: I have been very patient, but the way he provokes me has gone past all bounds.

sentence: Miyar da muka bari a kan tebur ta yi wari gum kafin safiya.
translation: The soup we left out on the table had turned rank and foul by morning.

sentence: Direban ya buɗe tagogin motar don kifin da muke ɗauka yana wari gum.
translation: The driver opened the car windows because the fish we were carrying stank.

sentence: Rigar da ya kwana da ita tana wari gum, na ƙi taɓa ta.
translation: The shirt he slept in reeks of must, and I refused to touch it.

sentence: Tun da ya gina babban gida, gadara ta shiga tsakaninsa da maƙwabta.
translation: Ever since he built the big house, moneyed arrogance has come between him and the neighbours.

sentence: Malamin ya yi huɗuba kan yadda gadara ke ɓata zumuncin ƴan uwa.
translation: The preacher gave a sermon on how the arrogance of wealth destroys family ties.

sentence: Ba na son zama da shi tun da arziki ya kawo masa gadara.
translation: I no longer enjoy his company, now that wealth has made him haughty.

sentence: Da sassafe mun ga barewa tana kiwo a gefen hanyar Gusau.
translation: At first light we saw a gazelle grazing beside the Gusau road.

sentence: Mafarauta sun ce barewa ta fi kowace dabba saurin gudu a jeji.
translation: The hunters said the gazelle outruns every other animal in the bush.

sentence: Kallon barewa tana tsalle a fili ya fi kowane hoto daɗi a gare ni.
translation: Watching a gazelle bound across open ground pleases me more than any photograph.

sentence: Zomo ya shiga gonarmu da dare, ya cinye kabejin da muka shuka.
translation: A hare got into our farm at night and ate up the cabbage we had planted.

sentence: A tatsuniyar Hausa, zomo yakan yaudari kura da wayonsa kafin ta cinye shi.
translation: In Hausa folktales the hare outwits the hyena with his cunning before she can eat him.

sentence: Yara sun yi ta dariya lokacin da zomo ya tsere daga hannun kakansu.
translation: The children laughed and laughed when the hare wriggled out of their grandfather's hands.

sentence: Sabon maƙwabcinmu Basakkwace ne, kuma karin harshensa ya bambanta da namu.
translation: Our new neighbour is a Sokoto man, and his dialect is different from ours.

sentence: Wani Basakkwace ne ya sayar mana da shanun nan a kasuwar Wurno.
translation: It was a man from Sokoto who sold us these cattle at the Wurno market.

sentence: Ni Basakkwace ne, amma tun shekara goma ina zaune a Legas ina kewar gida.
translation: I am a Sokoto man, but I have lived in Lagos for ten years, missing home.

sentence: Ɗan uwana ya kammala karatun likitanci a Yunan kafin ya dawo Kaduna.
translation: My brother finished his medical studies in Greece before coming back to Kaduna.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya nuna mana yadda falsafar Yunan ta shafi ilimin Larabawa.
translation: The history teacher showed us how Greek philosophy shaped Arab scholarship.

sentence: Ina fatan wata rana zan ziyarci tsibiran Yunan da nake gani a talabijin.
translation: I hope that one day I will visit the Greek islands I see on television.

sentence: Iyayen amarya sun rage sadaki domin ango ɗalibi ne mai ƙaramin albashi.
translation: The bride's parents lowered the bride price because the groom is a student earning very little.

sentence: A ranar daurin aure, liman ya karɓi sadaki naira dubu hamsin a masallaci.
translation: On the day the marriage was contracted, the imam received a bride price of fifty thousand naira at the mosque.

sentence: Ina ganin sadaki ya zama nauyi ga samari maimakon albarka ga iyalai.
translation: I think the bride price has turned into a burden on young men instead of a blessing for families.

sentence: Ƙaramin yaro ya hau mumbari kafin salla, sai limami ya sauke shi.
translation: A little boy climbed up onto the pulpit before the prayer, so the imam lifted him down.

sentence: A ranar Jumaʼa, limami ya hau mumbari ya yi huɗuba kan zaman lafiya.
translation: On Friday the imam went up the minbar and preached a sermon about living in peace.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na tsaya kusa da mumbari, zuciyata takan yi sanyi.
translation: Whenever I stand near the minbar, my heart settles and grows calm.

sentence: Bayan makaranta, yaran sun shafe yini suna sarara a cikin unguwa.
translation: After school the children spent the whole day drifting around the neighbourhood with nothing to do.

sentence: Maimakon neman aiki, ɗan uwansa yana sarara a kasuwa kowace safiya.
translation: Instead of looking for work, his brother wanders aimlessly around the market every morning.

sentence: Mahaifina ya gargaɗe ni kan sarara, ya ce lokaci ba ya jiran kowa.
translation: My father warned me about idling about, saying that time waits for nobody.

sentence: Ɗan uwana yana karatun likitanci a Maroko, yana dawowa Kano kowace shekara.
translation: My brother is studying medicine in Morocco, and he comes home to Kano every year.

sentence: Innata ta dawo daga Maroko da shayin naʼana da wasu kayan ƙamshi.
translation: My mother came back from Morocco with mint tea and some perfumes.

sentence: Muna zaune a gidan shayi muna kallon Maroko, sai wutar lantarki ta tafi.
translation: We were sitting in the tea shop watching Morocco play when the power went out.

sentence: Mun shiga cikin kurmi don neman itacen wuta kafin ruwa ya sauka.
translation: We went into the forest to gather firewood before the rain came down.

sentence: Mafarauta sun ce birai sun bar kurmi tun da aka sare bishiyoyi.
translation: The hunters say the monkeys abandoned the forest once the trees were cut down.

sentence: Ina tsoron shiga kurmi da daddare, domin muryar kuraye takan tsorata ni.
translation: I am afraid to go into the forest at night, because the sound of hyenas frightens me.

sentence: A bikin auren ƙanwata, maroƙi ya kaɗa kukuma har tsakar dare.
translation: At my younger sister's wedding a praise singer played the kukuma fiddle until midnight.

sentence: Kakana yakan kaɗa kukuma a farfajiya har yaran unguwa su taru.
translation: My grandfather plays his one-stringed fiddle in the courtyard until the neighbourhood children gather round.

sentence: Sautin kukuma yana tuna min da bukukuwan ƙauye lokacin da nake yaro.
translation: The sound of the kukuma reminds me of village celebrations back when I was a boy.

sentence: Bayan ʼyaʼya mata huɗu, Allah ya ba su ɗa namiji a bana.
translation: After four daughters, they were finally granted a son this year.

sentence: A ƙauyenmu, ɗa ɗaya tilo yakan gaji gonar mahaifinsa gaba ɗaya.
translation: In our village an only son inherits the whole of his father's farm.

sentence: Ba ni da ɗa namiji, amma ʼyata ta fi kowa kula da ni.
translation: I have no son, but my daughter looks after me better than anyone else.

sentence: Sabuwar manhaja ta zo da darussan kwamfuta tun daga aji uku.
translation: The new syllabus brings in computer lessons right from primary three.

sentence: Na duba manhaja kafin in sayi littattafan ɗana na sabuwar shekara.
translation: I looked through the syllabus before buying my son's books for the new school year.

sentence: Malamai suna korafin cewa manhaja ta yi yawa, lokacin karatu kuma ya ƙaranta.
translation: The teachers complain that the syllabus is overcrowded while teaching time has been cut short.

sentence: Ɗan kasuwa ya cika sito da buhunan shinkafa kafin farashin ya tashi.
translation: The trader filled the storeroom with sacks of rice before the price went up.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta ce in kwaso gero daga sito kafin ruwan sama ya sauka.
translation: My mother told me to bring the millet in from the storeroom before the rain fell.

sentence: Beraye sun lalata hatsin da ke cikin sito, abin ya ɓata mana rai.
translation: Rats ruined the grain inside the storeroom, and the whole thing left us heartsick.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifiyata takan soya fanke mu ci kafin mu tafi makaranta.
translation: Every morning my mother fries fanke cakes for us to eat before we leave for school.

sentence: Matan unguwa suna sayar da fanke a gefen hanya kafin a karya azumi.
translation: The neighbourhood women sell fanke by the roadside just before the fast is broken.

sentence: Ban taɓa cin fanke mai zaƙi irin na kasuwar Sabon Gari ba.
translation: I have never eaten fanke as sweet as the ones sold at Sabon Gari market.

sentence: Kakana ya yi aikin dogari a fadar Kano tsawon shekara talatin.
translation: My grandfather served as an emir's guard at the Kano palace for thirty years.

sentence: Dogarin sarki ya hana mu shiga har sai an gama majalisa.
translation: The emir's guard would not let us in until the council had finished.

sentence: Kowane yaro a unguwarmu yana son ya zama dogari sa'ad da ya girma.
translation: Every boy in our neighbourhood wants to be one of the emir's guards when he grows up.

sentence: Katifar da muka saya ta yi tsada, amma tana da laushi ƙwarai.
translation: The mattress we bought was expensive, but it is wonderfully soft.

sentence: Mun ɗauki katifa zuwa rufin gida don mu kwana a sanyi.
translation: We carried a mattress up to the roof so we could sleep in the cool air.

sentence: Ban iya barci ba domin tsohuwar katifa tana sa min ciwon baya.
translation: I couldn't sleep, because the old mattress leaves me with a sore back.

sentence: Ƙwan jimina ɗaya ya ishe mu duka a karin kumallo.
translation: A single ostrich egg was enough breakfast for all of us.

sentence: Malamin makaranta ya gaya mana cewa jimina ba ta iya tashi sama.
translation: Our schoolteacher told us that an ostrich cannot fly.

sentence: Na yi mamaki lokacin da na ga girman ƙafafun jimina a gidan namun daji.
translation: I was astonished when I saw how huge an ostrich's legs are at the wildlife park.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta shafa mini aidin a raunin da na ji a gwiwa.
translation: My mother dabbed iodine on the cut I got on my knee.

sentence: Likita ya ce mu sayi aidin da bandeji kafin mu koma gida.
translation: The doctor told us to buy iodine and bandages before we headed home.

sentence: Aidin yana ƙuna sosai, amma ƙanwata ba ta yi kuka ba ko kaɗan.
translation: Iodine stings badly, yet my little sister did not cry at all.

sentence: Ɗan'uwana ya kanne ido ɗaya kafin ya harbi tsuntsu da majajjawa.
translation: My brother shut one eye before shooting at the bird with his slingshot.

sentence: Kawuna ya kanne mini ido, sai na san bai yarda da labarin ba.
translation: My uncle winked at me, and I knew at once he didn't believe the story.

sentence: Ban so ya rinƙa kanne mini ido a gaban baƙi ba.
translation: I didn't like him winking at me in front of the guests.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta zuba alabo cikin ruwan zafi tana tuƙawa har tuwo ya nuna.
translation: My mother poured the cassava flour into boiling water and stirred until the tuwo was done.

sentence: Mun sayi buhun alabo a kasuwa domin bikin aurenmu na gobe.
translation: We bought a sack of cassava flour at the market for our wedding tomorrow.

sentence: Ba na son tuwon alabo, amma kakata ta ce yana da amfani.
translation: I don't like tuwo made from cassava flour, but my grandmother says it does you good.

sentence: Ruwan sama ya kwarara ta cikin silin har ya jiƙe katifarmu.
translation: The rain leaked through the ceiling and soaked our mattress.

sentence: Kafinta ya hau kan tebur don ya gyara silin ɗakin kwana.
translation: The carpenter climbed onto the table to repair the bedroom ceiling.

sentence: Na kwanta ina kallon ƙadangare yana tafiya a silin har barci ya ɗauke ni.
translation: I lay watching a lizard cross the ceiling until sleep took me.

sentence: Wannan mawaƙi mashahuri ne har yara a ƙauyenmu suna rera waƙarsa.
translation: This singer is so famous that even the children in our village sing his song.

sentence: Wani marubuci mashahuri zai ziyarci makarantarmu ranar Litinin mai zuwa.
translation: A famous writer is coming to visit our school next Monday.

sentence: Ban damu da ya zama mashahuri ba, ina son ya ci gaba da karatu.
translation: I don't care that he has become famous; I want him to stay in school.

sentence: Kowace safiya matan ƙauyen sukan je gulbi domin wanke kaya.
translation: Every morning the women of the village go down to the river to wash clothes.

sentence: Gulbin ya cika har ya rufe hanyar da muke bi zuwa kasuwa.
translation: The river rose until it swallowed the road we take to the market.

sentence: Ina kewar wasanninmu a gulbi lokacin damina, kafin mu bar ƙauyen.
translation: I miss the games we played at the river in the rainy season, before we left the village.

sentence: Malami ya bayyana yadda Najeriya ta canza daga fam zuwa naira.
translation: The teacher explained how Nigeria switched from the pound to the naira.

sentence: Ɗan'uwana da ke Landan ya aiko mana fam ɗari biyu don gyaran rufi.
translation: My brother in London sent us two hundred pounds to fix the roof.

sentence: Na yi mamaki da ganin tsoffin kuɗin fam a cikin akwatin kakata.
translation: I was amazed to find old pound notes inside my grandmother's chest.

sentence: Kifin da muka manta a kicin ya yi wari sum tun da safe.
translation: The fish we forgot in the kitchen has been stinking since morning.

sentence: Bayan ruwan sama, magudanar ruwa a kasuwarmu tana wari sum.
translation: After the rain, the drainage ditch in our market reeks.

sentence: Na ƙi cin miyar, don ta yi wari sum tun jiya da yamma.
translation: I refused to eat the stew, because it has smelled foul since yesterday evening.

sentence: Kakata ta sayar da gonarta domin ta biya kuɗin haji bana.
translation: My grandmother sold her farm so that she could pay for the hajj this year.

sentence: Mun raka mahaifina zuwa filin jirgin sama sa'ad da ya tafi haji.
translation: We saw my father off at the airport when he left for the hajj.

sentence: Tun ina yaro nake mafarkin zuwa haji, amma har yanzu ban samu ba.
translation: Since I was a boy I have dreamed of going on hajj, but I still have not managed it.

sentence: Kakana ya taɓa tafiya da ayari daga Kano zuwa Agadas domin sayar da gishiri.
translation: My grandfather once travelled with a caravan from Kano to Agadez to sell salt.

sentence: Ayarin fatake ya sauka a garinmu da yamma, suka nemi masauki.
translation: The traders' caravan halted in our town in the evening and looked for lodging.

sentence: Na fi son yin tafiya cikin ayari, don hanyarmu tana da 'yan fashi.
translation: I would rather travel in a group, because our road has bandits on it.

sentence: Yaron nan ya wuce haddi, yana wa manyansa magana kamar tsara.
translation: That boy has gone past the limit — he talks to his elders as if they were his age-mates.

sentence: Malamin ya ce ba a zartar da haddi sai shaidu huɗu sun tabbata.
translation: The teacher said the prescribed punishment is not carried out unless four witnesses confirm it.

sentence: Ina jin tsoron ƙetare haddin Allah, don haka na bar wannan aikin.
translation: I am afraid of overstepping God's limits, so I gave up that job.

sentence: Mushe Ibrahim ya zo daga Yamai, yana neman ɗakin haya kusa da kasuwa.
translation: Mr Ibrahim has come from Niamey and is looking for a room to rent near the market.

sentence: Mai gadi ya tare ni yana cewa, Mushe, ka nuna takardar izininka.
translation: The guard stopped me, saying: mister, show me your permit.

sentence: Ba na son a kira ni Mushe; sunana Sani, kuma ni ɗan gari ne.
translation: I don't like being called mister; my name is Sani, and I'm a local.

sentence: Kowace safiya nakan kai 'ya'yana makarantar Muhammadiyya kafin in tafi aiki.
translation: Every morning I drop my children at the Islamic school before I head to work.

sentence: Malamin Muhammadiyya ya raba wa yara allunan rubutu a ƙarƙashin bishiyar kuka.
translation: The Islamic-studies teacher handed out writing boards to the children under the baobab tree.

sentence: Karatun Muhammadiyya ya fi sauƙi a gare ni fiye da lissafi na boko.
translation: Islamic studies come easier to me than arithmetic at the Western school.

sentence: Da kyar na gusa gefe kafin babbar mota ta wuce a kunkuntar hanya.
translation: I barely moved aside before the lorry went past on the narrow road.

sentence: Matar ta ce mini in gusa don ta samu wurin zama a bas.
translation: The woman asked me to shift over so she could find a seat on the bus.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na zauna kusa da shi, sai ya gusa kamar ina wari.
translation: Every time I sit down beside him he edges away, as though I smelled.

sentence: Ina wanke kwano sai na ji kwaram, tukunyar ta faɗi daga kan tebur.
translation: I was washing dishes when I heard a thud — the pot had fallen off the table.

sentence: Muna cikin hira a majalisa sai wani baƙo ya shigo kwaram.
translation: We were chatting out in the front room when a stranger suddenly walked straight in.

sentence: Zuciyata ta yi tsalle sa'ad da iska ta buga ƙofar kwaram da tsakar dare.
translation: My heart jumped when the wind banged the door shut at midnight.

sentence: Dogarai sanye da jajayen riguna sun tsaya a ƙofar fadar Sarki.
translation: The emir's guards, dressed in red gowns, were standing at the palace gate.

sentence: Dogarai sun tare hanyarmu, muka jira har mahayan dawakai suka wuce.
translation: The emir's guards blocked our road, and we waited until the horsemen had gone by.

sentence: Kakana ya kasance ɗaya daga cikin dogarai, muna alfahari da shi har yau.
translation: My grandfather was one of the emir's guards, and we are proud of him to this day.

sentence: Ɗana ya sha kunu har cikinsa ya cika tatul, bai ci abinci ba.
translation: My son drank so much gruel that he was full to the brim and ate no food.

sentence: A wurin bikin aure, yara sun sha lemo har suka cika tatul.
translation: At the wedding the children drank soft drinks until they were completely bloated.

sentence: Jiya na sha nono har na cika tatul, yau kuwa ina jin nadama.
translation: Yesterday I drank sour milk until I was stuffed full, and today I regret it.

sentence: Mun kai yara gidan namun daji domin su ga mariri a karon farko.
