translation: We took the children to the zoo so they could see a scimitar-horned oryx for the first time.

sentence: Masu tsaron daji sun ce ba a ganin mariri a hamada tun shekaru talatin.
translation: The forest rangers say no oryx has been sighted in the desert for thirty years.

sentence: Kakana yakan ba mu labarin mariri da ya gani a hamada tun yana yaro.
translation: My grandfather likes to tell us about the oryx he saw out in the desert when he was a boy.

sentence: Malamin ya ce mu rubuta dukkan amsoshin a cikin sabon daftari kafin gobe.
translation: The teacher told us to write all the answers in a new notebook before tomorrow.

sentence: Mai shagon ya buɗe daftari, ya nuna mini bashin da na yi watan jiya.
translation: The shopkeeper opened his ledger and showed me the debt I ran up last month.

sentence: A ajinmu, ban taba ganin daftari mai tsafta kamar na Aisha ba.
translation: In our class I have never seen a notebook as neat as Aisha's.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta kawo tire cike da shayi da biskit ga baƙinmu.
translation: My mother brought in a tray loaded with tea and biscuits for our guests.

sentence: Hauwa ta ɗora tire a kanta ta nufi kasuwa tana kiran masu saya.
translation: Hauwa balanced the tray on her head and set off for the market, calling out to buyers.

sentence: Yaron ya zubar da tire a bikin auren, kunya ta kama shi sosai.
translation: The boy dropped the tray at the wedding and was overcome with embarrassment.

sentence: Mun tashi da asuba domin mu kai kayan gona kasuwar Soba.
translation: We set out at dawn to take the farm produce to the market at Soba.

sentence: Yawancin mutanen Soba manoma ne da ke noman masara da dawa.
translation: Most of the people of Soba are farmers who grow maize and guinea corn.

sentence: Kawata ta koma Soba bayan aure, tun daga lokacin ban gan ta ba.
translation: My friend moved to Soba after she married, and I haven't seen her since.

sentence: Usaina ta gama girki kafin mahaifinta ya dawo daga masallaci.
translation: Usaina had finished the cooking before her father got back from the mosque.

sentence: Malamin ya yaba wa Usaina saboda ta fi kowa a jarrabawar lissafi.
translation: The teacher praised Usaina because she outdid everyone in the maths exam.

sentence: Usaina tana fushi da ni har yau, saboda na yi mata dariya a bikin.
translation: Usaina is still angry with me to this day because I laughed at her at the party.

sentence: Kakata ba ta iya tauna nama tun da haƙoranta suka fara zubewa.
translation: My grandmother can't chew meat any more, now that her teeth have started falling out.

sentence: Tsofaffi suna zaune a ƙarƙashin bishiya suna tauna goro suna hira.
translation: The old men sit under the tree chewing kola nuts and chatting.

sentence: Likita ya gargaɗe ni cewa in tauna abinci sannu-sannu don kada in shaƙe.
translation: The doctor warned me to chew my food slowly so that I wouldn't choke.

sentence: Yayata ta dafa acca da miyar kuka don baƙin da suka sauka jiya.
translation: My elder sister cooked fonio with baobab-leaf soup for the guests who arrived yesterday.

sentence: A kasuwar Jos, ana sayar da acca a buhu kamar shinkafa.
translation: At the Jos market they sell fonio by the sack, just like rice.

sentence: Ban taba jin daɗin acca ba sai da na ci ta a gidan kawuna.
translation: I never liked fonio until the day I ate it at my uncle's house.

sentence: Wandon da aka saya mini gajere ne, sai da na mayar da shi shagon.
translation: The trousers they bought me were short, so I had to take them back to the shop.

sentence: Ɗan uwana gajere ne, amma shi ne ya fi kowa ƙwarewa a ƙwallon kwando.
translation: My brother is short, but he is the most skilful player on the basketball team.

sentence: Lokacin hutu ya yi gajere ƙwarai, ban ma isa gidan kakata ba.
translation: The holiday was far too short — I didn't even make it to my grandmother's house.

sentence: Jaririn ya yi tutu a kan tabarma, sai mahaifiyarsa ta wanke shi nan take.
translation: The baby pooped on the mat, so his mother washed him straight away.

sentence: Idan kana son yin tutu, ka gaya mini don kada ka ɓata kayanka.
translation: If you need to poop, tell me, so that you don't soil your clothes.

sentence: Yaya ta yi fushi don ƙaramin yaron ya yi tutu a cikin sabuwar motarta.
translation: My elder sister was furious because the little boy pooped inside her new car.

sentence: Ban taba fahimtar nahawu sosai ba, shi ya sa na faɗi jarrabawar Larabci.
translation: I never really understood grammar, and that is why I failed the Arabic exam.

sentence: Malamin makarantar allo yana koya mana nahawu kowace safiya bayan sallar asuba.
translation: The Qur'anic school teacher teaches us grammar every morning after the dawn prayer.

sentence: Nahawu ya fi lissafi wahala a gare ni, amma ina ƙoƙarin koyonsa.
translation: Grammar is harder for me than maths, but I keep trying to learn it.

sentence: Mahaifina ya sanya kaidi kan lokacin da muke kallon talabijin da dare.
translation: My father set a limit on how long we may watch television at night.

sentence: Hukumar kasuwa ta kafa sabon kaidi kan farashin hatsi a Kano.
translation: The market authority has imposed a new restriction on grain prices in Kano.

sentence: Wannan kaidi ya wuce gona da iri, kuma ɗalibai da yawa suna yin korafi.
translation: This restriction goes far too far, and a lot of students are complaining about it.

sentence: Bayan ruwan sama, kandamin da ke bayan gidanmu ya cika da bado.
translation: After the rains, the pond behind our house filled up with water lilies.

sentence: Masunta suna fama da bado da ya toshe hanyar jirginsu a kogin Neja.
translation: The fishermen are struggling with water lilies that have blocked their boat's way on the Niger.

sentence: Furen bado yana da kyau sosai, amma sauro yana yawaita a wurin.
translation: The water lily's flower is lovely, but mosquitoes multiply wherever it grows.

sentence: Kakana ya kulle hatsin bara a taska, ba ya barin kowa ya shiga.
translation: My grandfather has locked last year's grain in his private room, and he lets nobody in.

sentence: Mahaifina yakan kira mu cikin taska duk lokacin da muka yi laifi.
translation: My father calls us into his own room whenever we have done something wrong.

sentence: Ban taɓa shiga taska ba tun bayan rasuwar mahaifina, kuma ina jin tsoro.
translation: I have never set foot in his room since my father died, and it still frightens me.

sentence: Na sa satifiket a cikin jaka don kada ruwan sama ya jiƙa shi.
translation: I put the certificate inside a bag so that the rain would not soak it.

sentence: Sun ce ba za su ɗauke ni aiki ba sai na kawo satifiket.
translation: They said they would not hire me until I brought the certificate.

sentence: Ina alfahari da satifiket ɗin da na samu bayan shekaru uku na wahala.
translation: I am proud of the certificate I earned after three hard years.

sentence: Mun sauka a Lakwaja da tsakar dare saboda motar ta lalace a hanya.
translation: We stopped in Lokoja in the middle of the night because the car broke down on the road.

sentence: Kogin Neja da Benuwai suna haɗuwa a Lakwaja, kuma jiragen ruwa na tsayawa can.
translation: The Niger and the Benue meet at Lokoja, and the boats dock there.

sentence: Zafin Lakwaja ya fi na Kano, don haka ban daɗe a can ba.
translation: The heat in Lokoja is worse than Kano's, so I did not stay there long.

sentence: Karen maƙwabcinmu ya sace ƙashi daga tukunyar da muka bari a waje.
translation: Our neighbour's dog stole a bone out of the pot we had left outside.

sentence: Yaron ya faɗi daga bishiyar mangwaro, sai likita ya ce ƙashi ya karye.
translation: The boy fell out of the mango tree, and the doctor said a bone was broken.

sentence: Naman nan duk ƙashi ne, na ji haushin kuɗin da na biya.
translation: This meat is nothing but bone; I resent the money I paid for it.

sentence: Kakana yakan saurari labarin yaƙin Bosniya a rediyo lokacin da nake ƙarami.
translation: My grandfather used to listen to news of the Bosnian war on the radio when I was little.

sentence: Ƙanena yana karatun likitanci a Bosniya, yana kiran mu ta waya duk mako.
translation: My younger brother is studying medicine in Bosnia, and he phones us every week.

sentence: Ban taɓa zuwa Bosniya ba, amma ina son ganin tsofaffin masallatan da ke can.
translation: I have never been to Bosnia, but I would love to see the old mosques there.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifiyata takan soya akara ta sayar wa maƙwabta a gaban gidanmu.
translation: Every morning my mother fries bean cakes and sells them to the neighbours in front of our house.

sentence: Muna sayen akara a kan hanya kafin mu shiga aji da safe.
translation: We buy bean cakes on the way before we go into class in the morning.

sentence: Ban ci akara ba tun da likita ya ce in guji soyayyen abinci.
translation: I have not eaten a bean cake since the doctor told me to keep off fried food.

sentence: Na sayi sabon soso a kasuwa a makon jiya domin tsohon ya tsage.
translation: I bought a new loofah at the market last week because the old one had split.

sentence: Kakata takan yi wa jikokinta wanka da soso mai laushi kowace maraice.
translation: My grandmother bathes her grandchildren with a soft sponge every evening.

sentence: Ba na jin jikina ya yi tsafta idan ban yi wanka da soso ba.
translation: I never feel properly clean unless I have scrubbed myself with a loofah.

sentence: Kyanwa ta shiga kicin da dare ta zubar da miyar da muka ajiye.
translation: The cat got into the kitchen at night and knocked over the stew we had put away.

sentence: Maƙwabciyarmu tana ciyar da kyanwa kifi duk lokacin da ta dawo daga kasuwa.
translation: Our neighbour feeds the cat fish every time she gets back from the market.

sentence: Yarinyar tana kuka domin kyanwa ta ɓace tun ranar Asabar da safe.
translation: The little girl is crying because the cat has been missing since Saturday morning.

sentence: Duk lokacin da kakata ta dawo daga kasuwa, takan kawo mana hasafi.
translation: Every time my grandmother comes back from the market she brings us a little gift.

sentence: Bayan direban ya kai mu gida cikin ruwan sama, mun ba shi hasafi.
translation: After the driver got us home through the rain, we gave him a small gift.

sentence: Ko da hasafi ne kawai, na ajiye shi a kan teburina har yau.
translation: Even though it was only a small gift, I have kept it on my desk to this day.

sentence: Kakana yakan naɗa farin rawani duk ranar Jumaʼa kafin ya tafi masallaci.
translation: My grandfather winds a white turban every Friday before he sets off for the mosque.

sentence: A ranar naɗin sarauta, sabon hakimi ya sa rawani mai launin shuɗi.
translation: On the day of his installation the new district head wore a blue turban.

sentence: Ina ganin rawani ya fi kowace hula daraja a idon manyan gari.
translation: To my mind a turban carries more dignity than any cap in the eyes of the town elders.

sentence: Makiyayi ya kori shanunsa zuwa rafi tun kafin rana ta fito.
translation: The herder drove his cattle down to the stream before the sun was even up.

sentence: Alƙalin gari ya sasanta makiyayi da manomi bayan shanunsa sun shiga gonar dawa.
translation: The town judge reconciled a herder and a farmer after the herder's cattle got into the sorghum field.

sentence: Na yi mamakin yadda makiyayi ya san kowace akuya a garkensa.
translation: I was amazed at how the herder knew every single goat in his herd.

sentence: Kafin ta amince da auren, ta yi istihara har dare uku a jere.
translation: Before she agreed to the marriage she prayed istikhara three nights running.

sentence: Malam ya shawarce ni da in yi istihara kafin in karɓi aikin Legas.
translation: The malam advised me to pray istikhara before I accepted the job in Lagos.

sentence: Bayan na yi istihara, zuciyata ta kwanta kuma na daina jin tsoron tafiyar.
translation: After I prayed istikhara my heart settled and I stopped dreading the journey.

sentence: Alfadari ya ɗauki buhunan gishiri har ƙauyen da ke bayan tsauni.
translation: The mule carried the sacks of salt all the way to the village behind the hill.

sentence: A kasuwar Kano, na sayi alfadari mai ƙarfi don jigilar kayan gona.
translation: At the Kano market I bought a strong mule for hauling produce from the farm.

sentence: Alfadari ya fi doki haƙuri a hanya, amma taurin kansa yakan ba ni haushi.
translation: A mule outlasts a horse on the road, but its stubbornness drives me mad.

sentence: Manajan ya nuna wa maʼaikatansa tasku har suka bar kamfanin gaba ɗaya.
translation: The manager treated his workers with such cruelty that they all walked out of the company.

sentence: Kar ka yi wa jakinka tasku, don shi ma halitta ne mai jin zafi.
translation: Don't be cruel to your donkey; it too is a creature that feels pain.

sentence: Tasku ba ya kawo albarka; sarkin da ya zalunci talakawansa ba ya daɗewa.
translation: Cruelty brings no blessing; a ruler who oppresses his subjects does not last long.

sentence: Kakata takan nika ƙwayar guna ta dafa miya mai daɗi ga jikokinta.
translation: My grandmother grinds guna melon seeds and cooks a tasty soup for her grandchildren.

sentence: Manoma sun kwaso guna daga gona suka kai kasuwar Gwarzo da safe.
translation: The farmers gathered the guna melons from the field and took them to Gwarzo market at dawn.

sentence: Na ciji guna ina tsammanin kankana ce, sai bakina ya cika da ɗaci.
translation: I bit into a guna melon thinking it was a watermelon, and my mouth filled with bitterness.

sentence: Malamin ya bayyana cewa an saukar da Attaura ga Annabi Musa a Dutsen Sina.
translation: The teacher explained that the Torah was sent down to the Prophet Musa on Mount Sinai.

sentence: A ɗakin karatun jamiʼa, na sami tsohuwar Attaura da aka rubuta da Ibrananci.
translation: In the university library I came across an old Torah written in Hebrew.

sentence: Ina son karanta Attaura domin in fahimci labaran annabawa da muka koya tun ƙuruciya.
translation: I want to read the Torah so that I can understand the prophets' stories we learned as children.

sentence: Yara suna wasan karta a ƙarƙashin bishiya, sai Musa ya fitar da kos.
translation: The children were playing cards under the tree when Musa brought out the trump.

sentence: Lauyan ya ajiye shaidarsa ta ƙarshe kamar kos har ranar shariʼa ta zo.
translation: The lawyer saved his last witness like a trump card until the day of the trial.

sentence: Kullum ina ganin zan yi nasara, sai kakana ya buga kos ya ci wasan.
translation: Every time I think I am about to win, my grandfather plays a trump and takes the game.

sentence: Mantawa da kashe wutar lantarki ya zama sila ga gobarar da ta ci kicin.
translation: Forgetting to switch off the electricity was the cause of the fire that gutted the kitchen.

sentence: Rashin biyan albashi tsawon wata uku ya zama sila ta yajin aikin malamai.
translation: Three months of unpaid salaries became the cause of the teachers' strike.

sentence: Maƙwabciyata ce sila ta samun wannan aiki, ba zan taɓa mantawa ba.
translation: My neighbour is the reason I got this job, and I will never forget it.

sentence: Kakata takan zuba tuwon masara a cikin akushi kafin mu zauna mu ci.
translation: My grandmother ladles the maize tuwo into the wooden bowl before we sit down to eat.

sentence: Mai gidan cin abinci ya kawo mana tuwo a cikin baƙin akushi.
translation: The restaurant owner brought us tuwo in a blackened wooden bowl.

sentence: Ina son akushin nan domin kakana ne ya sassaƙa shi da hannunsa.
translation: I love this bowl because it was my grandfather who carved it with his own hands.

sentence: Bayan ta wanke kwanoni, sai ta kifa su a kan tebur don su bushe.
translation: After she washed the bowls, she turned them upside down on the table to dry.

sentence: Iska mai ƙarfi ta kifa jirgin ruwan masunta a tafkin Chadi.
translation: A strong wind capsized the fishermen's boat on Lake Chad.

sentence: Na damu sosai lokacin da ƙaramin yaro ya kifa tukunyar miya a ƙasa.
translation: I was really upset when the little boy tipped the soup pot over onto the floor.

sentence: Da safe nakan karya reshen nim in yi asawaki kafin in tafi makaranta.
translation: In the morning I snap off a neem twig to clean my teeth before I leave for school.

sentence: Mai magani yana sayar da ganyen nim ga masu fama da zazzaɓi.
translation: The herbalist sells neem leaves to people who are suffering from fever.

sentence: Na fi son inuwar nim da ke gaban masallaci fiye da kowace bishiya.
translation: I prefer the shade of the neem tree in front of the mosque to that of any other tree.

sentence: Kawuna hutsu ne ƙwarai, kowa a gida yana tsoron tayar masa da hankali.
translation: My uncle is thoroughly cantankerous; everyone at home is afraid of setting him off.

sentence: Direbanmu hutsu ne, yakan yi wa fasinjoji ihu a kowace tashar mota.
translation: Our driver is a cranky man; he shouts at the passengers at every motor park.

sentence: Tun da ya rasa aiki, ya zama hutsu, yana fushi kan kowane ƙaramin abu.
translation: Since he lost his job he has turned cantankerous, flaring up over every little thing.

sentence: Mafarauta sun sayi albarushi a kasuwa kafin su shiga daji da safe.
translation: The hunters bought gunpowder at the market before heading into the bush at dawn.

sentence: Kada ka ajiye albarushi kusa da wuta, domin zai iya tarwatsa gidan.
translation: Don't keep gunpowder near a fire, because it could blow the house apart.

sentence: Warin albarushi ya cika gari bayan an harba bindigogi don murnar sallah.
translation: The smell of gunpowder hung over the town after guns were fired to celebrate the Sallah.

sentence: Kafinta ya ɗauki zarto ya yanke katako biyu don gyaran ƙofar shago.
translation: The carpenter picked up a saw and cut two planks to repair the shop door.

sentence: Zarton da ke rataye a bango ya yi tsatsa saboda ruwan damina.
translation: The saw hanging on the wall has rusted because of the rainy-season damp.

sentence: Yarinyar nan zarto ce, tana gama aikin gida kafin sauran su tashi.
translation: That girl is a live wire; she finishes the housework before the others are even up.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan buɗe laima don kare kanta daga rana yayin tafiya kasuwa.
translation: My mother opens an umbrella to shield herself from the sun on the walk to the market.

sentence: Sun kafa babbar laima a farfajiya domin baƙin bikin auren su zauna.
translation: They pitched a big tent in the courtyard so the wedding guests would have somewhere to sit.

sentence: Ina jin daɗin sauraron ruwa yana bugun laima lokacin da muke tafiya makaranta.
translation: I love listening to the rain drumming on the umbrella while we walk to school.

sentence: Tunku ya shiga garken kaji da dare ya kashe manyan kaji biyu.
translation: A mongoose got into the chicken pen at night and killed two of the big hens.

sentence: Yara sun bi tunku har cikin ramin da ke bayan makarantar.
translation: The children chased a mongoose all the way into the hole behind the school.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda tunku yake kai wa maciji hari ba tare da tsoro ba.
translation: It amazes me how a mongoose attacks a snake without the slightest fear.

sentence: Ta ɗauko cali ta cika shi da albasa da tumatir daga kasuwa.
translation: She fetched a mesh bag and filled it with onions and tomatoes from the market.

sentence: Masuntan tafki sukan zuba kifi a cikin cali kafin su kai kasuwa.
translation: The lake fishermen pour their fish into a mesh bag before taking it to the market.

sentence: Kada ka dogara ga Musa, cali ne, kullum yana da wani uzuri.
translation: Don't count on Musa; he is full of excuses and always has one ready.

sentence: Ajalin miƙa takardun neman aiki ya ƙare gobe, ban ma fara ba.
translation: The deadline for handing in the job application papers ends tomorrow, and I haven't even started.

sentence: Kwamitin ya sanya ajali mai tsanani, wata biyu kacal don gama gina makarantar.
translation: The committee set a harsh deadline: only two months to finish building the school.

sentence: Tsohon ya ce ajalin kowa na hannun Allah ne, don haka ba ya damuwa.
translation: The old man said everyone's appointed span is in God's hands, so he does not worry.

sentence: Tuntun hular kakana ya tsinke, sai mahaifiyata ta sake ɗinka shi.
translation: The tassel on my grandfather's cap snapped off, so my mother stitched it back on.

sentence: Ɗalibai sun sha alfahari da tuntun hulunansu a ranar kammala karatu.
translation: The students were proud of the tassels on their caps on graduation day.

sentence: Ban taɓa son hula mai tuntu ba, amma wannan ta yi mini kyau.
translation: I never liked caps with a tassel, but this one actually suits me.

sentence: Za mu kafa tanti a bayan gida don baƙin da za su zo bikin.
translation: We'll pitch a tent behind the house for the guests coming to the wedding.

sentence: Likitoci suna yin allurar rigakafi a cikin tanti kusa da babbar hanya.
translation: The doctors are giving vaccinations in a tent beside the main road.

sentence: Ban ji daɗin kwana a tanti ba, saboda sauro ya hana ni barci.
translation: I hated sleeping in the tent, because the mosquitoes kept me awake all night.

sentence: Gwandar da ke gefen rijiya ta nuna, sai muka yanka ta bayan sallah.
translation: The papaya by the well had ripened, so we cut it open after prayers.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan sayi gwanda a kasuwar Sabon Gari kafin ta koma gida.
translation: My mother always buys papaya at Sabon Gari market before heading home.

sentence: Ba na son gwanda sosai, amma ƙanwata takan ci ta kowace safiya.
translation: I don't much care for papaya, but my little sister eats it every morning.

sentence: Wanzami ya wanke rezarsa kafin ya fara aske mini gashi.
translation: The barber rinsed his razorblade before he started cutting my hair.

sentence: Kada ka bar reza a kan tebur, yara ƙanana suna wasa a nan.
translation: Don't leave a razorblade on the table — small children play in here.

sentence: Ina jin tsoron reza tun ranar da ta yanke mini yatsa a makaranta.
translation: I've been afraid of razorblades ever since one sliced my finger at school.

sentence: Kakata ta gargaɗe mu kada mu yi santi a gaban baƙi.
translation: My grandmother warned us not to behave badly at table in front of guests.

sentence: Yaron ya nuna santi a wurin biki, ya fara ci kafin a yi addu'a.
translation: The boy disgraced himself at the party by starting to eat before the prayer.

sentence: A gare ni, santi a teburin cin abinci ya fi kowane laifi kunya.
translation: To my mind, bad manners at the dinner table are more shameful than any other fault.

sentence: Da safe muna cin gurasa da miyar taushe kafin mu tafi aiki.
translation: In the mornings we eat gurasa bread with pumpkin stew before we head off to work.

sentence: Matan unguwarmu suna toya gurasa a tanda tun kafin gari ya waye.
translation: The women of our neighbourhood are baking gurasa in the clay oven before daybreak.

sentence: Gurasar Kano ta fi ta ko'ina daɗi, in ji kowane baƙo da ya dandana.
translation: Kano's gurasa beats anyone else's, says every visitor who has ever tasted it.

sentence: Bututun ruwan tsohon gidanmu na darma ne, sai muka sauya shi bara.
translation: The water pipes in our old house were lead, so we replaced them last year.

sentence: Masunta suna ɗaura darma a tarunsu don su nutse cikin ruwa.
translation: The fishermen tie lead weights onto their nets so they sink into the water.

sentence: Likita ya gargaɗe mu cewa darma na da guba ga ƙananan yara.
translation: The doctor warned us that lead is poisonous to small children.

sentence: Tsigi ya sauka a bishiyar mangwaro sannan ya fara waƙa da safe.
translation: A warbler landed in the mango tree and started singing first thing in the morning.

sentence: Yara sun kama tsigi da tarko, sai kakansu ya sa suka sake shi.
translation: The children trapped a lark, but their grandfather made them let it go.

sentence: Ina son jin muryar tsigi da sassafe fiye da ƙarar motoci a hanya.
translation: I'd rather hear a lark at dawn than the racket of cars on the road.

sentence: Mafarin rashin lafiyarsa shi ne ruwan sanyi da ya sha jiya.
translation: The whole illness started with the cold water he drank yesterday.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya bayyana mana mafarin garin Kano da yadda ya girma.
translation: The history teacher explained to us the origins of Kano and how it grew.

sentence: Ƙaramar magana ce ta zama mafarin gaba tsakanin iyalan biyu na unguwarmu.
translation: One small remark became the beginning of a feud between two families in our neighbourhood.

sentence: Amarya tana shafa tozali a idanunta kafin a fito da ita.
translation: The bride is lining her eyes with antimony kohl before she is brought out.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan sa wa jariri tozali domin kare idanunsa daga ƙura.
translation: My mother always puts kohl on the baby to shield his eyes from the dust.

sentence: Ban taɓa siyan tozali a kasuwa ba, na fi son wanda kakata ke niƙawa.
translation: I've never bought kohl in the market; I prefer the kind my grandmother grinds herself.

sentence: Wani Bafilatani yakan kawo mana nono kowace safiya kafin kasuwa ta buɗe.
translation: A certain Fulani man brings us fresh milk every morning before the market opens.

sentence: Bafilatani ne ya koya mini yadda ake kiwon shanu a lokacin damina.
translation: It was a Fulani man who taught me how to herd cattle in the rainy season.

sentence: Kakana Bafilatani ne, don haka yana alfahari da harshen Fulfulde ƙwarai.
translation: My grandfather is a Fulani, so he is deeply proud of the Fulfulde language.

sentence: Mun ketare iyakar Cadi da dare, muna jin tsoron ƴan fashi.
translation: We crossed the border into Chad at night, afraid of bandits the whole way.

sentence: Fatake daga Cadi sukan zo kasuwar Maiduguri da shanu da rakuma.
translation: Traders from Chad come to the Maiduguri market with cattle and camels.

sentence: Na damu ƙwarai da yadda tafkin Cadi ke bushewa saboda ƙarancin ruwan sama.
translation: It worries me a great deal how Lake Chad is drying up for lack of rain.

sentence: Yaron ya ɗora buhun shinkafa kan amalanke ya tura shi zuwa gida.
translation: The boy loaded the sack of rice onto the pushcart and wheeled it home.

sentence: Mai amalanke ya nemi naira ɗari biyu kafin ya kai kayana kasuwa.
translation: The cart pusher asked for two hundred naira before he would take my goods to the market.

sentence: Amalanke ɗin ya karye a tsakiyar hanya, sai muka ɗauki kaya a kanmu.
translation: The pushcart broke down halfway along the road, so we carried the load on our heads.

sentence: Iyayena suna zaune a wata alkarya mai nisan kilomita talatin daga Kano.
translation: My parents live in a small town thirty kilometres out from Kano.

sentence: Malamin ya bar birni ya koma alkarya domin ya koyar da yara.
translation: The teacher left the city and went back to the village to teach the children.

sentence: Ban taɓa mantawa da natsuwar rayuwa a alkarya ba, musamman lokacin girbi.
translation: I have never forgotten how peaceful life in a country town is, especially at harvest time.

sentence: Kakannina sun ce sarakunan Haɓe sun yi mulki kafin jihadin Usman ɗan Fodiyo.
translation: My grandparents said the Habe kings ruled before Usman dan Fodio's jihad.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya bayyana bambanci tsakanin Haɓe da Fulani a cikin aji.
translation: The history teacher explained the difference between the Habe and the Fulani in class.

sentence: Wasu tsofaffi har yanzu suna kiran kansu Haɓe, ba Fulani ba, da alfahari.
translation: Some old people still proudly call themselves Habe, not Fulani.

sentence: Aradu ta yi ƙara mai ƙarfi, sai jariri ya farka yana kuka.
translation: Thunder cracked loudly, and the baby woke up crying.

sentence: Aradu ta buge itacen mangwaro a gonar kakana a bara.
translation: Lightning struck the mango tree on my grandfather's farm last year.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ji aradu, nakan tuna daren da rufin gidanmu ya tashi.
translation: Every time I hear thunder, I remember the night the roof of our house blew off.

sentence: Mun sauka a Jahun da yamma domin mu kwana a gidan aboki.
translation: We stopped in Jahun in the evening to spend the night at a friend's house.

sentence: Asibitin Jahun yana karɓar mata masu juna biyu daga dukan ƙauyukan Jigawa.
translation: The hospital at Jahun takes in pregnant women from every village in Jigawa.

sentence: Ban san hanyar Jahun ba, don haka na biyo bayan babbar mota.
translation: I did not know the road to Jahun, so I followed along behind a lorry.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan latsa lemun tsami cikin ruwa kafin ta zuba sukari.
translation: My mother squeezes a lime into the water before she stirs in the sugar.

sentence: Mai gyaran waya ya latsa maɓallin sau biyu kafin allon ya haskaka.
translation: The phone repairer pressed the button twice before the screen lit up.

sentence: Cunkoson mutane a kasuwa ya kusa latsa wani yaro ƙarami har ya yi kuka.
translation: The crush of people at the market nearly squashed a small boy until he burst into tears.

sentence: Yaran sun tona shuri a bayan gida suna neman gara don kaji.
translation: The children dug open the termite mound behind the house, hunting termites for the chickens.

sentence: Manomi ya yi amfani da ƙasar shuri wajen gyara bangon rumbunsa.
translation: The farmer used soil from the termite mound to repair the wall of his granary.

sentence: Shuri ɗin da ke gefen hanya ya fi ni tsayi, yana ba ni mamaki.
translation: That termite mound by the roadside is taller than I am; it astonishes me.

sentence: Kakata takan zuba fura a kasko kafin ta kai wa baƙi.
translation: My grandmother pours the fura into a clay bowl before carrying it out to the guests.

sentence: Mai tukwane ya sayar mini da kasko a kasuwar Wudil kan naira ɗari.
translation: The potter sold me an earthenware bowl at the Wudil market for a hundred naira.

sentence: Na fi son shan koko a kasko domin yana sanyaya shi da sauri.
translation: I prefer drinking koko out of a clay bowl, because it cools the drink quickly.

sentence: Kowace safiya nakan tsinka gwaiba biyu daga itaciyar bayan gidanmu.
translation: Every morning I pick two guavas off the tree behind our house.

sentence: Matar da ke sayar da gwaiba a kasuwar Kurmi ta ƙi rage min kuɗi.
translation: The woman selling guavas at Kurmi market refused to bring the price down for me.

sentence: Ban taɓa cin gwaiba mai zaƙi kamar wadda kakata ke shukawa ba.
translation: I have never eaten a guava as sweet as the ones my grandmother grows.

sentence: Maya ta shiga geron da muka ajiye a rumbu tun bara.
translation: Weevils have got into the millet we put away in the granary last year.

sentence: Manoma sukan zuba maganin maya a cikin buhunan masara kafin su ajiye su.
translation: Farmers pour weevil powder into the maize sacks before they store them away.

sentence: Na ji haushi ƙwarai da na ga maya ta lalata waken da na tanada.
translation: I was furious when I saw that weevils had ruined the beans I had saved up.

sentence: Babana yana da taguwa guda ɗaya da yake sawa duk ranar Jumaʼa.
translation: My father owns just one gown, and he wears it every Friday.

sentence: Maɗinki ya yi mini taguwa uku kafin Sallah, kowace da launi daban.
translation: The tailor made me three gowns before Sallah, each one a different colour.

sentence: Yana jin daɗin sanya farar taguwa duk lokacin da za a yi biki.
translation: He loves putting on a white gown whenever there is a celebration.

sentence: Da muka tona ƙasa, sai muka ga saiwa ta toshe bututun ruwan gida.
translation: When we dug into the ground we found that a root had blocked the house's water pipe.

sentence: Mai magani ya haƙa saiwa daga daji, sai ya daka ta don maganin zazzaɓi.
translation: The herbalist dug a root out of the bush and pounded it into fever medicine.

sentence: Ina ganin ilimi saiwa ce ta ci gaban kowace ƙasa.
translation: To my mind, education is the root of any country's progress.

sentence: Muryar ladani ta tashe ni tun kafin agogon ƙararrawa ya buga.
translation: The muezzin's voice woke me before my alarm clock had even gone off.

sentence: Ladani ya yi rashin lafiya, sai wani yaro ya hau ya yi kiran sallah.
translation: The muezzin fell ill, so a boy climbed up and gave the call to prayer instead.

sentence: Kowa a unguwarmu yana girmama ladani saboda muryarsa mai daɗi da haƙurinsa.
translation: Everyone in our neighbourhood respects the muezzin for his beautiful voice and his patience.

sentence: Kakana ya bar mana gona mai eka uku a bayan ƙauyen.
translation: My grandfather left us a three-acre farm on the far side of the village.

sentence: Mun yi ta noma har muka gama eka biyu kafin ruwan sama ya sauko.
translation: We kept hoeing until we had finished two acres before the rain came down.

sentence: Rikicin eka ɗaya ya raba mahaifina da ɗanʼuwansa har shekara goma.
translation: A quarrel over a single acre kept my father and his brother apart for ten years.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta zuba garwashi a murhu don ta dumama miyar da safe.
translation: My mother put embers in the stove to warm up the soup in the morning.

sentence: Mai suya yana busa garwashi da faifai domin naman ya gasu da sauri.
translation: The suya seller fans the embers with a mat so the meat roasts quickly.

sentence: Ka yi hankali, garwashi na iya ƙona ƙafarka duk da toka ta rufe shi.
translation: Be careful — embers can still burn your foot even when ash has covered them.

sentence: A birnin Kano kowace ƙabila tana da unguwarta, amma kasuwa tana haɗa kowa.
translation: In Kano city each ethnic group has its own quarter, but the market brings everyone together.

sentence: Iyayenmu sun fito daga ƙabila biyu, don haka muna jin harsuna biyu a gida.
translation: Our parents come from two different ethnic groups, so we speak two languages at home.

sentence: Ina ganin bai kamata ƙabila ta hana mutum samun aiki ba.
translation: I don't think a person's ethnic group should keep them from getting a job.

sentence: Malamin kiɗa ya ba ni gula, ya nuna mini yadda ake bugun ganga.
translation: The drumming teacher handed me a drumstick and showed me how the drum is beaten.

sentence: Kawuna yakan sassaƙa gula daga itacen kirya sannan ya sayar wa maroƙa.
translation: My uncle carves drumsticks out of kirya wood and then sells them to the praise-singers.

sentence: Yaron ya karya gula a tsakiyar bikin, sai maroƙin ya yi fushi ƙwarai.
translation: The boy broke the drumstick in the middle of the wedding, and the drummer was furious.

sentence: Na daɗe ina zaune kan tabarma har ƙafata ta sage gaba ɗaya.
translation: I sat on the mat so long that my leg went completely numb.

sentence: Manomin ya yi noma har bayansa ya sage, sai ya kwanta a inuwa.
translation: The farmer hoed until his back seized up, then he lay down in the shade.

sentence: Tun bayan bugun jini, gefen jikin kakana ya sage, ba ya iya tafiya.
translation: Ever since the stroke, one side of my grandfather's body has been paralysed and he cannot walk.

sentence: Fis ɗin gidanmu ya ƙone da daddare, sai muka kwana cikin duhu.
translation: The fuse in our house blew during the night, so we slept in darkness.

sentence: Mai gyaran wutar lantarki ya sayo sabon fis a kasuwar Sabon Gari.
translation: The electrician went and bought a new fuse at Sabon Gari market.

sentence: Na gaji da yadda fis ke ƙonewa duk lokacin da aka kunna janareta.
translation: I am tired of the way the fuse blows every time the generator is switched on.

sentence: Yayyafi ya fara sauka, sai mahaifiyata ta ce mu tattara tufafin da muka shanya.
translation: A drizzle began to fall, so my mother told us to gather in the washing we had hung out.

sentence: Yayyafi ya sauka a kasuwa, sai ʼyan kasuwa suka rufe kayansu da leda.
translation: Light rain came down on the market, so the traders covered their goods with plastic sheeting.

sentence: Ina son yayyafi na safe fiye da ruwan sama mai ƙarfi da tsawa.
translation: I prefer a morning drizzle to heavy rain with thunder.

sentence: Baba ya ɗauki diga ya fara tona rami don shuka itacen mangwaro.
translation: Father picked up the pickaxe and started digging a hole to plant a mango tree.

sentence: Maʼaikatan hanya suna fasa dutse da diga tun kafin rana ta yi zafi.
translation: The road workers break the rock with a pickaxe well before the sun turns hot.

sentence: Bayan saʼa ɗaya kawai ina aiki da diga, hannuwana sun fara ciwo.
translation: After only one hour of working with the pickaxe, my hands began to hurt.

sentence: Kwalin ashana ya jiƙa da ruwan sama, sai muka kasa kunna fitila.
translation: The box of matches got soaked by the rain, so we could not light the lamp.

sentence: Mai shayi ya kunna murhunsa da ashana kafin ʼyan achaba su iso.
translation: The tea seller lit his stove with a match before the motorcycle-taxi riders arrived.

sentence: Kada ka bar ashana a hannun yara, don wuta ba wasa ba ce.
translation: Don't leave matches in children's hands, because fire is no joke.

sentence: An yi wa ƙanena kaciya a asibiti, bai ma yi kuka ba.
translation: My little brother was circumcised at the hospital, and he did not even cry.

sentence: Bikin kaciyar jikan Malam Sani ya tara maƙwabta duka a unguwarmu.
translation: The celebration for the circumcision of Malam Sani's grandson brought together every neighbour in our quarter.

sentence: Likita ya ce a yi kaciya tun yana jariri, don hakan ya fi sauƙi.
translation: The doctor said the circumcision should be done while he is still a baby, since that is easier.

sentence: Maryamu ta tashi da sassafe ta dafa koko ta soya ƙosai wa yara.
translation: Maryamu got up at first light, cooked millet porridge and fried bean cakes for the children.

sentence: Maryamu ce ta fi kowa maki a jarrabawar lissafi a ajinmu.
translation: It was Maryamu who scored higher than anyone else on the maths exam in our class.

sentence: Malamin makaranta ya karanta mana labarin Maryamu, sai ajin duka ya yi shiru.
translation: The teacher read us the story of Maryamu, and the whole class fell silent.

sentence: Sanyin hunturu ya yi tsanani, sai na ƙara wani bargo a kan gado.
translation: The harmattan cold turned bitter, so I put another blanket on the bed.

sentence: Ƙungiyar agaji ta ba kowane iyali bargo ɗaya bayan ambaliyar ruwa.
translation: The relief organisation gave every family one blanket after the flood.

sentence: Bargon da kakata ta saƙa mini ya fi duk wanda na saya ɗumi.
translation: The blanket my grandmother wove for me is warmer than any one I have bought.

sentence: Ruwan sama ya rushe garun gidanmu, sai awakin maƙwabta suka shiga lambu.
translation: The rain brought down our compound wall, and the neighbours' goats got into the garden.

sentence: Masu yawon buɗe ido suna ɗaukar hoto a gaban tsohon garun birnin Kano.
translation: Tourists are taking photographs in front of the old city wall of Kano.

sentence: Mahaifina ya ce garu mai tsawo ba ya hana ɓarawo, sai kyakkyawan maƙwabci.
translation: My father says a high wall does not keep a thief out — only a good neighbour does.

sentence: Ɗinkin rigar bai yi mini ba, sai na koma wurin maɗinki don sakiya.
translation: The gown was not sewn to fit me, so I went back to the tailor for an alteration.

sentence: Kwamitin ya yi sakiya a dokokin ƙungiyar bayan muhawara ta kwana biyu.
translation: The committee made an amendment to the association's rules after a two-day debate.

sentence: Sakiyar da suka yi a jadawalin jirgi ta ɓata mini tafiyar bikin.
translation: The change they made to the train timetable ruined my journey to the wedding.

sentence: Ka mayar da kayan aiki a mahallinsu bayan kun gama gyaran rijiya.
translation: Put the tools back where they belong once you have finished repairing the well.

sentence: Malam ya ce maʼanar kalma takan sauya bisa ga mahallin jimlar da take ciki.
translation: The teacher said a word's meaning shifts according to the context of the sentence it sits in.

sentence: Ba na jin daɗin zama a wannan mahalli, domin hayaniya ba ta ƙarewa.
translation: I do not enjoy living in this place, because the noise never stops.

sentence: Bayan jarrabawar ƙarshe, mun hole a gidan kakata har dare ya yi.
translation: After the last exam we relaxed at my grandmother's house until nightfall.

sentence: Maʼaikatan kamfanin sun hole a Kano bayan sun kammala aikin watanni uku.
translation: The company's workers unwound in Kano after finishing three months on the job.

sentence: A ganina, ya kamata kowa ya hole kaɗan kafin ya koma aikinsa.
translation: In my view everyone ought to enjoy themselves a little before going back to work.

sentence: Kafin mu fita zuwa masallaci, mahaifina ya nemi fula tasa a ɗaki.
translation: Before we set off for the mosque my father hunted for his cap in the bedroom.

sentence: Mai sayar da fula a kasuwar Kano ya rage min kuɗi saboda na saba.
translation: The cap seller in Kano market knocked something off the price because I'm a regular.

sentence: Ina son wannan fula ja, amma farashinta ya fi ƙarfina.
translation: I love this red fez, but the price is well beyond my means.

sentence: Ban yarda da wannan labari ba sai na ji daga wani tushe sahihi.
translation: I won't believe this story until I hear it from a reliable source.

sentence: Malamin ya karanta mana hadisi sahihi kafin ya fara huɗubar Jumaʼa.
translation: The teacher read us an authentic hadith before he began the Friday sermon.

sentence: Masana sun ce hoton ba sahihi ba ne, an gyara shi da kwamfuta.
translation: The experts said the photograph isn't genuine — it was doctored on a computer.

sentence: Yara sun shimfiɗa bajau a ƙarƙashin bishiyar mangwaro suka fara buga karta.
translation: The lads spread the playing cloth out under the mango tree and started a game of cards.

sentence: Bayan an tashi daga wasa, Musa ya naɗe bajau ya sa a jaka.
translation: Once the game broke up, Musa rolled the card cloth away and stuffed it in a bag.

sentence: Mahaifina ba ya son bajau a gidansa, yana cewa wasan karta banza ne.
translation: My father won't have a card cloth in his house; he says card playing is a waste of time.

sentence: Ƙofar ƙarfe ta yi tsatsa saboda ruwan sama, yanzu ba ta buɗewa.
translation: The iron gate has rusted from the rain, and now it won't open.

sentence: Makanike ya goge tsatsa daga injin motar kafin ya sa sabon fenti.
translation: The mechanic scrubbed the rust off the car's engine before putting on fresh paint.

sentence: Ina jin haushin ganin tsatsa a kan sabuwar motata bayan wata uku kacal.
translation: It infuriates me to see rust on my new car after barely three months.

sentence: Mutane sun cika masallaci domin sauraron shaihi da ya dawo daga Makka.
translation: People packed the mosque to hear the great scholar who had come back from Mecca.

sentence: Kakana shaihi ne a garinmu, kowa yakan zo neman shawararsa da yamma.
translation: My grandfather is a revered scholar in our town; everyone comes for his counsel in the evening.

sentence: Kowane malami ba shaihi ba ne, sai wanda ya yi shekaru yana nazari.
translation: Not every teacher is a true scholar — only one who has spent years at his studies.

sentence: Bayan mun buɗa baki, muka tafi masallaci domin sallar asham tare da maƙwabta.
translation: After we broke our fast we walked to the mosque for the tarawih prayers with the neighbours.

sentence: Limamin garinmu yakan tsawaita asham a kwanaki goma na ƙarshe na Ramadan.
translation: Our town's imam draws the tarawih out longer during the last ten nights of Ramadan.

sentence: Na gaji sosai jiya, amma ban rasa asham ba domin ina son karatun limamin.
translation: I was worn out yesterday, but I didn't miss the tarawih because I love the imam's recitation.

sentence: Malamar ta rubuta wasali a allo, ta nemi yara su maimaita sautinsa.
translation: The teacher wrote a vowel on the blackboard and asked the children to repeat its sound.

sentence: A cikin harshen Hausa, kowace kalma tana buƙatar wasali tsakanin baƙaƙe biyu.
translation: In Hausa every word needs a vowel between any two consonants.

sentence: Ina fama da wasali mai tsawo, saboda rubutun Hausa bai nuna tsawon sauti ba.
translation: I struggle with the long vowel, because Hausa spelling gives no sign of vowel length.

sentence: Mutanen unguwar suna girmama shi domin sharifi ne daga zuriyar Annabi.
translation: The people of the neighbourhood hold him in honour because he is a sharif of the Prophet's line.

sentence: Kakata takan ce mahaifinta sharifi ne wanda ya zo daga Madina.
translation: My grandmother always says her father was a sharif who came from Medina.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda sharifi yake rayuwa cikin tawaliʼu duk da darajarsa.
translation: It amazes me how humbly the sharif lives in spite of his standing.

sentence: Bayan doguwar tafiya, muka nemi makwanci a gidan wani malami a ƙauyen.
translation: After the long journey we looked for somewhere to sleep at a teacher's house in the village.

sentence: Maʼaikatan gona sun shirya makwanci a rumfa domin ruwan sama ya kama su.
translation: The farm hands rigged up a place to sleep in the shed because the rain caught them out.

sentence: Allah ya sanya makwancinsa ya zama mai sanyi, in ji imamin a janaʼizar.
translation: May God make his resting place cool, the imam said at the funeral.

sentence: Kakana ya ce ya taɓa ganin ayu a kogin Neja tun yana yaro.
translation: My grandfather says he once saw a manatee in the River Niger when he was a boy.

sentence: Masuntan Yauri sun daina kama ayu tun da gwamnati ta haramta farautarsa.
translation: The fishermen of Yauri stopped catching manatees once the government banned hunting them.

sentence: Yaran makaranta sun yi mamakin girman ayu a gidan namun daji na Jos.
translation: The schoolchildren were astonished at how big the manatee was at the Jos wildlife park.

sentence: Yara ƙanana suna wasa a bayan gida har rana ta faɗi.
translation: The little children play behind the house until the sun goes down.

sentence: Tumatir ɗin da yake sayarwa duk ƙanana ne, don haka na wuce.
translation: The tomatoes he was selling were all small ones, so I walked on past.

sentence: Gidan yana da kyau, sai dai ɗakunansa ƙanana ne ƙwarai.
translation: The house is nice enough, except that its rooms are really small.

sentence: Magini ya ce dole mu jira sati biyu kafin bangon ya bushe.
translation: The builder said we have to wait two weeks before the wall dries.

sentence: Mun ɗauki magini daga Kano don ya gyara rufin makarantar kafin damina.
translation: We brought in a builder from Kano to repair the school roof before the rains.

sentence: Ina mamakin yadda magini ɗaya ya gina wannan katafaren gida cikin wata uku.
translation: I am amazed that a single builder put up this huge house in three months.

sentence: Direban ya ƙi tashi har sai kowa ya ɗaura bel ɗinsa.
translation: The driver refused to set off until everyone had fastened their seatbelt.

sentence: Bel ɗina ya yi tsawo, sai na huda masa wani rami.
translation: My belt turned out too long, so I punched another hole in it.

sentence: Na tsorata sosai lokacin da mota ta yi birki, amma bel ya riƙe ni.
translation: I was badly frightened when the car braked hard, but the seatbelt held me.

sentence: Bayan kwana uku ana bincike, sai muka gane cewa jita-jitar ba dahir ba ne.
translation: After three days of looking into it, we realised the rumour was not the truth.

sentence: Talaucin da muke ciki a ƙauye dahir ne, ba labarin da aka ƙaga ba.
translation: The poverty we live in out in the village is a reality, not a made-up story.

sentence: Da farko ban gaskata ba, sai da na ga dahirin lamarin da idona.
translation: At first I didn't believe it, not until I saw the truth of the matter with my own eyes.

sentence: Kowace safiya makiyayi yakan kai shanunsa inda ciyawa ta fi yawa.
translation: Every morning the herdsman takes his cattle to where the grass is thickest.

sentence: Ciyawa ta cika farfajiyar gidan, sai na aro adda wajen maƙwabci.
translation: Grass has taken over the compound yard, so I borrowed a machete from the neighbour.

sentence: Bayan ruwan sama, ƙanshin sabuwar ciyawa yakan tuna mini ƙuruciyata a ƙauye.
translation: After rain, the smell of fresh grass always reminds me of my childhood in the village.

sentence: Kakata ba ta iya karanta Alƙurʼani sai ta sanya tabarau mai kauri.
translation: My grandmother can't read the Qur'an unless she puts on her thick glasses.

sentence: Likita ya ce sai na sa tabarau idan ina karatu da dare.
translation: The doctor said I must wear glasses whenever I read at night.

sentence: Na yi ta neman tabarau na, ashe yana kan kaina tun farko.
translation: I hunted everywhere for my glasses, and all along they were sitting on my head.

sentence: Ɗan kokawa ya ɗaura guru a ƙugunsa kafin ya shiga dandali.
translation: The wrestler tied his charm-belt around his waist before stepping into the arena.

sentence: Wani tsoho yana sayar da guru a kasuwar Kurmi kowace Jumaʼa.
translation: An old man sells charm-belts at Kurmi market every Friday.

sentence: Kakana ya bar mini guru ɗinsa, amma mahaifina ya ce kada in sa shi.
translation: My grandfather left me his charm-belt, but my father told me never to wear it.

sentence: Sauro sun yi mini addaba tsawon dare, don haka ban yi barci ba.
translation: Mosquitoes tormented me the whole night, so I never got any sleep.

sentence: Shugaban aiki yana yi mata addaba har sai da ta yi murabus.
translation: Her boss kept harassing her until she finally resigned.

sentence: Ban iya jure addaba daga maƙwabta ba, sai na ƙaura zuwa wata unguwa.
translation: I couldn't put up with the harassment from the neighbours, so I moved to another neighbourhood.

sentence: Zik ɗin jakata ya karye a hanya, sai littattafai suka fara zubowa.
translation: The zip on my bag broke on the way, and the books started spilling out.

sentence: Maɗinki ya ce zai sauya zik ɗin wandona kafin ranar Jumaʼa.
translation: The tailor said he would replace the zip on my trousers before Friday.

sentence: Yarinyar ta yi kuka domin ba ta iya rufe zik ɗin rigarta ita kaɗai.
translation: The little girl cried because she couldn't do up the zip of her dress on her own.

sentence: Yaron ya taka bawon ayaba ya faɗi wanwar a tsakiyar ɗaki.
translation: The boy stepped on a banana peel and went flat on his back in the middle of the room.

sentence: Da ya zame a kan laka, sai ya faɗi wanwar gaban mutanen kasuwa.
translation: He slipped in the mud and went sprawling flat on his back in front of the whole market.

sentence: Ban taɓa jin kunya ba kamar ranar da na faɗi wanwar a bikin.
translation: I have never been so ashamed as the day I fell flat on my back at the wedding.

sentence: Muna buga karta a bakin shago, sai Audu ya fitar da caka.
translation: We were playing cards outside the shop when Audu brought out a club.

sentence: Kowane katin da na ja daga tsibin ya zama caka.
translation: Every single card I drew off the pile turned out to be a club.

sentence: Kakana ya ce caka shi ne katin saʼa, amma ban yarda ba.
translation: My grandfather says clubs is the lucky suit, but I don't believe it.

sentence: Kada ki tsinke gunda tukuna, bari kabewar ta nuna a gona.
translation: Don't pick the young pumpkin yet — let it ripen out in the field.

sentence: Yaran gona sun cika kwando da gunda kafin ruwan sama ya sauka.
translation: The farm boys filled a basket with young pumpkins before the rain came down.

sentence: Ba na son gunda ko kaɗan, amma kakata ta ce tana da amfani.
translation: I don't like unripe pumpkin at all, but my grandmother says it does you good.

sentence: Mahaifiyata takan tafasa ganyen kurna don ta wanke gashin yara.
translation: My mother boils thorn-tree leaves to wash the children's hair.

sentence: Ƙayar kurna ta huda min takalmi yayin da nake kiwon shanu.
translation: A thorn-tree spike went straight through my shoe while I was herding the cattle.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ga kurna, sai in tuna da gidan kakana.
translation: Every time I see a thorn tree, I think of my grandfather's compound.

sentence: Kullum ana jidali a tashar mota kan kuɗin motar zuwa Kano.
translation: There is always an argument at the motor park over the fare to Kano.

sentence: Jidali ya barke a taron ƙauyen kan wanda zai jagoranci aikin.
translation: A dispute broke out at the village meeting over who would lead the work.

sentence: Na gaji da jidali tsakanin ʼyan uwana kan gadon mahaifinmu.
translation: I am worn out by the wrangling among my siblings over our father's inheritance.

sentence: Kaza ta kife kwanon shinkafa a ƙasa kafin mu gama cin abinci.
translation: The hen knocked the bowl of rice over onto the ground before we had finished eating.

sentence: Mai sayar da gyaɗa ya kife kwandonsa a kan tabarma don ya auna.
translation: The groundnut seller tipped his basket out onto the mat so he could measure it.

sentence: Zuciyata ta yi tsalle lokacin da kwale-kwalen ya kife a tsakiyar kogi.
translation: My heart jumped when the canoe capsized in the middle of the river.

sentence: Bayan girbi, mun cika rumbu da gero har bakinsa.
translation: After the harvest we filled the granary with millet right up to its mouth.

sentence: Sarki ya umarce mu da mu buɗe rumbu domin a raba hatsi.
translation: The chief ordered us to open the granary so the grain could be shared out.

sentence: Ina tsoron cewa rumbu zai zama fanko kafin damina ta dawo.
translation: I am afraid the granary will stand empty before the rains come back.

sentence: Bisimilla, ku zauna ku ci tuwo kafin ya yi sanyi.
translation: Come now, sit down and eat the tuwo before it goes cold.

sentence: Da baƙi suka iso, kakata ta miƙa musu kwano tana cewa bisimilla.
translation: When the guests arrived, my grandmother handed them a bowl and said bisimilla — help yourselves.

sentence: A gidanmu, ba wanda zai taɓa abinci sai baba ya ce bisimilla.
translation: In our house nobody touches the food until father says bisimilla.

sentence: Ban sani ba ko kadari ya yi yawa, don haka na tambayi maƙwabciyata.
translation: I couldn't tell whether the price was too high, so I asked my neighbour.

sentence: A kasuwar dabbobi, kadari yakan sauka idan ruwan sama ya yi yawa.
translation: At the livestock market the price usually drops when the rains have been heavy.

sentence: A ganina, kadari ba ya nuna soyayyar da ke cikin kyauta ba.
translation: To my mind, the price of a gift says nothing about the love inside it.

sentence: Na kwana biyu a ofishin jakadanci kafin su ba ni biza.
translation: I spent two whole days at the embassy before they gave me a visa.

sentence: Yayana ya aiko da kuɗin biza domin mu tafi aikin hajji.
translation: My elder brother sent the visa money so that we could go on the hajj.

sentence: Na yi baƙin ciki lokacin da suka ƙi ba ni biza karo na biyu.
translation: I was heartbroken when they refused me a visa for the second time.

sentence: Yara sun fito daga gida su kalli husufin rana da tabarau masu duhu.
translation: The children came out of the house to watch the solar eclipse through dark glasses.

sentence: Malamin makaranta ya zana a kan allo yadda husufin rana ke faruwa.
translation: The schoolteacher drew on the blackboard how a solar eclipse happens.

sentence: Kakata ta ce husufi alama ce ta ikon Allah, ba abin tsoro ba.
translation: My grandmother said an eclipse is a sign of God's power, not something to be afraid of.

sentence: Ungozoma ta yi wa mata jawabi kan tsaftar duri bayan haihuwa.
translation: The midwife gave the women a talk on vaginal hygiene after childbirth.

sentence: Likita ya gaya mata cewa ciwon duri yakan warke da magani cikin mako guda.
translation: The doctor told her that a vaginal infection usually clears up with medicine within a week.

sentence: Mata da yawa suna jin kunyar ambaton duri, don haka ba sa zuwa asibiti.
translation: Many women are too embarrassed to say the word vagina, so they never go to the clinic.

sentence: Maciji ya sare yaron, mahaifinsa kuwa ya garzaya zuwa asibiti neman makari.
translation: A snake bit the boy, and his father rushed off to the hospital to look for an antidote.

sentence: Maʼaikatan asibitin sun ce babu makarin dafin kunama a duk garin nan.
translation: The hospital staff said there is no antidote for scorpion venom anywhere in this town.

sentence: Malaminmu ya ce haƙuri shi ne makarin fushi, ba ramuwa ba.
translation: Our teacher said patience is the antidote to anger, not revenge.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta dafa gwaza, ta zuba mai da yaji a kai.
translation: My mother boiled the taro and poured oil and pepper spice over it.

sentence: A kasuwar Kurmi, mata suna sayar da gwaza da doya kusa da hanya.
translation: At Kurmi market the women sell taro and yam right beside the road.

sentence: Manoma sun koka cewa ambaliya ta lalata gwazar da suka shuka bana.
translation: The farmers complained that the flood destroyed the taro they had planted this year.

sentence: Da yaron ya fara tafiya, kakansa ya ɗaga hannu ya ce, “Tubarkalla!”
translation: When the little boy took his first steps, his grandfather raised his hand and said, “Praise God!”

sentence: Iyaye sun yi ta cewa “Tubarkalla!” saʼad da yaran suka sauke Alƙurʼani.
translation: The parents kept calling out “Bravo!” as the children finished their recitation of the Qurʼan.

sentence: Tubarkalla! Ban taɓa ganin an gina masallaci cikin wata biyu ba.
translation: Praise God! I have never seen a mosque put up in two months.

sentence: Kakata takan ce, “Ka nemi tsarin Allah daga ibilis kafin ka kwanta barci.”
translation: My grandmother would always say, “Ask God to protect you from the devil before you lie down to sleep.”

sentence: Limami ya gargaɗi mabiya cewa ibilis yakan haifar da rigima tsakanin maƙwabta.
translation: The imam warned the congregation that the devil is forever stirring up quarrels between neighbours.

sentence: Alƙali ya ce ba ibilis ne ya sace kuɗin ba, ƙwaɗayin ɓarawon ne.
translation: The judge said it was not the devil who stole the money, but the thief's own greed.

sentence: Mahauci ya yanke tozon sa ya sayar da shi da tsada a kasuwa.
translation: The butcher cut off the bull's hump and sold it at a high price in the market.

sentence: Raƙuma sun isa rijiyar, tozonsu ya ragu bayan doguwar tafiya a hamada.
translation: The camels reached the well with their humps shrunken after the long journey across the desert.

sentence: Yaron ya tambaye ni ko ruwa ne ke cikin tozon raƙumi, na yi murmushi.
translation: The boy asked me whether it is water that sits inside a camel's hump, and I smiled.

sentence: Hakkan, ba zan taɓa mantawa da ranar da muka isa Makka ba.
translation: Truly, I will never forget the day we arrived in Mecca.

sentence: Shaidun sun tabbatar cewa hakkan mutumin bai kusanci shagon ba a daren satar.
translation: The witnesses confirmed that the man really did not go near the shop on the night of the theft.

sentence: Hakkan na gaji yau, tun safe nake wanki har rana ta faɗi.
translation: I am truly worn out today; I have been washing clothes from morning until sundown.

sentence: Kakata tana saƙa wa jikanta hular ulu kafin hunturu ya kama.
translation: My grandmother is knitting her grandson a wool cap before the harmattan cold sets in.

sentence: Ɗan kasuwa ya kawo zaren ulu daga Kano, mata suka yi ta sayayya.
translation: A trader brought wool thread down from Kano, and the women kept buying it up.

sentence: Rigar ulu tana ɗumama ni sosai, amma tana sa min ƙaiƙayi.
translation: The wool sweater keeps me really warm, but it makes me itch.

sentence: Malamin tarihi ya bayyana yadda mulukiya ta bambanta da mulkin dimokuraɗiyya.
translation: The history teacher explained how a monarchy differs from democratic rule.

sentence: Kakana yakan ba mu labarin mulukiyar da ta yi mulki kafin zuwan Turawa.
translation: My grandfather used to tell us about the monarchy that ruled here before the Europeans came.

sentence: Ban yarda ba, a mulukiya talakawa ba sa zaɓen shugabanninsu.
translation: I don't agree: under a monarchy ordinary people never get to elect their leaders.

sentence: Da sassafe na yi wanki, sannan na dafa wa yara kunu.
translation: Early in the morning I did the laundry, then I made the children some kunu.

sentence: Ya yi shekara goma yana aiki a bankin Kano kafin ya yi murabus.
translation: He spent ten years working at the bank in Kano before he resigned.

sentence: Abincin da mahaifiyata ta dafa jiya ya yi daɗi ƙwarai.
translation: The food my mother cooked yesterday was absolutely delicious.

sentence: Rigar nan da na saya a kasuwar Kurmi ba ta yi mini ba.
translation: This gown I bought at Kurmi market doesn't fit me.

sentence: Tun daga safe muke zaune a nan, amma likitan bai zo ba tukuna.
translation: We have been sitting here since morning, but the doctor still hasn't come.

sentence: Daga nan zuwa Kaduna tafiya ce ta awa uku, ina jin gajiya tuni.
translation: From here to Kaduna is a three-hour journey, and I'm tired already.

sentence: Yaran sun dawo daga makaranta, sun ci abinci, yanzu suna wasa a waje.
translation: The children got back from school, ate, and now they're playing outside.

sentence: Maƙwabtanmu sun ƙaura zuwa Kano tun watan da ya wuce.
translation: Our neighbours moved away to Kano last month.

sentence: Abin mamaki ne, sun gama gina masallacin cikin watanni uku kacal.
translation: It's astonishing — they finished building the mosque in just three months.

sentence: Kowace safiya mahaifina yakan tafi gona kafin rana ta fito.
translation: Every morning my father goes off to the farm before the sun comes up.

sentence: Mun tafi bikin auren ƙanwata a Zariya, muka dawo da daddare.
translation: We went to my younger sister's wedding in Zaria and came back late at night.

sentence: Bai kamata ka tafi ba kafin mu warware wannan matsala tsakaninmu.
translation: You shouldn't leave before we settle this problem between us.

sentence: Idan ruwan sama ya tsaya, sai mu fita mu kama tasi.
translation: Once the rain stops, then we'll go out and catch a taxi.

sentence: A kasuwar nan ba a karɓar katin banki, sai kuɗi na hannu.
translation: In this market they don't take bank cards, only cash.

sentence: Ban gane darasin ba sai da malamin ya sake bayyana shi a hankali.
translation: I didn't understand the lesson until the teacher explained it again slowly.

sentence: Muna zaune a ƙarƙashin bishiyar mangwaro muna jiran motar Kaduna.
translation: We're sitting under the mango tree waiting for the Kaduna bus.

sentence: Muna gyara rufin makarantar kafin damina ta shigo gaba ɗaya.
translation: We're repairing the school roof before the rainy season sets in properly.

sentence: Muna da wata tsohuwar mota, amma tana lalacewa duk bayan mako biyu.
translation: We have an old car, but it breaks down every couple of weeks.

sentence: Mun sayi shinkafa da mai a kasuwa, amma mun manta da sukari.
translation: We bought rice and oil at the market, but we forgot the sugar.

sentence: Mun gama girbin gero kafin ruwan sama ya sake sauka a gonar.
translation: We finished harvesting the millet before the rain came down on the farm again.

sentence: Mun ji daɗin ziyarar ƙauyen kakanmu, har ba mu son komawa birni.
translation: We enjoyed the visit to our grandfather's village so much we didn't want to go back to the city.

sentence: Mahaifiyata tana dafa miyar kuka a murhu tun kafin mu farka.
translation: My mother has been cooking baobab-leaf soup on the stove since before we woke up.

sentence: A ranar Sallah muka dafa wa maƙwabta tuwo da naman rago.
translation: On Sallah day we cooked tuwo and mutton for the neighbours.

sentence: Duk wanda ya dafa wannan shinkafar bai sa gishiri ba ko kaɗan.
translation: Whoever cooked this rice didn't put in a grain of salt.

sentence: Yara sun ɓata kwanukan da muka saya jiya, mahaifiyarsu ta yi fushi.
translation: The children broke the bowls we bought yesterday, and their mother was furious.

sentence: Malamin ya raba yara kashi biyu don su yi gasar karatu.
translation: The teacher split the children into two groups for a reading contest.

sentence: Ina jin daɗin sauraron yara suna dariya a farfajiya kowace maraice.
translation: I love listening to the children laughing in the courtyard every evening.

sentence: Ɗan uwana zai iso Kano da jirgin ƙasa gobe da safe.
translation: My brother will get into Kano by train tomorrow morning.

sentence: Shugaban ƙauyen ya ce zai buɗe rijiyar ruwa kafin watan Ramadan.
translation: The village head said he will open the water well before the month of Ramadan.

sentence: Ina tsoron farashin man fetur zai sake tashi kafin ƙarshen wata.
translation: I'm afraid the price of petrol will go up again before the end of the month.

sentence: Kakana tsoho tukuf ne, amma har yanzu yana noman gonarsa da kansa.
translation: My grandfather is extremely old, but he still farms his field by himself.

sentence: Motar da muka saya a kasuwar Kano tsohuwa tukuf ce, tana lalacewa kullum.
translation: The car we bought at the Kano market is ancient — it breaks down every day.

sentence: Malamin nan tsoho tukuf ne, amma muryarsa tana burge kowa a masallaci.
translation: That teacher is very old indeed, yet his voice still moves everyone in the mosque.

sentence: Da safe wani alhudahuda ya sauka a bishiyar mangwaro da ke bayan gidanmu.
translation: This morning a hoopoe landed in the mango tree behind our house.

sentence: Malam ya gaya mana labarin alhudahuda da ya kai saƙo wurin Sarki Sulaiman.
translation: The teacher told us the story of the hoopoe that carried a message to King Solomon.

sentence: Ina jin daɗin kallon alhudahuda a gonarmu, gashin kansa yana ba ni mamaki.
translation: I love watching the hoopoe out in our field; the crest on its head always amazes me.

sentence: Ina zuwa kasuwa da ƙanwata don mu sayi kayan miya kafin ruwan sama.

sentence: Malaminmu yana da haƙuri, don haka ɗalibai ba sa jin tsoron tambaya.

sentence: Da yamma ina jin kewar mahaifiyata, sai in kira ta ta wayar hannu.

sentence: Ɗan uwana ya karya tukunyar miya, sai mahaifiyarmu ta yi fushi sosai.

sentence: Malami ya rubuta tambayoyin jarabawa a allo kafin ɗalibai su shiga aji.

sentence: Zuciyata ta kwanta lokacin da ya dawo gida lafiya daga Legas.

sentence: Ƙanena yana wanke mota a bayan gida tun kafin rana ta fito.

sentence: Wani mai sayar da waina yana kiran abokan ciniki a gefen titin kasuwa.

sentence: Sabon shugaban ƙauyen yana da gaskiya, shi ya sa mutane suke girmama shi.

sentence: Na tashi da sassafe don in dafa wa yara kunu kafin makaranta.

sentence: Na sadu da tsohon abokina a tashar mota, muka yi hira sosai.
translation: I ran into an old friend at the motor park, and we talked for ages.

sentence: Na yi nadamar sayar da gonar kakana, amma bashi ya matsa mini ƙwarai.
translation: I regret selling my grandfather's farm, but the debt was pressing me hard.

sentence: Wannan mota ta mahaifiyata ce, ni kawai na aro ta yau da safe.

sentence: Likitar da ta duba ɗana jiya sabuwa ce a wannan asibiti.

sentence: Ya ce mini zai zo da yamma, amma bai zo ba har yanzu.

sentence: Ka zo da wuri gobe, za mu tafi gonar kakanka tare.
translation: Come early tomorrow — we're going to your grandfather's farm together.

sentence: Baƙi sun zo daga Kano don bikin auren ƙanwata a ranar Asabar.

sentence: Na yi farin ciki lokacin da likita ya zo bayan mahaifiyata ta suma.

sentence: Ina wanke kayan yara a bayan gida lokacin da ruwan sama ya fara.

sentence: Ina kake tafiya da wuri haka, sanye da sabuwar riga?
translation: Where are you off to so early, dressed in a new gown?

sentence: Ina da ƙanwa guda ɗaya kawai, kuma ita ce amintacciyar abokiyata.
translation: I have only one younger sister, and she is my most trusted friend.

sentence: Ba mu sami ruwa ba a famfo yau, sai da muka je rijiya.

sentence: Jiya ba ta zo aiki ba domin ɗanta yana da zazzaɓi mai tsanani.
translation: She didn't come to work yesterday because her son had a bad fever.

sentence: Ban taɓa ganin irin wannan kyautatawa ba tun da na koma unguwar nan.

sentence: Akwai koko da ƙosai a ɗakin girki, amma babu sukari.
translation: There's koko and bean cakes in the kitchen, but there's no sugar.

sentence: A kasuwar Kurmi akwai mutane da yawa, don haka ka riƙe jakarka.

sentence: Akwai fata a raina cewa ɗana zai ci jarabawar shiga jamiʼa.

sentence: Ƙanwata ta fi ni ƙwarewa wajen dafa tuwo, amma ni ce babba.

sentence: Wannan kasuwa ta fi ta Sabon Gari araha, shi ya sa nake zuwa nan.
translation: This market is cheaper than the one at Sabon Gari, which is why I come here.

sentence: Na fi son karatu da daddare, domin gidanmu yakan yi tsit gaba ɗaya.
translation: I prefer studying late at night, because our house goes completely quiet then.

sentence: Mahaifiyata ta sayo mini riga sabuwa don sallah, amma ta yi mini girma.
translation: My mother bought me a new gown for Sallah, but it turned out too big for me.

sentence: Motar shugaban makaranta sabuwa ce, kuma yara duk suna kallonta da mamaki.

sentence: Sanaʼar nan sabuwa ce a gare ni, don haka ina jin tsoro kaɗan.

sentence: Jiya da yamma wutar lantarki ta tafi, sai muka ci abinci cikin duhu.

sentence: Jiya mun kwashe saʼoʼi uku a asibiti kafin likita ya zo.

sentence: Har yanzu ina jin haushin abin da ya faɗa mini jiya.

sentence: Ka wanke faranti sosai kafin ka ajiye su a kan tebur.

sentence: Malamin ya yaba mana sosai bayan muka gama gyara ajin da yamma.
translation: The teacher praised us warmly after we finished tidying the classroom that evening.

sentence: Ina son garin Kano sosai, amma hayaniyarsa takan gajiyar da ni.
translation: I love the city of Kano very much, but its noise wears me out.

sentence: Gobe da safe za mu tashi da wuri mu je gonar kakana.
translation: Tomorrow morning we'll get up early and go out to my grandfather's farm.

sentence: Ka tuna cewa gobe ne ranar biyan kuɗin haya, kada ka manta.
translation: Remember that tomorrow is the day the rent is due — don't forget.

sentence: Zuciyata tana bugawa, domin gobe za a sanar da wanda ya samu aikin.
translation: My heart is pounding, because tomorrow they announce who got the job.

sentence: Na gan shi a tashar mota yana jiran bas zuwa Kaduna.
translation: I saw him at the motor park waiting for the bus to Kaduna.

sentence: Ban gan ta ba tun bikin ƙawata, ina jin ta koma ƙauye.
translation: I haven't seen her since my friend's wedding; I think she's gone back to the village.

sentence: Da muka gan su suna dariya, sai muka san komai ya daidaita.
translation: When we saw them laughing, we knew everything had turned out fine.

sentence: Kana da lokaci ka taimaka mini ɗaukar ruwa daga rijiya kafin magariba?
translation: Do you have time to help me carry water from the well before sunset?

sentence: Duk lokacin da na kira ka, kana aiki a shago har dare.
translation: Every time I ring you, you're working at the shop right into the night.

sentence: Kana da kirki ƙwarai, kuma kowa a unguwarmu yana girmama ka.
translation: You are exceptionally kind, and everyone in our neighbourhood respects you.

sentence: Baba bai dawo daga masallaci ba tukuna, mu jira shi kafin mu ci.
translation: Dad isn't back from the mosque yet; let's wait for him before we eat.

sentence: Ɗanʼuwana zai dawo Kano daga Legas bayan ya kammala kwantiragin aikinsa.
translation: My brother will come back to Kano from Lagos once he finishes his work contract.

sentence: Na yi kewar mahaifiyata; zan dawo gida kafin watan azumi ya ƙare.
translation: I miss my mother; I'll come home before the fasting month is over.

sentence: Kakata tana zaune a bakin ƙofa tana ba yara labari kowace maraice.
translation: My grandmother sits by the doorway telling the children stories every evening.

sentence: Ina kake zaune a Kano, ko har yanzu kana gidan kawunka?
translation: Whereabouts in Kano do you live, or are you still at your uncle's house?

sentence: Muna zaune a wannan unguwa shekara goma, kuma ba ma son ƙaura.
translation: We've been living in this neighbourhood for ten years, and we don't want to move.

sentence: An gyara ƙofar ɗakina jiya, amma har yanzu tana yin ƙara.
translation: The door of my room was repaired yesterday, but it still squeaks.

sentence: An gayyace mu zuwa taron malaman makaranta da ƙarfe takwas na safe.
translation: We were invited to the school teachers' meeting at eight in the morning.

sentence: An sace kuɗin asibitin gari, sai mutanen unguwa suka ji haushi ƙwarai.
translation: The town hospital's money was stolen, and the neighbourhood was furious.

sentence: Kishiyar mahaifiyata ta kawo mana tuwo, sai muka ci tare da murna.
translation: My mother's co-wife brought us tuwo, and we ate it together happily.

sentence: A gasar makarantu, mun sha kashi a hannun kishiyar makarantarmu ta Kano.
translation: In the schools' tournament, we were beaten by our school's rival from Kano.

sentence: Malam ya tunatar da mu cewa kishiyar haƙuri fushi ne, ba ƙarfi ba.
translation: The teacher reminded us that the opposite of patience is anger, not strength.

sentence: Aikin gida ya ishe ni yau, don haka na kwanta da wuri.
translation: The housework wore me out today, so I went to bed early.

sentence: Aikin ginin sabon asibiti ya tsaya tun watan jiya saboda rashin kuɗi.
translation: Work on the new hospital has been stopped since last month for lack of money.

sentence: Ina son aikin koyarwa duk da ƙarancin albashi, domin yana faranta mini rai.
translation: I love teaching in spite of the poor salary, because it makes me happy.

sentence: Jiya da dare ban yi barci lafiya ba, sauro ya dame ni sosai.
translation: Last night I didn't sleep well; the mosquitoes bothered me badly.

sentence: Ban isa taron a kan lokaci ba, domin motarmu ta lalace a hanya.
translation: I didn't get to the meeting on time, because our car broke down on the way.

sentence: Ban taɓa mantawa da ranar da mahaifina ya sayo mini keke ba.
translation: I have never forgotten the day my father bought me a bicycle.

sentence: Nawa ne kuɗin buhun shinkafa a kasuwar Sabon Gari yau?
translation: How much does a sack of rice cost at Sabon Gari market today?

sentence: Direban motar haya ya tambaye mu fasinjoji nawa suka rage kafin tashi.
translation: The taxi driver asked us how many passengers were still missing before we set off.

sentence: Littafin nan nawa ne, don haka ka mayar mini da shi yau.
translation: This book is mine, so give it back to me today.

sentence: Dare ya yi, sai muka zauna a farfajiya muna sauraron tatsuniyoyin kakarmu.
translation: Night fell, and we sat in the courtyard listening to our grandmother's folktales.

sentence: Likitan ya yi aiki dukan dare a asibiti, bai ma sami barci ba.
translation: The doctor worked all night at the hospital and didn't even get any sleep.

sentence: A cikin dare mai sanyi na hunturu, na ji kewar iyalina ƙwarai.
translation: On a cold harmattan night, I missed my family terribly.

sentence: In ruwan sama ya sauka yau, ba za mu je gonar gero ba.
translation: If it rains today, we won't go to the millet farm.

sentence: In ka isa kasuwa da wuri, za ka sami nama mai arha.
translation: If you get to the market early, you'll find cheap meat.

sentence: Bari in gaya maka gaskiya kafin ka sayar da gonar kakanka.
translation: Let me tell you the truth before you sell your grandfather's farm.

sentence: Muna buƙatar sabon famfo, domin wanda ke ɗakin wanka ya lalace.
translation: We need a new tap, because the one in the bathroom is broken.

sentence: Kamfanin yana buƙatar maʼaikata biyar masu iya sarrafa kwamfuta kafin ƙarshen wata.
translation: The company needs five staff who can use a computer before the end of the month.

sentence: Bayan rasuwar mahaifinsa, yaron yana buƙatar ƙauna fiye da kuɗin makaranta.
translation: After his father's death, the boy needs affection more than he needs school fees.

sentence: Kayan lambu yayi tsada a kasuwa, don haka na sayi ƙanana kawai.
translation: Vegetables have got expensive at the market, so I only bought small ones.

sentence: Lokaci yayi da za mu fara taro, amma shugaban bai zo ba tukuna.
translation: It's time for us to start the meeting, but the chairman still hasn't arrived.

sentence: Rigar da kika ɗinka mini yayi kyau ƙwarai, kowa ya yaba a bikin.
translation: The gown you sewed for me looked wonderful; everyone praised it at the wedding.

sentence: Ƙaramin ɗana yana tafiya tamkar tsoho, tun bayan da ya faɗi daga bishiya.
translation: My little son walks like an old man ever since he fell out of a tree.

sentence: Sabon malamin nan yana kula da mu tamkar ʼyaʼyansa na ainihi.
translation: This new teacher looks after us just as though we were his own children.

sentence: Ranar da muka rasa shi, gidan ya yi shiru tamkar kabari.
translation: The day we lost him, the house fell as silent as a grave.

sentence: Ruwan da ya rage a tulu kaɗan ne, don haka ban wanke faranti ba.
translation: There was only a little water left in the pot, so I didn't wash the plates.

sentence: Malam ya ba mu lokaci kaɗan kafin jarrabawa, har muka firgita.
translation: The teacher gave us very little time before the exam, so much that we panicked.

sentence: Ina jin sanyi kaɗan, amma ba zan sa hula a gaban abokaina ba.
translation: I'm a bit cold, but I'm not going to put on a cap in front of my friends.

sentence: Da muka isa bikin, abincin ya ƙare, sai shayi kawai ya rage.
translation: By the time we reached the wedding the food had run out; only tea was left.

sentence: Ban taɓa mantawa da abincin da muka ci a ranar Sallah ba.
translation: I have never forgotten the food we ate on the day of the Sallah feast.

sentence: Kayan da kuka saya a kasuwa sun cika ɗakin, babu inda za a wuce.

sentence: Me ya sa kuka bar taron kafin shugaba ya gama jawabinsa?
translation: Why did you all leave the meeting before the chairman finished his speech?

sentence: Labarin da kuka kawo mini jiya ya sa ban yi barci ba.

sentence: Yara sun yi murna sosai lokacin da mahaifinsu ya dawo daga tafiya.
translation: The children were overjoyed when their father came back from his journey.

sentence: Malamai sun yi murna ƙwarai bayan gwamnati ta ƙara musu albashi.

sentence: Tun da aka rufe makarantar, ban ga murna a fuskarta ba.

sentence: Waƙar da mahaifiyata takan rera da dare har yanzu tana kwantar mini da hankali.

sentence: Waƙar bikin ta yi ƙarfi sosai har ba mu ji juna ba.
translation: The wedding music was so loud that we couldn't hear each other.

sentence: Duk lokacin da na ji waƙar nan, sai in tuna da ƙauyenmu.
translation: Every single time I hear that song, I end up remembering our village.

sentence: Ɓarawo ya shiga gidanmu da dare ya saci kaji uku.

sentence: Mutanen unguwa sun kama ɓarawo a kasuwa, sai suka kai shi ofishin ʼyan sanda.

sentence: Ba na son a kira ni ɓarawo, ban taɓa satar kome ba.

sentence: Yaron ya yi ta bin kaza a farfajiya har ya kama ta da wahala.

sentence: ʼYan sanda sun kama direban da ya bugi babur a kan hanya.

sentence: Muryarka tana kama da ta kawuna, sai na yi mamaki a waya.

sentence: Ya kawo wa ʼyarsa kyauta daga Kano, sai ta yi ta rawa.

sentence: Mun sayi kyauta ga malaminmu wanda zai yi ritaya mako mai zuwa.

sentence: Ban buƙaci kyauta ba, zaman lafiya a gidan nan ya ishe ni.

sentence: Da hadari ya sauka, komai da ke kan igiyar wanki ya jiƙe.

sentence: Komai nisan ƙauyensu, zan kai musu gaisuwa kafin watan azumi ya ƙare.

sentence: Ya yi alkawari zai gaya mana komai, amma sai ya ɓoye gaskiya.

sentence: Kakana ya gaji, sai na zuba masa ruwan sanyi a ƙarƙashin bishiya.

sentence: Direban ya ɓata hanya, sai muka nuna masa titin da zai bi.

sentence: Har yanzu ban gafarta masa ba, ko da yake ya nemi afuwa sau uku.

sentence: Da safe ʼyan makaranta sukan taru a gaban shago suna sayen ƙosai.

sentence: Da muka isa shingen bincike, ʼyan sanda sun nemi takardun motarmu.
